However, there's an issue that taints my otherwise pleasant experience - an issue not unique to All Trails, but pervasive across various apps - the unnecessarily convoluted cancellation process for their subscription service. It's an aspect that feels akin to a roach motel strategy, easy to enter but hard to exit. This practice is not just frustrating, but also undercuts the trust between the app and its users.

In conclusion, while my love for All Trails and its services remain undiminished, I strongly feel that the ease of subscription cancellation should match the ease of subscription itself. Improvements in this area would not just benefit the user experience but also enhance the app's credibility and reputation. After all, a truly user-centric service considers all aspects of the user's journey, from start to end.
author: ofSaintss

title: Lifeline
content:
The subscription and lifeline service is useless if you don’t have a data connection. If there is no service at the trail head your connections have no way of knowing where you are. Pointless in many wilderness areas so do not subscribe for that purpose alone.

UPDATE: Thank you for your reply but this is what your ad says about Lifeline “ Lifeline is an AllTrails Pro feature that keeps your friends and loved ones informed while you are out on the trail. With Lifeline, you can select up to 5 safety contacts who will be able to track:
Your planned start and finish time + date
Your planned starting and ending location
Your total tracked distance and elevation gain
Your real-time location on a map plotted against your planned route
You can quickly send pre-formatted status updates to your safety contacts with just a tap while you are out on the trail. Most importantly, if you are overdue for your scheduled finish time, Lifeline will automatically send an alert to your safety contacts along with your last known coordinates.

Anyone with an email address or cell phone number can be a safety contact. Safety contacts do not need to download the AllTrails app or have an AllTrails account to view your real-time location.”

No where in this promo does it say anything about a data connection!  Deceiving. It’s no better than find my iPhone as a lifeline and certainly not a reason to subscribe as there are a great many hikes/trails that have no data service. Truth in advertising please.
author: Fordtunes

title: Fantastic! Except for a couple of things
content:
Let me start by saying I really love this app and use it weekly, even several times a week. The maps have helped me get back on track when my rambling exploring has been too rambly and it has helped me discover new awesome places to hike with my dog. In addition, it can be really helpful when I’m following something that is, for instance, a 6 mile hike but I don’t want to go that far, I can see shortcuts that will make it more the length I am after - though sometimes they are more adventurous than I expected!

On to the less good stuff: it can take a lot of poking around to figure out some of the functions and it can be hard to search by location. That is, it will let me search by proximity to my home location (I pay for the “pro” and consider it worth it) but when I’m looking for new places to explore in a particular area a little farther from my home I will search “parks to walk in near x” on google and then run those results by AllTrails to pick a new place.

The other weird thing is their Community function: you can ‘follow’ people but there is absolutely no way to communicate directly with them within the app, nor, once you follow each other can you even, say, comment on their hikes. So Community seems a bit of a misnomer since you can’t actually meet or even talk to the people you follow or are followed by unless you happen to meet on the trail accidentally. 

Having said that, I definitely like it and use it a LOT and was happy to pay for the pro version (downloadable maps, distance away function … other stuff?). I’m definitely hoping they refine it a bit more but even if they don’t I’ll keep using it.
author: Renniebrooke

title: Very useful!
content: Love this app for 3 main reasons- one it forces me to find new trails instead of just sticking to the same ones I know. Two, it makes finding new trails easy, especially with the filters. And third, it makes me feel safe because I can download the map before I go and when I’m on the trail with no reception, I can track exactly where I am and where I’m headed - it’s saved us quite a few times from getting lost on some of the trails! Couple of suggestions: 1) have a “daily report” that people can update in regards to conditions of that hike on that particular day/week (don’t always want to scour reviews for that) - we went on a hike that was incredibly overgrown over the summer and encountered a bees nest in the midst of it and really did not enjoy it. 2) be able to tick off trails we have done and have a “past trails” list or “history” list that isn’t tied to recordings or anything. Otherwise, great job! Thanks!
author: podcastnerd86

title: A couple of things
content:
Recently, the app keeps reverting my title to “morning” hike, “afternoon” hike, etc. I am Using All Trails to track my hikes for the 52 Hike Challenge. This is a new issue, and I am not sure why the change. Also I can’t find a way to edit the title back to what I want it to be. The title reverts just after I “save” the hike and the screen changes. If those 2 things could change, I’d give it 5 stars. I really like All Trails and all the other features. Overall, an excellent app!

Got an email from AllTrails. Swiftly too.  I appreciated that. I need to clarify, I guess. I know about three dots. But once the hike is “saved” and I close it, I can’t go back and edit the title. Or at least when I hit those three dots, the edit feature is no longer there once I leave the hike or the app. Also the reversion to the default title is new. Maybe the last week or so…before that, it wasn’t an issue. But hey, I’ll take all the help I can get cause this is a pain.
author: ugh2491

title: This app saved our life
content:
Thank you to the couple who stopped us on our hike in Anza-Borrego, CA. We parked and found our GPS wasn’t turning on, but decided to venture forward anyway. During our hike into the mountains, we ran into a couple. They were clearly shaken and upset, telling us that the trails were unmarked, extremely ambiguous, and they had gotten lost in the desert and ran out of water. They told us about this app and urged us to download it before we lost service. We did. 

These two people were the only people we saw the entire trip, and they most definitely saved our life. We got to our camp around 4pm and set out to do a 7 mile loop. In the day light the trail was next to impossible to follow, with many false paths going the wrong way. We eventually found a hill near the half way point to watch the sun set. After dark, the trail WAS impossible - That is, without this app. 

I was surprised to find that the app worked with the airplane and battery saver modes both on (after downloading the trail for offline use), and loaded fairly quickly each time we consulted it when we couldn’t decide if the trail was entering a pitch black sliver of a slot canyon or going above to circumvent it. Many times the beaten path veered off in the wrong direction, and we would find we were a half mile off course following the traces of people that clearly didn’t have this app. After a long hike in the dark with 3 extra miles on top of the 7 mile loop, we got to our camp safely ONLY because of this app. 

Thank you again to the couple we ran into, and thank you to the developers for creating this invaluable tool, it will live on our phones forever.
author: Cianrawr

title: Most recent update makes some features worse…
content: The most recent update made a few things worse. For one they took away the ability to comment on peoples activities which I find confusing. Wouldn’t you want people to spend more time on your app and therefore make the app more social? I would love the ability to DM users, but now I can’t even leave comments on peoples activities to ask questions about hiking conditions and whatnot. Second I’ve found that to access photos of a hike, you have to navigate a series of many menus that could be so much simpler. It’s clunky and not intuitive the way it is laid out now. Third I’ve found that it’s more difficult to access a scrolling menu of a hikes most recent activities. I have to click through two more menus than before to access them. This update seems like a honest attempt at improving the app but they made it more complicated then it needs to be. Other than that I found that the layout looks nicer, I would prefer to dig through less menus to access what I want though.
author: West norton

title: Worst update of all time. Please UNDO all of it!
content:
Ever since you updated the app, it’s a nightmare. Tells me I have done double the elevation gain I’ve done. Stops tracking me when I exit the app to check a text or my timer. Totally ruined my Grand Canyon hike by separating into 10 separate completed small hikes, instead of tracking my complete hike including offshoots off the main trail (which it used to do well). 

It’s terrible. I hate it. I’ve recommended it to hundreds of people and cannot anymore. PLEASE UNDO YOUR HORRIBLE UPDATES! And seriously how dare you try and force me to rate, name, add photos to and comment on every single walk I ever take. That’s insane. I hike some trails 4 times a week. Why would I do that? Then it freezes up when I try and exit the forced commenting and I have no choice. 

HORRIBLE. HORRIBLE. Upgrade. Writing this at a summit where I’ve once again lost my whole hike because the app stopped tracking when I got a text message. WTaF?
author: crzgrlprdctns

title: Was Great except latest update has ruined the "magic"
content: This is my older review which I forgot to send: I've used it over a year as a Pro, paying the subscription. It's gotten slower and slower in uptake onto my iPhone. Wicked slow. I had to delete and reinstall via iCloud and apparently a lot of my trail reports are gone. I was a real "pro" at it. Did save photo connections but those are already stored on my phone anyway. Sad to see my reports gone !!! Can not rely on this like other gps apps apparently. I like the social aspect of seeing other people's reviews of trails but the slow uptake of the app is very annoying. Probably lack of servers on their end. None of my other apps opened up as slow as this one! PS. Above was written awhile back. Latest updates removed my favorite feature of this app. The AllTrails map! It's still listed in "layers" but, no, it's just the inferior MapBox map affiliated with OpenStreetMaps but it is not "open source" either. MapBox recognizes only a few features that the former AllTrails map did. I don't see well known trails and parks and nature preserves that were in the original AllTrails map. I thought AllTrails maps were superior to Gaia's and Strava's which I also use occasionally. Instead, Lots of children's style map gimmicks are now added like the atrocious 3D modeling that doesn't look a bit like the real terrain out there. Much more detail is on Google maps now ... where in the past AllTrails which was aligned with the excellent National Geographic maps in the past was really good imo. Cost savings, profits and layoffs perhaps are the reason for the downgrades. Paid two year's subscriptions and I am probably in the top 1 percent of users with hundreds of activities a year ... now I feel betrayed and fooled that I could rely upon AllTrails. Bring back the old AllTrails as of two months ago. Can't believe I trusted something so ephemeral 😜
author: data2dave

title: Great iPhone app, bad Apple Watch app
content: The iPhone app and functionality this application gives is fantastic. I have gotten into hiking a lot in the past year and AllTrails has been my resource for discovering trails and also navigating them with the offline maps if I think I am getting lost. I have no real complains for the iPhone app but the same cannot be said for the watch app. It’s kind of garbage because of how unreliable it is. When it works it’s super buggy and reloads the entire UI very often, feeling super janky. The real problem is some days it doesn’t work period, getting stuck in the “connecting to the phone app” screen. At this point it’s a coin toss for me, half the time I can use my watch to see the trail map and my location and leave my phone in my backpack, awesome, and the other half the time the watch app won’t work and I have to pull out my phone anytime I wanna make sure I am not going off the trail path, kind of tedious.
author: Cesarbiods

title: Great app!
content: I love this app and I use it every weekend to find a trail based on the filters it provides (length, elevation gain, activity, etc.). I recommend it to everyone! The only things I’d change are that when I save a trail to my favorites, I could unsave it and save it again and it would be at the top of my list if I have it sorted as “most rencently saved.” Currently, it keeps your save list in the same order if you’ve previously saved a trail. This change makes it nice if you’re going on a trail that doesn’t have great reception and you want to open the trail map to check where you are without having to search for the trail name. I would also change the fact that if you’re in your favorites list and open a trail, when you go back you’re at the beginning of your list again. Other than those small changes, the app is amazing!
author: Kzgxz

title: Buyer Beware
content:
I bought this app a couple of days ago and tried to use it for a backpacking trip in a nearby national forest. Firstly, the app’s maps didn’t match the park’s trail maps AT ALL, so I decided to take both with me of course. As I went on, it seemed like the AllTrails version was just random gps points that had been made up. We were somewhat in the general area but absolutely could not have used it to find our way anywhere out there. 
I tried it again on another trail when we got back just to see and it wasn’t accurate either! Most of them have been, but if even some of them aren’t, then I cannot trust it. I planned to use this product for multi-day trips but it seems super unsafe now. 
The worst part is, when I went to request a refund for the above reasons, I got immediate denied (without anyone even looking into my claim) and it’s near impossible to get ahold of anyone at AllTrails. So, that’s $60 that I’ll never see again for a product that I’ll certainly never use. 
I do not recommend this product! The free version for simple day hikes was great. But if you want it for anything more in depth, this is not the right app for you!
author: emilypcut17

title: The latest version update made Alltrails useless
content:
This app is my most used hiking tools, I go to every trail with AllTrails on.  However the lasted update must have a huge glitch.  When you search nothing shows up no matter how you set the search.  It keeps saying no trails are found.  It is very disappointing the last update made recording so much more difficult to use (you have to first find a trail to link, then use the trail to navigate, then activity category / hiking, hold on to start then continue, in comparison to previous one click of round radio button to start.  Now this most recent update made AllTrails useless as you can’t find any single trail.  Very disappointed to see how a popular app goes on downward.  Don’t make updates for the sake of it, keep user experience in mind please.  

I am lowering my previous rating for I can’t use the app anymore
author: TripPlus

title: I adore this app with one exception
content:
I have done so much more hiking this summer now that I have this app. I absolutely love the ability to find and filter trails so easily and it works like a charm for me when on the trail. It’s gotten me out of a pinch a few times that trails have petered out and I’ve had a hard time finding my way. 

My one feature request is mostly to cover for my own stupidity:  At least 50% of the time I forget to press Finish when I’m done with the trail and then when I finally remember the app says my hike was not only the distance I walked but also the entire drive home. Either build into the app an ability to edit hike details OR automatically stop tracking distance/time when it’s clear the user is traveling at rapid speeds or has significantly left the area of the trail. 

Still: I’m a subscriber and will continue to be. SO worth it.
author: A from Mass

title: Love this App
content:
This App is awesome, I use it every time I hike, which is at least once a week. Well worth the price of the Pro version IMO. Still needs some work though. What I’d love to see, is some sort of intelligence built in, so it knows when you’re driving in a car versus walking. Sometimes after a long hike I’m exhausted, and forget to turn off the recorder. The app then records my ride home, and adds it to my hike. This has also screwed up my stats, and it makes a mess of the trail I’ve just recorded. 

I’d also love to see more levels of maps able to be saved offline. I’m out of cell service often when hiking in the mountains. Yes the map is saved to my phone, but at only one zoom level. If I try to zoom in to see more details about where I am, and I have no service, the map doesn’t redrawn. My cell phone has 200GB of available storage, id love to be able to fill it up with maps!
author: peterherrm

title: Big supporter, but app is getting less userfriendly
content:
I have used AllTrails since it first came out; so a longterm supporter here. With every update recently, it’s getting harder to use. 

Examples being: 
1. Using the map to find trails - you used to be able to just hover over an area & all the trail options with mini summaries would pop up at the bottom. Now you have to individually click on each trail on the map, which is SOOOOO time consuming. It was really nice to be able to quickly flit thru 20+ trails in one little area, then move the map around if none of those hit the spot. 
2. The pictures - omg this has gotten horrid. To have them separated by month/year, it calls for more clicking in and out of stuff (just like the map situation). Previously, I could easily see at the bottom corner when the pic was taken. And to have them all run together so i could just quickly & seamlessly scroll thru them & get an idea of the landscape was so much easier than what it is today. Whew. I never make it past a few pics now bc it is so complex just to see them! 

There are a few other small changes but those two really deter me from using the app as much as I once did. Just too much clicking and not as easy as it once was. Maybe there is a way to have optional settings for older layouts, so everyone is happy. Sometimes the good things don’t need “updating/fixing.” I really miss how easy this app was!
author: Shmaynard

title: Superb so far
content:
Downloaded this app before going off-grid in the Okanagan. Lots of hiking areas in BC and elsewhere are no where close to cell signals and this app (with downloaded maps) has been awesome with keeping us on track and giving confidence to venture around. Putting our phones on Airplane mode (mine is an iPhone 7S) saves serious battery so I feel confident I can go a full day with no issues. 
When mountain biking I still use this over TrailForks because it more clearly shows logging roads and other trails. I’ve had accuracy issues with TrailForks but none so far with AllTrails. Both are useful when mountain biking but as you’d guess: garbage in, garbage out. The maps are only as good as the person who uploaded it (and their GPS track). I’ve just found that AllTrails has been more accurate in that regard but again it’s not perfect either.
author: GF8000

title: Love this App; can’t live without it
content:
I’m an avid hiker, both locally and across different states, and I absolutely love this app. It’s incredibly reliable and well worth the annual subscription fee, which I find reasonably priced. It feels like it has every trail in the country—and it’s consistently accurate. It’s never let me down.

I especially appreciate the automatic metrics, like total distance, remaining distance, and estimated time. The visual features are fantastic too—the app highlights the trail as you go, so you always know where you are and how much farther you have to hike.

One of my favorite features is the ability to download maps for offline use. Reception is often spotty on the trails, and this app has been a real lifesaver. Compared to paper maps from parks, which can be confusing or poorly designed, this app eliminates the need to carry one altogether.
author: Orangetabbies

title: Amazing resource for hikers 🥾
content: I love this app. I use it daily to check for my “not completed” and “completed trails.” I love doing a new trail every time I go out for a walk or hike and it’s easy to search for things around you and just get out there! I wish I could put trails into a category like “don’t do for a variety of reasons” but I hacked that by “saving” the trail and adding it to a list named just that. All in all, I like All Trails and love that my family has access to my location when I’m out there, as long as I send them the link that I’m starting the trail. However, my family has told me that it is delayed, so I wish there was a way for my family to get the app too and see my location within the app. It’s instead a link to a browser/web page with my location on the trail. But I still love this app! Just wanted to give my feedback :)
author: Ejbruin2011

title: Great app+Frustrating experience+good service=happy user!
content:
Updated: I was contacted by the developer and was told to delete and download the app and it worked! Anyone experiencing the below issue, try this fix! I love all trails and I’m so happy I can continue to use it glitch free!

I used to LOVE AllTrails! It was the most effective way for me to map, track and find trails in my area and get good info on the trails. It’s even helped me (when I had service) in spots when I would get off trail. But recently (starting in September maybe?) the app freezes and crashes within 45 seconds to a minute of use. I can barely use it so unfortunately I’ve stopped using it, which is frustrating because like I said I love this app! I have updated the app as much as I can, and my phone (iPhone8) and nothing has seemed to fix this problem. Super disappointed that I have to find another app or another way to navigate trails!
author: kbrance5

title: Fully converted to be a fan, I love it.
content:
Update: This is a must have for all hikers. The limitations that I found are almost entirely addressed by getting the Pro version. However, most people who just want to find a nearby place to go walking or hiking will love the free version. The saved recorded tracks from other users are invaluable. I really like the planning and drawing features in pro. I especially like how people are able to collectively add to the trails, and how layers of pictures that are geotagged and waypoints answer many questions about what to expect. I also like the archiving features for saving your adventures and I was even able to make a custom list for trails that I would like to try. Everything intuitively flows, you can open a trail wherever you see it in the app. Great job, I also appreciate how responsive the developers are to suggestions and questions.

—————————————

In principle this app was exactly what I was looking for but it has a couple of things lacking which are kind of frustrating.

First it seems to be incomplete. One specific example is Raptor Ridge Viewpoint in Escondido. I know that it is a continuation of a trail but it sure doesn’t show up.

There are some trails that have no information on them, you just see the trail symbol, you can’t highlight it, so basically it is a map only.

Then the display is frustrating because you can basically only highlight one trail at a time, so you lose information of trails that connect to it, I understand there’s a reason for wanting to display a single trail if someone is only looking for one trail but when you’re just exploring an area you want to see all the available trails.
author: M Shaw

title: Good to find hikes, not great to navigate
content:
This app has been fantastic in helping me find new hikes and developing my new found love of hiking over the past year. The user reviews and photos are helpful, directions are generally good using google maps and very helpful to download the trail maps with gps of your location.  

The record function needs to be improved.  I generally use this to navigate new hikes, especially those with lots of offshoots.  Unfortunately when I lock my phone the app doesn’t notify when I’ve gone off the trail until I open it again.  I’ve tried using on my Apple Watch, but have had problems with the record function stopping my existing recording (and then am forced to rate the hike before I can restart) and expanding the map to something I can actually see on the watch.  This seems to have gotten worse with the recent update and generally means keeping your phone unlocked for the duration of the hike.
author: hiker9999

title: Invaluable Tool
content: Just “broke in” the AllTrails app on our first hike of 2020...and can immediately see, this is going to be an invaluable tool.  I’m genuinely regretting my delay in getting this, subscribing to the PRO, and allowing this app to fully enhance our hiking experiences.  No more!  On our first use...even beyond the amazing stats...we experienced the significance of the “off trail” warning provided by the app.  Based off of the use of the GPS system (cell signal NOT required)...we inadvertently missed a turn.  Not realizing it...”the beep” that I thought was a text message coming through from someone...?  It was the app signaling to me that we were off the trail.  Saved us who knows how much time and effort. So many reason to upgrade to PRO...but considering the significant hikes associated with our ADK 46’er journey we’ll be undertaking...I can’t imaging hiking without it.  Thank you All Trails!!!
author: UpstateNY Dad

title: Love it
content: I love using AllTrails however, sometimes the mileage is inaccurate. I also wish that they had an iPhone widget to start tracking a hike without having to go through the app. I tend to forget to start tracking a hike until after I’ve started. Having a widget on the Home Screen would make it so much easier to remember. I think my favorite feature is that you can build your own map (I think this is a paid for feature however). As a naturalist who has to plan hikes for groups, this feature helps me to plan routes that many people wouldn’t think to take because it’s not an already established route. It also gives an estimated mileage which is helpful, but you do have to be mindful that in order to have the most accurate mileage, one needs to add a lot of points along the route to account for any smaller curves that you can’t see unless you’re zoomed in.
author: gordysmiles

title: Navigator Issues Ruin Great App
content:
There’s some great stuff here and some things that urgently need improvement.

FREE FEATURES: As a database, AllTrails is fantastic. I love being able to sort, filter, and find just the right trail anywhere I go. I also love that the reviews often provide excellent up-to-date trail reports (like whether snow has melted or how bad the mud is, currently)

PRO FEATURES: I have subscribed to AllTrails Pro for the last three years and have loved being able to download offline maps and plot my own route using the web tool before I hit the mountains. Mountains where I live seldom have cell-coverage, so offline maps is a very handy tool.

However, lately the new “Navigator” has been frustratingly unreliable. My GPS location will sometimes freeze for over an hour (makes things frustrating when you are trying to decide which fork in a trail to take—or if your summit is this one or the next one). Additionally, recorded tracks will often lack accurate data regarding vertical climb and miles travelled. Sometimes it doesn’t even recognize that I finished the route. This is especially frustrating, too when I go to tag the DSLR photos from my adventure.

On a side note, the watch app is halfhearted, but could be really great (as anyone who has used WorkOutDoors can tell you). Activity data is weirdly duplicated if you share with Apple’s Activity app and maps don’t load on the watch (even if you have pro) and do not have a cellular connection.

Sadly, I won’t renew my Pro subscription. Keep working AllTrails and I’ll be back!
author: Mark the Hiker

title: Saved our lives
content: I might be a bit dramatic but my dog and I were lost in the woods.  We decided to do some new trails today and lost our way.  We spent 30 minutes trying to figure out how to get back to where we parked.  Luckily I had cell service so I opened Google Maps.  It showed my location but just the forest canopy which was no help at all.  We continued to walk in circles and I thought I was going to have to call emergency services because we were cold, wet, and lost.  The snow had turned to rain and we were getting soaked.  I downloaded All Trails and found our location.  I was able to determine which direction to go and the trails to find.  After crossing a river and climbing some steep inclines we finally made it back to the car.  Your app saved our lives or at least a call to emergency services to find us.  I should have downloaded it before we started but never imagined we would get lost.  Definitely worth every penny!
author: These nicknames are a joke

title: Great iPhone Terrible Watch
content:
I really don’t get it.  Yes it is nice I guess for casual hikers and short walks that the watch application can sort of be independent of the phone.  Sort of as you have to have a route on the phone and have the phone to transfer that route.  Not great even for this case. 

For serious backpackers the watch app used to be a great tool before the company sold out and the new application was written. I assure you the watch battery is only going to last at most a couple hours running this application. But the phone it will last hours and hours and can be plugged into a battery while still recording your track. If you would like to put that phone into your pack and monitor that active long running route from your watch. Well.  Hmm. You used to be able to do this but not with the current application. 

Don’t get me wrong I am not asking for the sort of stand alone features to be removed.  I am sure there are groups that love those features though really the built in Apple apps have you covered there.  But give me the ability to also monitor my active route on the phone from the watch.
author: Rokair

title: Free version is good wasn’t impressed with PRO at all
content: I would give the free version 5 stars but the paid version 2-3. The free version allows me to see the maps I need and the standard trail when I’m within service areas or no signal just fine. I’ve used the free version for over 10-15 long hikes outside of cellphone service areas. I purchased the pro access today before an attempted long hike and it made absolutely no difference when I was in the middle of trying to hike a trail at 11,000 ft altitude snowshoeing through snowed over trails with way over 5 feet of snow. My main objective was accessing the topography maps and weather overlays. I downloaded the maps before hitting the trail, but once I was I was on the trail I didn’t have access to them since there was no signal. I got the same features as I did with the free version so I was somewhat disappointed. The app also constantly resets so you have to bring up the map several times which isn’t ideal if you out hiking trying to make sure you stay on track, while also looking out for wildlife.
author: Jsmzm

title: Great app with an annoying conclusion
content: I used this app for the first time today on a 5 mile hike in the North GA mountains. We got lost up here last year due to some undocumented trails intersecting our trail and a lack of signage. This app took all the stress out of the hike and made it fun again. The frustrating conclusion was trying to share the recap. Saving to instagram can only post stories. There’s no option to save as a reel or a post, and the video gets cut off too short anyway. I really just wanted to save the video to my photos app on my iPhone, but there is no option for that! Why?!? The option to save to files quietly does nothing. There’s an option to save to a shared album. What shared album? I tried it, it never finishes and the only choice is to cancel. I tried sending the video via text message but it also gets cut off too short. I finally did a screen record, but I’m frustrated now. This could be a perfect app, but I feel like I’m trying to spring my recap video from prison or something. Please free my recap! Grrr!
author: jimgrill

title: Used to be great, now DANGEROUS
content: I’ve hiked over 600 miles this year alone using this app. I used to get to the trail, turn on the app, go into “Airplane Mode” to preserve battery life and then watch the curser move around the map as I explored trails and side trails for hours without issue. It WAS amazing and wholly reliable and above all else SAFE. I suggested the app to everyone I met on trail and off. I just updated the app, went out on the trail, but can no longer go into Airplane Mode, or all the black dotted line side trails vanish from the map. Why?!! Left with no safe alternative, I didn’t go into Airplane Mode to retain the side trails up on my map screen, which should have enabled me to explore other trails off of the AllTrails suggested hiking loop (the way I always do). BUT, with this new update, I lost internet connection and ALL of the black-dotted side trail lines INSTANTLY VANISHED from the map screen. I was literally in the middle of the woods with no trail map—no marked route back to the main trail, attempting to blindly navigate back. I ended up on a treacherously steep and narrow ledge trail with my leashed dog and no idea how to navigate out of our predicament. It was absolutely FRIGHTENING. Later, I bumped into someone with a paid membership heading in the opposite direction, who lost connection and for the first time (like me) could not tell which trail to take at a 4-way intersection to get out of the deep woods. Thank goodness it was a very well-blazed trail with posted maps, because it was getting late in the day and we both still had miles to go before finishing our hikes. This app was once a real safety tool, but could now easily result in a 911 SEARCH AND RESCUE emergency.
author: Mothmom12

title: Fatal Errors
content:
No matter what you think of it, don’t use it without a backup! I’ve been a paying user since 2019. The app was always very slow and buggy, but in the absence of an alternative I continued using it. There were all sorts of UX issues in an impressive variety, new ones rolled out with every new version. As of late it developed a couple of fatal issues. First, some of the recordings are vanishing showing an “activity” just of seconds instead of hours. Secondly, when you navigate to a trailhead using the “navigate” button, the coordinates are copied onto Google Maps with errors and Google Maps then sends you an hour away from an actual trailhead. This issue is particularly acute in the mountains. So yesterday, for example, I lost approximately 40 minutes on rerouting and then my hiking activity wasn’t recorded at all. Needless to say, you can’t add an activity later, at least in the phone app.

P.S. Since I first wrote this review the app has crashed more than once without showing a downloaded route. Luckily I was standing on the trail, otherwise it would be dangerous.
author: alexbogd

title: This app saved us!
content: One beautiful January day, my sister, our friend, and I decided to go hike the redwoods in Santa Cruz (Henry Cowell redwoods). We were out for a while, maybe 8 miles at this point and decided to turn around to head back to the car before it got dark. My dear sister thought it would be a good idea to use a paper map, which ended up getting us turned around multiple times. We literally were walking back and forth for an hour or so. All of our phones were about to die and the sun had set. Finally I decided to pull this app out because I knew I could see the trails and track us back to the car but also knew I had only 10% left and it wouldn’t last us the whole time. What I didn’t know was that I could use the GPS feature with my phone on airplane mode. With 5% battery and 10 miles of hiking behind us we finally returned to the car. It was so dark when we took a picture you could barley see our faces! Thank you All Trails, you are my favorite hiking app ever!!!
author: Auntie Jeja

title: Love the app hate the privacy policy
content:
I attempted to read through the privacy policy and find a way to not have my data sold to third parties. I am quite surprised that a hiking app has such a convoluted and lengthy legal policy for it. I am not a stupid person and have a college education, but I still find it difficult to consume and understand all of this legal jargon. All I want to know is, how do I keep my data from being sold when using this app. 

I use this app every day and sometimes multiple times per day. I love it and it’s the only way I’m able to find hiking in the areas I travel to. It works wonderful. I love seeing other peoples pictures and reading their reviews. I love the option of my own review and suggestions as well as posting pictures. I do not want to give up this app, but I also really resist the idea of having my information in one more location available to hackers. Data breaches happen all of the time.

I am asking for the ability to select what information gets used by this app.
author: Cindysheph

title: Developers undermined decent app
content:
In some sort of misguided attempt to compete with Instagram (why?) they have “updated” the app to push other people’s pictures in a bad insta simulacra— and for unknown reasons have removed all of the usefulness of the stats. Instead of stats you just get undifferentiated blobs. Who makes an app *less* useful? Less informative? Currently looking for an app with functionality that doesn’t want to be a knock off bobo fake Instagram. 

Updated in response to developer: I have repeatedly reached out to support and they have been pointedly unhelpful. They keep pointing me to where I can find the feature that you broke in your relaunch and then telling me I “can get what I’m looking for” if I click through fourteen other pages. First, no amount of clicking will get anyone what they used to have when the stats were an interactive graph. And they aggressively miss the point that YOU USED TO HAVE A SINGLE INTERACTIVE GRAPH. No one thinks that dispersing the information, making people click through page after page, scrolling up and down endless lists and then having to make my own out of app graph of the data is useful. Again, who looks at a feature that was user friendly, helpful, easy to grasp and quick to use and says, who wants usability? Let’s remove all the utility from it and make people click through seventeen pages to a quarter of what they used to in one place. I have pushed through long periods when AllTrails was super buggy, when it would crash halfway through every hike, when taking a picture would make it shut down, because it had features that were (when they worked) useful. Your relaunch is a disaster. No one wants a low rent knock off Instagram for hikers— I can just search hiking hashtags in Instagram. People just want usability and information.
author: Phnomda

title: Useful and Accurate
content: This is a great little app.  I’m pretty new to hiking, but this app has encouraged me to try different trails that I’d previously steer clear of for sheer lack of knowledge and fear of getting lost.  In this sense, it is a game-changer for me.  Haven’t used the social platform because it seems a little lacking.  So the connectivity is challenging.  For instance, it would be nice if people could respond to reviews, but the only way to do that is to write a review yourself.  Would be nice to be able to comment on pics too.  I realize it’s primarily for tracking and mapping—and in this sense I couldn’t ask for anything more.  But the tinkering it does with social connection makes me feel like it could be much more than it is—or why even hint at it and make it difficult to connect?  I guess what I would like to see is a kind of Waze system where you can see where other hikers are live and what the encounter.  Could be helpful if someone gets hurt or lost if the connectivity was more advanced.
author: Jdcop1974

title: Get app with eye to future
content:
I have used this app for a couple of years now with the pro version.   In the beginning it might have had issues but I think they are tied to performance issues of the phone and the network and satellite hardware.   I have been to many trails and it has worked great.   This new lifeline feature is going to be great especially for my wife since I usually hike alone.  It has helped me get back on the trail in areas where the trail is poorly marked or no real markings at all like out in West Texas. 

I took a turn off a trail ( not on purpose) thinking that was the trail.  It was the most dangerous turn possible.  I finally sat down and pulled out my phone and looked at my all trails plot.  I was way off but too dangerous to back track.  So I plotted a way across the steep mountain side to reconnect to the actual trail.   

    On thing that would be nice is if would tell me when I have diverged from the trail with a voice warning kinda like google maps or tell me I’m at an intersection and take the left turn again via a voice notification.
author: Chasgard

title: Life changing
content: This app has truly changed my life. I’ve always loved to hike and have relied on my eagle eye ability to spot a trail head. I knew I was missing trails everywhere, and this app was the beacon I needed to find them. I have never had so much fun in my life, going on beautiful adventures with my dog on my days off instead of chillin at home or spending money on random things I don’t need. The app provides all the clarity you need about the trails, too. Whether they are dog friendly trails, the ease of parking, incline levels, length of the trail, and what kinds of sights to expect to see. While I always loved to hike, some of those unknowns would sometimes make me hesitant to embark on a trail. AllTrails answers those questions for you, allowing you to know what to expect so you can hike with peace of mind. I truly love this app and have been telling all my friends about it. I hope you download it and start having all the fun I’ve been having !!
author: papichulocervantesjr

title: Love the Information, but….
content:
I have used AllTrails a lot over the years. MN North Shore Hiking, South Cali hiking, Hawaii hiking, etc. However, just a couple of days ago, I started looking at my profile and noticed that EVERYTHING was public. All of my lists, my activities, which maps I downloaded, just to name a few. So I figured I would go into settings and change all of that, but that only changes the setting on FUTURE additions. So I had to go back and individually change everything to only show to my connections. Oh, and I also had to then make sure that I approved all my connections. The first test of someone requesting a follow was not good either. No notifications when you are in the app or a simple place to go. I had to dig deep. This would almost be a deal breaker for me (Pro user for years), but I decided to just put as little information in it as possible. Including reviewing and tracking trails. What a bummer.

Response to developer:

Just checked and the option is not there on my phone.
author: BossHoss_16

title: App update ruined a formerly great app
content:
I’ve been a All Trails premium subscriber for years. All previous versions were excellent.  I used the browser version on my home computer to research hiking trips and print maps and the phone app version to make sure that I stay on course. This is particular helpful when trails or intersections are poorly marked. It was also helpful when you just wanted to know how close you are. All trails also has a feature allowing you to record your route. I have zero interest in this feature. I prefer not to drain my phone battery and I’m already recording on my GPS watch. Well with the new update, you are basically forced to record. The start button takes up 40% of the screen and can’t be removed. You can’t see much of the map until you start navigation. Additionally, it’s so sensitive that you will probably turn it on accidentally. 

I doubt that anyone from All Trails reads these reviews, but if you do, be aware that making navigation an mandatory feature is RUINED the app. Please restore the earlier version or add a setting that allows the “classic” view
author: MSK425

title: Constant Manipulation
content: The AllTrails app has become littered with manipulation and tricks to get you to pay for premium. For example, when you click on "Get Directions", it shows a popup asking if you want to see a "tour". Sounds somewhat close to directions, and it feels like that's what you're supposed to click. But it turns out it's a premium feature. So you get navigated to this screen where they show you some photos and then put a full screen popup saying upgrade to view. But where are my directions? Oh, for that, you need to close out all of these distractions they just popped up and click the "Get directions" button again, and then decline their tour question. There are lots of these types of tactics throughout the app. It's totally understandable to have premium features, but don't waste our time trying to shove them down our throats. Mark clearly which features are reserved for premium, put a lock indicator or something like that so we know which functionality is not available, and keep the free functionality actually usable. For now, I'm just really disappointed that they've basically turned this app into junkware.
author: gman995

title: Love this app for hiking! Here are some recommendations to improve the app
content:
First off, need to say i love this app and use it as a hiking bible!! Some recommendations I have for the developers:

Under reviews, show a user’s reputation score next to their name. It would be helpful to know if the person saying this trail is “soooo hard” is a complete noob to hiking or someone whose been on hundreds of trails, just for a frame of reference. Why have the reputation score if it isn’t displayed next to the usernames in the comments and reviews?

Also, while reading about the app it mentions you can upload edits to trails and routes. I can’t figure out how to do this on the app? There are many trails that the All Trails trail takes u into an unsafe area, and I would like to edit that for future users. I’ve noticed the desktop has some features the mobile app doesn’t.... such as making “lists” and creating new trails. 

Next, in addition to easy medium and hard.... add a safety ranking! Here on Oahu there are easy hikes that are super treacherous and then super hard hikes that are on huge pieces of land with nowhere to fall or get lost. For somewhere like Hawai’i this feature is very necessary. 

Finally, think there should be a DM (direct message) feature to make the app a bit more social! Or at least link to Instagram. 

I was sad that Sacred Falls was removed from the app. While it is an illegal hike, those choosing to do it could need it as a lifeline.... better safe than sorry
author: chay55537736788

title: So close to perfect!
content:
Considering I only have one negative thing to say about the app as a whole I will put that up front.  I wish I could reverse a loop trail!!!  

Other than that I have been using this app happily for about a year.  It has absolutely saved me from unplanned miles on poorly marked trail junctions.  It has helped me introduce people to hiking and backpacking.  I use it any time I am in a new place and can always find a trail, or a drive worth taking.

I use this app on every bike I take, weather that is an hour or a multi-day backpacking trip.    

It has REPLACED my need for a dedicated GPS device.   I don’t recommend it but honestly I don’t carry maps or books either, this has simply replaced them and that means saving weight (I mean always carry your map...lol)

I am a pro (paid) member and so long as the app continues to update and add new content I will continue to pay to use it.  

I don’t really understand people complaining about it not working without cellular coverage!  If you are going somewhere without cellular coverage you should be a pro member if for nothing else your own safety!!!!  You should have a downloaded map!   On top of that your phone can last for days on airplane mode with active GPS.  Compare the fee to any GPS device, map books, etc. and you will see you can pay to use this for years before approaching those prices.  

Thanks AllTrails!  For the saved miles and countless hours planning my next trip!
author: sir nok

title: Long Time User Pro Account
content: A few times the app doesn’t load. I’m currently trying to load it on my upgraded home WiFi and gray screen. It’s been happening more often lately. I check my WiFi speed and opened google, CNN, watched videos lightening fast so it is not my WiFi. It’s happening more and more recently and it’s frustrating. Especially for a paid app. Something changed. And I’m reading others posted similar. I was raving about your app and that will cease as this issue you’re having is continuing to worsen. And contact your support team... as recommended in prior review. Is unacceptable. It’s your issue your developer and taking subscriptions you figure it out and you waste your time not mine. I downloaded Mt Maggie / lakes maps in Springville Ca and plan to start in 6 hours. Now all is useless just a blank grayed out screen. Fix your issues please so I can once again enjoy it. Fellow hikers dumped your app because of issues I’m holding out hope. Thank You
author: Breathtakingphotos BTP

title: Best choice for the casual hiker
content:
All Trails is my go to app for hiking locally. I really like the search (browse) feature and the fact that I can filter by distance from me, length, and difficulty. Couple that with the ability to locate features and I can look for “all trails within 25 miles that are between 2 and 5 miles long with waterfalls” makes it a great day planner.

Then I can get directions to the trail head. Once there I can record my hike. This is where the fifth star is lost! When you see the prompt to “start recording” you’re taken to the map screen. You might to think you are recording but unless you scroll the screen up to reveal the hidden Start button - yeh, that’s right, they hide the critical step off screen!

Also there is no iPad app. If you think, like I do, that the extra screen area could improve your searching and reviewing; too bad because all you get is the double size iPhone view. Archaic? You bet!

I subscribe to the app for the ability to download the maps for offline navigation. When I was evaluating All Trails on several occasions I found myself looking at a white screen with a blue dot indicating my position. Not cool, but with WiFi or cellular that’s to be expected.

Other niceties like off-trail alerts and the ability to share your location with someone lat home” could literally be life savers.

In my opinion Gaia is better for back country hikes and route planning such hikes, but All Trails is best for searching for established trails and enjoying a day or two on the trail.
author: iWanit

title: AWESOME APP but Needs One Addition
content:
I love this app!  I ride an Adventure Bike (GS 1200) and the reviews are great to research various trails to determine if I’m able to do them or how much effort the trail will require. The GS 1200 is a BIG motorcycle and I like knowing if there are “Rock Gardens”, massive ruts, steep declines, etc.  Other users often give distances to significant trail challenges which comes in handy!!!  Of course, remember that trail conditions change constantly so don’t ride wild based on reviews...

The one addition that is needed (in my opinion) is an additional FILTER Category of “Adventure Riding” or “Off Road Motorcycling”.  It’s easy enough to use “Off Road Driving” to identify trails that are open to Off Road Riding but the numerous trail user write ups is mostly from rock crawlers or 4x4’ers.  I often read these when I’m out and about riding the trails and it would make reviewing up and coming trails much quicker. 

I upgraded to the Pro version last year and it is the best money I have spent on an app!
author: Todd_M_Peterson

title: AllTrails and AI
content: I (mostly) love AllTrails! I am an avid backpacker and hiker in Colorado and use it literally every weekend in the summary and many weekdays in between. It is invaluable for routefinding on trail, finding good trails while at home, and learning about trail conditions. I honestly don’t think I could do many of the adventures I love without it. Which is why it’s so frustrating to leave a 4 star review—largely because AllTrails has started using AI throughout their app. The AI trail review summaries are often bad, and moreover, undercut one of the great things about the app: the trail community. I don’t want to talk to a computer and I don’t particularly care for a computers thoughts on trails. Instead, I want to read the often-entertaining trail reviews of my fellow outdoor enthusiasts. I honestly don’t understand why they exist beyond providing the App an “in” to the tech thing of the moment (see how well that went for everyone who bought into NFTs two years ago). I hope AllTrails gets rid of AI in the next few updates.
author: Trevoreggg

title: Apple Watch Maps Removed - App Downgrade
content:
I am beyond frustrated with this app / company.  I spent over an hour today before our hike trying to figure out why the ultra useful trail maps were not loading on my Apple Watch Ultra 2.  I was already out on the trail with very poor signal when I finally found the statement the maps have been removed and replaced with the far, far, less useful compass ring.  Big thank you for the waste of my time, frustration and bickering that ensued as I attempted to diagnose.  Anyone who actually hikes and uses the moving maps knows how invaluable they were.  This is perhaps one of the biggest boneheaded feature removals in app, and not an inexpensive app, that I have ever seen.

In addition, when hiking the find closest trail when changing your mind on where to go is basically useless.  How hard is it show trails close by based on your GPS position?  Doesn’t work.  Fail.

Other than all this the app is great for keeping you on the trail and not lost.  App was great- being back the Watch moving maps and I will be singing your praises again.

content: I used all trails for hiking and mountain biking quite a bit. I live in a very rural area where we build new trails all the time. author: Oli McClure

title: Great app for big trips and everyday use! A usability request.
content:
I am a fan of Alltrails app for several years ago. It works wonderfully during my hikes/walks around town and was super helpful  guiding me and my friends on the trails during a Tour de Mont Blanc trip three years ago.

I found one usability issue in the latest version (13.0.2). I use it mostly on daily walks, and it used to feature the tracking function with a big “record” button at the bottom of the display. Then I figured out that I now have to press 4 clicks to start recording. For a function that (I suspect) many users use frequently this is a terrible UI design. I hope the developers will update the interface to bring back the big start/record button.

Thanks!
author: CleanUI

title: Concerns About GPS and Route Recording
content: I saw another comment on here complaining about All Trails and his GPS signal being lost, as well as his routes not being recorded.   This has nothing to do with the All Trails app, and there’s nothing AllTrails can do to fix this issue.  It has to do with the strength of the GPS receiver in your phone.  If the GPS signal is lost because of cloud cover or whatever, AllTrails will stop recording your route because it cannot locate you while your GPS receiver is unable to connect with the GPS in orbit around Earth.  Sometimes it doesn’t matter how good your GPS receiver is, and the signal connection will still be lost.  If your phone is constantly losing GPS connection, either your phone’s receiver is low quality, the weather is impeding the connection, or you’re simply in a location where a GPS receiver is going to constantly drop connection no matter how good your receiver is.  I hope this helps.
author: rhnotte

title: A Love-Hate Relationship with All Trails
content:
In the realm of outdoor exploration, All Trails stands out as a beacon of convenience and functionality. It is an app that has become an indispensable part of my adventures, helping me navigate the hidden troves of nature's beauty with its comprehensive collection of trails and routes.

However, there's an issue that taints my otherwise pleasant experience - an issue not unique to All Trails, but pervasive across various apps - the unnecessarily convoluted cancellation process for their subscription service. It's an aspect that feels akin to a roach motel strategy, easy to enter but hard to exit. This practice is not just frustrating, but also undercuts the trust between the app and its users.

In conclusion, while my love for All Trails and its services remain undiminished, I strongly feel that the ease of subscription cancellation should match the ease of subscription itself. Improvements in this area would not just benefit the user experience but also enhance the app's credibility and reputation. After all, a truly user-centric service considers all aspects of the user's journey, from start to end.
author: ofSaintss

title: Lifeline
content:
The subscription and lifeline service is useless if you don’t have a data connection. If there is no service at the trail head your connections have no way of knowing where you are. Pointless in many wilderness areas so do not subscribe for that purpose alone.

UPDATE: Thank you for your reply but this is what your ad says about Lifeline “ Lifeline is an AllTrails Pro feature that keeps your friends and loved ones informed while you are out on the trail. With Lifeline, you can select up to 5 safety contacts who will be able to track:
Your planned start and finish time + date
Your planned starting and ending location
Your total tracked distance and elevation gain
Your real-time location on a map plotted against your planned route
You can quickly send pre-formatted status updates to your safety contacts with just a tap while you are out on the trail. Most importantly, if you are overdue for your scheduled finish time, Lifeline will automatically send an alert to your safety contacts along with your last known coordinates.

Anyone with an email address or cell phone number can be a safety contact. Safety contacts do not need to download the AllTrails app or have an AllTrails account to view your real-time location.”

No where in this promo does it say anything about a data connection!  Deceiving. It’s no better than find my iPhone as a lifeline and certainly not a reason to subscribe as there are a great many hikes/trails that have no data service. Truth in advertising please.
author: Fordtunes

title: Fantastic! Except for a couple of things
content:
Let me start by saying I really love this app and use it weekly, even several times a week. The maps have helped me get back on track when my rambling exploring has been too rambly and it has helped me discover new awesome places to hike with my dog. In addition, it can be really helpful when I’m following something that is, for instance, a 6 mile hike but I don’t want to go that far, I can see shortcuts that will make it more the length I am after - though sometimes they are more adventurous than I expected!

On to the less good stuff: it can take a lot of poking around to figure out some of the functions and it can be hard to search by location. That is, it will let me search by proximity to my home location (I pay for the “pro” and consider it worth it) but when I’m looking for new places to explore in a particular area a little farther from my home I will search “parks to walk in near x” on google and then run those results by AllTrails to pick a new place.

The other weird thing is their Community function: you can ‘follow’ people but there is absolutely no way to communicate directly with them within the app, nor, once you follow each other can you even, say, comment on their hikes. So Community seems a bit of a misnomer since you can’t actually meet or even talk to the people you follow or are followed by unless you happen to meet on the trail accidentally. 

Having said that, I definitely like it and use it a LOT and was happy to pay for the pro version (downloadable maps, distance away function … other stuff?). I’m definitely hoping they refine it a bit more but even if they don’t I’ll keep using it.
author: Renniebrooke

title: Very useful!
content: Love this app for 3 main reasons- one it forces me to find new trails instead of just sticking to the same ones I know. Two, it makes finding new trails easy, especially with the filters. And third, it makes me feel safe because I can download the map before I go and when I’m on the trail with no reception, I can track exactly where I am and where I’m headed - it’s saved us quite a few times from getting lost on some of the trails! Couple of suggestions: 1) have a “daily report” that people can update in regards to conditions of that hike on that particular day/week (don’t always want to scour reviews for that) - we went on a hike that was incredibly overgrown over the summer and encountered a bees nest in the midst of it and really did not enjoy it. 2) be able to tick off trails we have done and have a “past trails” list or “history” list that isn’t tied to recordings or anything. Otherwise, great job! Thanks!
author: podcastnerd86

title: A couple of things
content:
Recently, the app keeps reverting my title to “morning” hike, “afternoon” hike, etc. I am Using All Trails to track my hikes for the 52 Hike Challenge. This is a new issue, and I am not sure why the change. Also I can’t find a way to edit the title back to what I want it to be. The title reverts just after I “save” the hike and the screen changes. If those 2 things could change, I’d give it 5 stars. I really like All Trails and all the other features. Overall, an excellent app!

Got an email from AllTrails. Swiftly too.  I appreciated that. I need to clarify, I guess. I know about three dots. But once the hike is “saved” and I close it, I can’t go back and edit the title. Or at least when I hit those three dots, the edit feature is no longer there once I leave the hike or the app. Also the reversion to the default title is new. Maybe the last week or so…before that, it wasn’t an issue. But hey, I’ll take all the help I can get cause this is a pain.
author: ugh2491

title: This app saved our life
content:
Thank you to the couple who stopped us on our hike in Anza-Borrego, CA. We parked and found our GPS wasn’t turning on, but decided to venture forward anyway. During our hike into the mountains, we ran into a couple. They were clearly shaken and upset, telling us that the trails were unmarked, extremely ambiguous, and they had gotten lost in the desert and ran out of water. They told us about this app and urged us to download it before we lost service. We did. 

These two people were the only people we saw the entire trip, and they most definitely saved our life. We got to our camp around 4pm and set out to do a 7 mile loop. In the day light the trail was next to impossible to follow, with many false paths going the wrong way. We eventually found a hill near the half way point to watch the sun set. After dark, the trail WAS impossible - That is, without this app. 

I was surprised to find that the app worked with the airplane and battery saver modes both on (after downloading the trail for offline use), and loaded fairly quickly each time we consulted it when we couldn’t decide if the trail was entering a pitch black sliver of a slot canyon or going above to circumvent it. Many times the beaten path veered off in the wrong direction, and we would find we were a half mile off course following the traces of people that clearly didn’t have this app. After a long hike in the dark with 3 extra miles on top of the 7 mile loop, we got to our camp safely ONLY because of this app. 

Thank you again to the couple we ran into, and thank you to the developers for creating this invaluable tool, it will live on our phones forever.
author: Cianrawr

title: Most recent update makes some features worse…
content: The most recent update made a few things worse. For one they took away the ability to comment on peoples activities which I find confusing. Wouldn’t you want people to spend more time on your app and therefore make the app more social? I would love the ability to DM users, but now I can’t even leave comments on peoples activities to ask questions about hiking conditions and whatnot. Second I’ve found that to access photos of a hike, you have to navigate a series of many menus that could be so much simpler. It’s clunky and not intuitive the way it is laid out now. Third I’ve found that it’s more difficult to access a scrolling menu of a hikes most recent activities. I have to click through two more menus than before to access them. This update seems like a honest attempt at improving the app but they made it more complicated then it needs to be. Other than that I found that the layout looks nicer, I would prefer to dig through less menus to access what I want though.

author: crzgrlprdctns

title: Was Great except latest update has ruined the "magic"
content: This is my older review which I forgot to send: I've used it over a year as a Pro, paying the subscription. It's gotten slower and slower in uptake onto my iPhone. Wicked slow. I had to delete and reinstall via iCloud and apparently a lot of my trail reports are gone. I was a real "pro" at it. Did save photo connections but those are already stored on my phone anyway. Sad to see my reports gone !!! Can not rely on this like other gps apps apparently. I like the social aspect of seeing other people's reviews of trails but the slow uptake of the app is very annoying. Probably lack of servers on their end. None of my other apps opened up as slow as this one! PS. Above was written awhile back. Latest updates removed my favorite feature of this app. The AllTrails map! It's still listed in "layers" but, no, it's just the inferior MapBox map affiliated with OpenStreetMaps but it is not "open source" either. MapBox recognizes only a few features that the former AllTrails map did. I don't see well known trails and parks and nature preserves that were in the original AllTrails map. I thought AllTrails maps were superior to Gaia's and Strava's which I also use occasionally. Instead, Lots of children's style map gimmicks are now added like the atrocious 3D modeling that doesn't look a bit like the real terrain out there. Much more detail is on Google maps now ... where in the past AllTrails which was aligned with the excellent National Geographic maps in the past was really good imo. Cost savings, profits and layoffs perhaps are the reason for the downgrades. Paid two year's subscriptions and I am probably in the top 1 percent of users with hundreds of activities a year ... now I feel betrayed and fooled that I could rely upon AllTrails. Bring back the old AllTrails as of two months ago. Can't believe I trusted something so ephemeral 😜
author: data2dave

title: Great iPhone app, bad Apple Watch app
content: The iPhone app and functionality this application gives is fantastic. I have gotten into hiking a lot in the past year and AllTrails has been my resource for discovering trails and also navigating them with the offline maps if I think I am getting lost. I have no real complains for the iPhone app but the same cannot be said for the watch app. It’s kind of garbage because of how unreliable it is. When it works it’s super buggy and reloads the entire UI very often, feeling super janky. The real problem is some days it doesn’t work period, getting stuck in the “connecting to the phone app” screen. At this point it’s a coin toss for me, half the time I can use my watch to see the trail map and my location and leave my phone in my backpack, awesome, and the other half the time the watch app won’t work and I have to pull out my phone anytime I wanna make sure I am not going off the trail path, kind of tedious.
author: Cesarbiods

title: Great app!
content: I love this app and I use it every weekend to find a trail based on the filters it provides (length, elevation gain, activity, etc.). I recommend it to everyone! The only things I’d change are that when I save a trail to my favorites, I could unsave it and save it again and it would be at the top of my list if I have it sorted as “most rencently saved.” Currently, it keeps your save list in the same order if you’ve previously saved a trail. This change makes it nice if you’re going on a trail that doesn’t have great reception and you want to open the trail map to check where you are without having to search for the trail name. I would also change the fact that if you’re in your favorites list and open a trail, when you go back you’re at the beginning of your list again. Other than those small changes, the app is amazing!
author: Kzgxz

title: Buyer Beware
content:
I bought this app a couple of days ago and tried to use it for a backpacking trip in a nearby national forest. Firstly, the app’s maps didn’t match the park’s trail maps AT ALL, so I decided to take both with me of course. As I went on, it seemed like the AllTrails version was just random gps points that had been made up. We were somewhat in the general area but absolutely could not have used it to find our way anywhere out there. 
I tried it again on another trail when we got back just to see and it wasn’t accurate either! Most of them have been, but if even some of them aren’t, then I cannot trust it. I planned to use this product for multi-day trips but it seems super unsafe now. 
The worst part is, when I went to request a refund for the above reasons, I got immediate denied (without anyone even looking into my claim) and it’s near impossible to get ahold of anyone at AllTrails. So, that’s $60 that I’ll never see again for a product that I’ll certainly never use. 
I do not recommend this product! The free version for simple day hikes was great. But if you want it for anything more in depth, this is not the right app for you!
author: emilypcut17

title: The latest version update made Alltrails useless
content:
This app is my most used hiking tools, I go to every trail with AllTrails on.  However the lasted update must have a huge glitch.  When you search nothing shows up no matter how you set the search.  It keeps saying no trails are found.  It is very disappointing the last update made recording so much more difficult to use (you have to first find a trail to link, then use the trail to navigate, then activity category / hiking, hold on to start then continue, in comparison to previous one click of round radio button to start.  Now this most recent update made AllTrails useless as you can’t find any single trail.  Very disappointed to see how a popular app goes on downward.  Don’t make updates for the sake of it, keep user experience in mind please.  

I am lowering my previous rating for I can’t use the app anymore
author: TripPlus

title: I adore this app with one exception
content:
I have done so much more hiking this summer now that I have this app. I absolutely love the ability to find and filter trails so easily and it works like a charm for me when on the trail. It’s gotten me out of a pinch a few times that trails have petered out and I’ve had a hard time finding my way. 

My one feature request is mostly to cover for my own stupidity:  At least 50% of the time I forget to press Finish when I’m done with the trail and then when I finally remember the app says my hike was not only the distance I walked but also the entire drive home. Either build into the app an ability to edit hike details OR automatically stop tracking distance/time when it’s clear the user is traveling at rapid speeds or has significantly left the area of the trail. 

Still: I’m a subscriber and will continue to be. SO worth it.
author: A from Mass

title: Love this App
content:
This App is awesome, I use it every time I hike, which is at least once a week. Well worth the price of the Pro version IMO. Still needs some work though. What I’d love to see, is some sort of intelligence built in, so it knows when you’re driving in a car versus walking. Sometimes after a long hike I’m exhausted, and forget to turn off the recorder. The app then records my ride home, and adds it to my hike. This has also screwed up my stats, and it makes a mess of the trail I’ve just recorded. 

I’d also love to see more levels of maps able to be saved offline. I’m out of cell service often when hiking in the mountains. Yes the map is saved to my phone, but at only one zoom level. If I try to zoom in to see more details about where I am, and I have no service, the map doesn’t redrawn. My cell phone has 200GB of available storage, id love to be able to fill it up with maps!
author: peterherrm

title: Big supporter, but app is getting less userfriendly
content:
I have used AllTrails since it first came out; so a longterm supporter here. With every update recently, it’s getting harder to use. 

Examples being: 
1. Using the map to find trails - you used to be able to just hover over an area & all the trail options with mini summaries would pop up at the bottom. Now you have to individually click on each trail on the map, which is SOOOOO time consuming. It was really nice to be able to quickly flit thru 20+ trails in one little area, then move the map around if none of those hit the spot. 
2. The pictures - omg this has gotten horrid. To have them separated by month/year, it calls for more clicking in and out of stuff (just like the map situation). Previously, I could easily see at the bottom corner when the pic was taken. And to have them all run together so i could just quickly & seamlessly scroll thru them & get an idea of the landscape was so much easier than what it is today. Whew. I never make it past a few pics now bc it is so complex just to see them! 

There are a few other small changes but those two really deter me from using the app as much as I once did. Just too much clicking and not as easy as it once was. Maybe there is a way to have optional settings for older layouts, so everyone is happy. Sometimes the good things don’t need “updating/fixing.” I really miss how easy this app was!
author: Shmaynard

title: Superb so far
content:
Downloaded this app before going off-grid in the Okanagan. Lots of hiking areas in BC and elsewhere are no where close to cell signals and this app (with downloaded maps) has been awesome with keeping us on track and giving confidence to venture around. Putting our phones on Airplane mode (mine is an iPhone 7S) saves serious battery so I feel confident I can go a full day with no issues. 
When mountain biking I still use this over TrailForks because it more clearly shows logging roads and other trails. I’ve had accuracy issues with TrailForks but none so far with AllTrails. Both are useful when mountain biking but as you’d guess: garbage in, garbage out. The maps are only as good as the person who uploaded it (and their GPS track). I’ve just found that AllTrails has been more accurate in that regard but again it’s not perfect either.
author: GF8000

title: Love this App; can’t live without it
content:
I’m an avid hiker, both locally and across different states, and I absolutely love this app. It’s incredibly reliable and well worth the annual subscription fee, which I find reasonably priced. It feels like it has every trail in the country—and it’s consistently accurate. It’s never let me down.

I especially appreciate the automatic metrics, like total distance, remaining distance, and estimated time. The visual features are fantastic too—the app highlights the trail as you go, so you always know where you are and how much farther you have to hike.

One of my favorite features is the ability to download maps for offline use. Reception is often spotty on the trails, and this app has been a real lifesaver. Compared to paper maps from parks, which can be confusing or poorly designed, this app eliminates the need to carry one altogether.
author: Orangetabbies

title: Amazing resource for hikers 🥾
content: I love this app. I use it daily to check for my “not completed” and “completed trails.” I love doing a new trail every time I go out for a walk or hike and it’s easy to search for things around you and just get out there! I wish I could put trails into a category like “don’t do for a variety of reasons” but I hacked that by “saving” the trail and adding it to a list named just that. All in all, I like All Trails and love that my family has access to my location when I’m out there, as long as I send them the link that I’m starting the trail. However, my family has told me that it is delayed, so I wish there was a way for my family to get the app too and see my location within the app. It’s instead a link to a browser/web page with my location on the trail. But I still love this app! Just wanted to give my feedback :)
author: Ejbruin2011

title: Great app+Frustrating experience+good service=happy user!
content:
Updated: I was contacted by the developer and was told to delete and download the app and it worked! Anyone experiencing the below issue, try this fix! I love all trails and I’m so happy I can continue to use it glitch free!

I used to LOVE AllTrails! It was the most effective way for me to map, track and find trails in my area and get good info on the trails. It’s even helped me (when I had service) in spots when I would get off trail. But recently (starting in September maybe?) the app freezes and crashes within 45 seconds to a minute of use. I can barely use it so unfortunately I’ve stopped using it, which is frustrating because like I said I love this app! I have updated the app as much as I can, and my phone (iPhone8) and nothing has seemed to fix this problem. Super disappointed that I have to find another app or another way to navigate trails!
author: kbrance5

title: Fully converted to be a fan, I love it.
content:
Update: This is a must have for all hikers. The limitations that I found are almost entirely addressed by getting the Pro version. However, most people who just want to find a nearby place to go walking or hiking will love the free version. The saved recorded tracks from other users are invaluable. I really like the planning and drawing features in pro.
