I especially like how people are able to collectively add to the trails, and how layers of pictures that are geotagged and waypoints answer many questions about what to expect. I also like the archiving features for saving your adventures and I was even able to make a custom list for trails that I would like to try. Everything intuitively flows, you can open a trail wherever you see it in the app. Great job, I also appreciate how responsive the developers are to suggestions and questions.

—————————————

In principle this app was exactly what I was looking for but it has a couple of things lacking which are kind of frustrating.

First it seems to be incomplete. One specific example is Raptor Ridge Viewpoint in Escondido. I know that it is a continuation of a trail but it sure doesn’t show up.

There are some trails that have no information on them, you just see the trail symbol, you can’t highlight it, so basically it is a map only.

Then the display is frustrating because you can basically only highlight one trail at a time, so you lose information of trails that connect to it, I understand there’s a reason for wanting to display a single trail if someone is only looking for one trail but when you’re just exploring an area you want to see all the available trails.
author: M Shaw

title: Good to find hikes, not great to navigate
content:
This app has been fantastic in helping me find new hikes and developing my new found love of hiking over the past year. The user reviews and photos are helpful, directions are generally good using google maps and very helpful to download the trail maps with gps of your location.  

The record function needs to be improved.  I generally use this to navigate new hikes, especially those with lots of offshoots.  Unfortunately when I lock my phone the app doesn’t notify when I’ve gone off the trail until I open it again.  I’ve tried using on my Apple Watch, but have had problems with the record function stopping my existing recording (and then am forced to rate the hike before I can restart) and expanding the map to something I can actually see on the watch.  This seems to have gotten worse with the recent update and generally means keeping your phone unlocked for the duration of the hike.
author: hiker9999

title: Invaluable Tool
content: Just “broke in” the AllTrails app on our first hike of 2020...and can immediately see, this is going to be an invaluable tool.  I’m genuinely regretting my delay in getting this, subscribing to the PRO, and allowing this app to fully enhance our hiking experiences.  No more!  On our first use...even beyond the amazing stats...we experienced the significance of the “off trail” warning provided by the app.  Based off of the use of the GPS system (cell signal NOT required)...we inadvertently missed a turn.  Not realizing it...”the beep” that I thought was a text message coming through from someone...?  It was the app signaling to me that we were off the trail.  Saved us who knows how much time and effort. So many reason to upgrade to PRO...but considering the significant hikes associated with our ADK 46’er journey we’ll be undertaking...I can’t imaging hiking without it.  Thank you All Trails!!!
author: UpstateNY Dad

title: Love it
content: I love using AllTrails however, sometimes the mileage is inaccurate. I also wish that they had an iPhone widget to start tracking a hike without having to go through the app. I tend to forget to start tracking a hike until after I’ve started. Having a widget on the Home Screen would make it so much easier to remember. I think my favorite feature is that you can build your own map (I think this is a paid for feature however). As a naturalist who has to plan hikes for groups, this feature helps me to plan routes that many people wouldn’t think to take because it’s not an already established route. It also gives an estimated mileage which is helpful, but you do have to be mindful that in order to have the most accurate mileage, one needs to add a lot of points along the route to account for any smaller curves that you can’t see unless you’re zoomed in.
author: gordysmiles

title: Navigator Issues Ruin Great App
content:
There’s some great stuff here and some things that urgently need improvement.

FREE FEATURES: As a database, AllTrails is fantastic. I love being able to sort, filter, and find just the right trail anywhere I go. I also love that the reviews often provide excellent up-to-date trail reports (like whether snow has melted or how bad the mud is, currently)

PRO FEATURES: I have subscribed to AllTrails Pro for the last three years and have loved being able to download offline maps and plot my own route using the web tool before I hit the mountains. Mountains where I live seldom have cell-coverage, so offline maps is a very handy tool.

However, lately the new “Navigator” has been frustratingly unreliable. My GPS location will sometimes freeze for over an hour (makes things frustrating when you are trying to decide which fork in a trail to take—or if your summit is this one or the next one). Additionally, recorded tracks will often lack accurate data regarding vertical climb and miles travelled. Sometimes it doesn’t even recognize that I finished the route. This is especially frustrating, too when I go to tag the DSLR photos from my adventure.

On a side note, the watch app is halfhearted, but could be really great (as anyone who has used WorkOutDoors can tell you). Activity data is weirdly duplicated if you share with Apple’s Activity app and maps don’t load on the watch (even if you have pro) and do not have a cellular connection.

Sadly, I won’t renew my Pro subscription. Keep working AllTrails and I’ll be back!
author: Mark the Hiker

title: Update is terrible!
content: I have the pro version and before this recent update I was always able to look up trails- even when I didn’t have reception!  Now I have to look them up before I go and download them beforehand. A little annoying because sometimes we will change our mind and choose a different trail in the area. Also the red map lines are now written over the names of the trails! Really frustrating! Sometimes the names of hikes don’t match up to the route drawn, so I always like to zoom in and double check. Especially when hiking in the smokies. I also can’t read the distance points on the maps anymore. The red lines are written over those too. Please fix this!!!!! I have been a pro member for 3 years and which to continue being one.
author: atlantaree

title: Honest company
content: I don’t usually leave reviews but was really super pleased with their customer service. I accidentally forgot to cancel my 7 day subscription (because I had to log in on a web browser even though I had upgraded to plus on the app so not sure why it wasn’t available to manage directly in my iPhone subscriptions as instructed by the app itself) and was refunded without any hassle when I asked. As someone that lives in London, I don’t have much use for the app and really only intended to use it for one day so I was super relieved and grateful to not have to cover that expense!! The app itself is great as well—only used it for one day in the Grand Canyon but was super helpful especially considering I didn’t have phone service! Thank you!
author: Ana Rb

title: Good for finding trails, not recording hikes
content:
Probably the best app for finding good reviews of hikes. Unfortunately the recording leaves a lot to be desired. 1. HUGE power drain - just did a 3hr/5.5mile hike and my apple watch used 70% battery. It usually lasts all day no issue. Strava recording drains far less. 2. Found it paused about 1.5 miles in, but it was paused at .8 miles. Even if I did accidentally click pause, there was no way to tell until I noticed it hadn't been increasing numbers when I checked two times. I'd expect it to alert me to resume when it sensed movement. 3. After resuming from the pause, the GPS only updated my location when I opened the app or looked at my watch. So the rest of the hike has my track playing connect the dots every fork in the path when I checked the map. I stopped recording when we finished the loop, but it didn't record gps there so it ended about a mile short. Overall, a trail labeled 5.4miles (partners garmin says 5.5) registered as 3.3 on here. 4. This was all on the paid version of the app.

Update to respond to developer response:
1. Just lost a star. I reported an issue, you ignored it and have generic troubleshooting on an app store review. 
2. I sent support an email BEFORE writing that review, hoping to sort this issue out. It's been over a week and I haven't gotten a reply yet. 
3. It's not necessary for me to do this killing of other apps, I've never had an issue like this recording with Strava for example. I'd suggest fixing your app so it performs better.
author: GChaprnka

title: App crashes after roughly 5 seconds
content:
App repeatedly crashes a few seconds after launch today. It paused my hike twice but didn’t crash (app closes completely) when used two days ago. Powered down and restarted iPhone but that didn’t help. Searched App Support, which says I should send a crash report… but app crashes before I can do so. Signed in to AllTrails website as last ditch effort to find a trail and am surprised to see Someone Else’s Profile, including location of their deer blind set-up. Additionally, website doesn’t recognize that I have a paid subscription so I’m continually getting windows asking me to sign up as I try to sort/filter local trails. Literally can’t find anything “AllTrals”working today. I’m really running out of reasons to continue with AllTrails.

UPDATE: Deleted and reinstalled app on iPhone and it is working now. (Hopefully this info helps someone else.)

I still see someone else’s profile on AllTrails website so it seems the two issues are exclusive from one another.
author: TPZ2010

title: Easy to use for beginners but limited and not reliable
content: I have gone through a love/hate relationship with this app over the years. I used to use it as my main hiking app but moved to Gaia when they started forcing you to rate every hike. It is still a good app for finding nearby trails, but is not reliable for navigation and can direct you off trail. And the forced rating thing probably contributes to the dubious ratings. (On the occasions when I do use it I just click on a random rating for the hike so I can dismiss the screen and I know plenty of people who do something similar.) The paid version isn’t worth it because if you want offline navigation there are MUCH better options. I will repeat advice you will find a lot in the hiking community: Use the free version of All Trails for trail ideas, but don’t rely on it for navigation because it is not reliable. Instead get a paid version of a real navigation app for use on the trail.
author: Lightly Salted

title: Terrible
content: I paid for the membership mainly for the Apple Watch features, but it is completely useless.  First of all, you have to have your phone with you and have the app open on your phone which is a complete non-starter.  The Apple Watch app should be completely independent for this to be useful/valuable.  Second, it is almost impossible to get the app to even open on the watch (I had to force close the app on the watch and the phone, then open them at the same time… basically you have to get lucky for it to even work).  If you are lucky enough to get the Watch app to open, the top 1/4th of the map screen is blurred for no apparent reason AND the bright green trail line isn’t even visible.  It also drains the battery on your phone like crazy (not exactly what you want when you’re doing a multi day hike and need your phone to last as long as possible).  For me, this app is absolutely useless and I don’t understand how it got awarded best app of the year by Apple. It certainly is not.
author: dfeivelson

title: Good stuff, needs iPad app!
content:
I love AllTrails, great application and website. Use it all the time to do research on new hikes and enjoy adding conditions/photos from my experiences to pay it forward. I don’t do much to track hikes through AllTrails, which seems to be where most users are complaining. 

I can’t give it 5 stars, though, because it’s missing a dedicated iPad app! This is a wildly popular app, and I’m sure I’m not the only person who travels with an iPad instead of a laptop. The browser experience is less ideal on tablets, and the iPad app just displaying the phone app is a pretty clumsy execution.

I know adding iPadOS to your dev plate might be a hassle, but this is where I do my trail research while traveling. Not having any of the advantages a tablet brings over a phone is just a disappointment these days, but everything else is top notch
author: Tofuslasher

title: Awesome but can be improved
content:
I love this app and have been using it for years. 
Improvements needed:
1) They recently changed it so when you click on a trailhead on the map view, the little thumbnail no longer shows the elevation gain, it only shows the distance. I’m almost positive it used to show both. Distance and elevation gain are the two major factors I’m trying to quickly scan through to find my hikes. Please fix the thumbnails to show these two very important pieces of information!
2) When I’m searching the map view for hikes, and there is a cluster, WHY does it have to zoom way in? This is sooo annoying. I’m constantly having to zoom out. I want to click on the trailhead and see the red line (the route) in relation to the map view of the area. The app always zooms in so far that you have to back it out in order to see the outline of the route.
author: Mbeach85

title: Find trails and never get lost.
content:
A great app for discovering trails while traveling. Being able to see where you are located along the trail is the most useful feature. 
Wishlist: 
1) I wish the app would tell me which trail I’m on when I find one. I’ve visited parks with many trails… and sometimes I’m not at a trailhead to know which trail I’ve discovered. The app should be able to tell me which trail I’m on and where I am.
2) many hiking areas have multiple trails and some overlap.  The app separates each one by name….it would be less confusing to show trails overlapping not isolated. Perhaps separated by color?
3) when searching for trails in a specific park or conservation area the app often suggests trails elsewhere. That’s confusing when visiting a place for the first time. Just show me the trails in the geographic area I’ve tried to designate.
author: Forest Figure Sculptor

title: Not all updates are good
content: I very rarely write app reviews, but felt like I had to. I’ve had AllTrails for years, and absolutely loved it! From local trails in upstate NY to major hikes in the Rockies, AZ, CA, etc. Interface, usability, scanning through pictures, summaries of trails, map overviews and downloads were all amazing. The latest update has made the app less user friendly with respect to a few features — can’t easily scan through all photos of a trail and when looking, my phone actually slows down; the save your place map feature is not as user friendly as the options from before, since when I open a map of a hike I’m planning, I want to see the actual route and not a zoomed out map that includes my current location. This is something that I’ve seen a few other devoted users post, so please consider restoring some of the original features.
author: poe783

title: One little gripe, otherwise the best rail app
content:
This is a great app and I recommend any hiker use it. I’ve used it on four continents in at least 10 countries and it’s been great. My only complaint is the relationship between looking at a trail and looking at the map of trails around that trail. 

Sometimes I search for a specific location and I can only see one trail in that location. There should be a way to search for hikes around a trail. In other words, if I’m in a specific trail looking at it, there should be an easy button that says show me the map around this trail or something to that effect. That way I can see what other trails are immediately in the vicinity. 
Today, the functionality makes me go to the main map and scroll around until I find the location and that is cumbersome and irritating.
author: Nickname here you go

title: Why is a trail review is asked for in the middle of the hike?
content:
I am new to AllTrails. While on the first hike just when I needed to check my location in order to navigate around an obstacle a pop up screen is suddenly asking me to rate the hike and add a photo. I was not allowed to continue navigating until I complied. I would be happy to rate the hike maybe after it was completed but please don’t require a rating while I’m on the trail.
Later…
AllTrails has promptly replied to my comment which I really appreciate. They assured me that a rating request should not happen during the hike. Like I said , I’m a newbie to AllTrails so I’ll wait and see what happens. Subsequent hikes with AllTrails have been great with a rating request at the end of the hike but I’m still being locked out until I comply with their request.
Don’t get me wrong, I still like AllTrails.
author: ~_~gr

title: Bait and Switch on Lifetime Pro
content: If you purchased a few years ago like me, you may now be experiencing the push to upgrade to Pro. Reached out to customer support and they were argumentative and combative after I submitted the documentation they request. I provided my receipt from original purchase as well as a screen shot of my expired apps to show that no where on the receipt did it say it was a 3 year subscription and it also never auto renewed or expired like my other subscriptions. After submitting the documentation, the rep was rude and stated that the receipt didn’t say it was for a lifetime membership. It did not. It all did it say it was for a 3 year membership and the app wasn’t treated like a subscription app like all of my forgers (ie My Fitness Pal). It’s not my fault they started off with a bad business model, but it is their fault that they did and now aren’t honoring. I recommend you use Gaia GPS or one of the other apps. The offline maps for Gaia are better and no bait and switch with the subscription.
author: OphieK

title: This app truly has everything
content:
I have used this app on hikes in multiple countries on multiple continents. I’m astonished at how it has seemingly every hiking trail in the world on it. And it has saved my life a few times when it has shown me the way after some trail markers had disappeared. 

Most importantly are the great features of downloading offline maps (for when the Internet is low, as often happens on distant hikes), as well as information on specifics on the trails. 

Finally, this app gives great opportunities to scope out and plan future hikes easily, based on either location or any other criteria you want to search under.  My favorite is the map option where I can just scan the area and see which trails are available near me.
author: KSmith4964

title: Can no longer search my saved activities
content: This app has never been perfect - trails are crowd sourced and not always official trails. You should always refer to official trail maps for reference. The mileage and elevation gain are usually off compared to my Garmin. I use All Trails primarily to record my hikes, and up until recently, my saved activities could be found in the “saved” tab, where I could search easily for the name of the activity. I did this ALL time to refer back to how long a particular hike took me, what the elevation gain was, etc. With a new update to that app, that feature is now gone. Now the only way to search for an activity I’ve previously recorded is to use a browser, which is ridiculous. This update makes the app almost useless to me, as I can use Gaia GPS for saving and finding recorded activities instead. I hope All Trails fixes this quickly!
author: Beckyphry

title: Changes & removing trail
content:
This app allows trail names to be changed, trail information distance shortened or non existent, routes changes and / or modified. They allow whomever with whatever motivation to be rogue content advisors. Which I feel impacts a hiker bc  the information becomes inaccurate. They remove content of trails without explanation - which is not accurate with other sites including government websites. As a local to an area I have witnessed All Trails do harmful map and trail distortions and manipulative content modifications that as a local avid hiker finds to be 100% unacceptable. The maps should show All Trails - in oder to be worthy and honorable of its name. So this app is a farce. I do not recommend.
I hope in time this once decent resource goes away for its lack of due diligence.
author: MV in Clark County

title: Good app, but with a major flaw
content:
I appreciate the variety of maps available, and especially the active community with comments, often very recent, which help greatly in planning and knowing about expected trail conditions. The serious flaw is that on the map for each trail, it does not show any of the surrounding trails. So you can be looking at one possible hike, and not know that there are several others right nearby, or not understand where this hike is in relationship to other hikes that you may have already done. What makes this even more annoying is that there is no map view that provides an overview of all the trails in an area. You have to somehow search by the name of trails, or give a location, and it gives a list of all the different trails nearby. Except that many times the trails are simply different sections of the same trail, which wouldn’t be a problem if the map showed them both together, but it doesn’t. It only shows section a as hike a, and section b as high b, with no information showing the relationship. I find this to be greatly annoying and very inconvenient. OnX-Backcountry addresses this issue very nicely. On every map you can see all the surrounding trails, and you can tap on that trail to go look at it as well. I am going to be switching my subscription.
**** addendum in response to developer response: Thanks for the response. It is nice that there are pins showing nearby trailheads, however it would be still more useful to see all the nearby trails. Most importantly because they often interconnect. It is very frustrating when you are on one trail, and the network of surrounding trails is not visible on the map.  Frustratingly, all of the trails are in fact marked on the base maps with dotted lines, but there are no names nor is there any other identifying information(Such as distances or elevation gain etc.). Many times a hike may consist of starting on one “trail”, and connecting to other “trails“. It would be very helpful to see the trails all together. This is a feature that On-X Backcountry offers.
author: zebulon303

title: Wish it didn’t crash
content:
I love this App when it works. In the last year I have logged close to 600 miles through it. However, there would be more if it didn’t unexpectedly crash. Thankfully it “Saves you place” for you so if you catch that it’s not tracking you, you can restart. 

Crashes during hikes most often happen when I take photographs. Unfortunately, that is a huge part of why I walk so many miles. So that is a problem. It has gotten to the point where sometimes I choose not to take pictures because I don’t want the app to crash. 

That also means that instead of being present in the moment while I walk, I am worrying about an app that should run silently and reliably in the background. 

Finally, downloading maps, which is critical for any off grid hikes, exacerbates the crashing. To the point that when I let the app download the map from last night’s hike, I could no longer keep it open long enough to see my stats. The only solution when the app repeatedly crashes on launch is to delete the app and its data from my phone. Then reload it and sign into my Pro account. 

The fact that despite all of these shortcomings, frustrations, and bugs, I still use it for every hike, should indicate how potentially great this app could and should be.
author: rsnyder

title: I use AllTrails religiously!
content:
I seriously love this app. It’s the best for anything from planning multi-day backpacking trips to spontaneous trail runs. 

One update I would LOVE to see would be the option to tag other AllTrails users in my hikes! It would be so fun for the social aspect—having a log of who went with you where. It would also be sweet if when you were tagged you had the option to add your friend’s recorded stats. Sometimes you forget to hit record or resume, so how awesome would it be to have a backup recording from your friend so no trail goes unlogged?

Also... it wouldn't hurt to have a different cycle of photos to show up on the loading screen. Anyone else get a kick out of the current picture of a girl that looks like she’s headed to a dainty sorority picnic rather than a hike in the mountains...? 😂
author: Sammie Francis

title: Always closes while hiking
content: I put in 200 miles last year with this app (likely much more) but the app is always closing in the background. I went to troubleshoot on the website and they only offer the solution to “use navigator to make sure it’s doing enough activity in the background” which I do. It is ridiculous to expect users to keep the app on their screen with the screen open for the whole hike when your phone battery can be a lifesaver. Please update this bug. I’ve used this app with an iPhone 8+ as well as an 12 pro max with the same issues on both devices. Running the most up to date iOS at all times. Please fix. Until then I mostly have to use competitor’s apps. It also takes multiple tries to even get the app to boot up half the time. Please help, there is a lot potential for this app if it could be fixed.
author: thesecityskies

title: No Brainer! Hike YOUR best trails.
content:
I love paper maps and the mystery/surprise of following a new or unknown trail. However All Trails is a lifesaver for strenuous and long hikes ANYWHERE! 
I started hiking the White mountains this summer and there are literally thousands of trails up hundreds of summits. AllTrails is helping me find the most scenic routes that match my ability.  I can browse trail length and difficulty to find whatever I feel like on a given day.
You can download the AllTrails map on your phone so you will know if you’re on your planned route even if you have no cell service. Or you can print a PDF of your route and put it in a plastic baggie before you go.
  If I you have service, you can decide to shake your plan up and read reviews and ratings for crossing trails.
author: tmurph612

title: Intro to hiking must
content: Went out to Denver for a hiking trip. Had hiked a couple trains in the Smokey’s before so knew enough to take hiking boots but wasn’t ready for the vast selection and variations in trails. Friend recommended all trails once I got out there. Discovered it was possibly the next best thing since sliced bread. Got home opened all trails realizing I had tons of trails near me that I never really knew about. Great to know before going somewhere whether I can bring my dog or not. Also time durations are pretty accurate if you hold pace and don’t take any breaks. Don’t forget to record your hikes, allows you to make notes so you can put things like ‘when you think you’re at the top, you still have 1 mile to go.’ Or a note about mud or hiking poles. It sounds silly but you’ll be glad you do it.
author: ripchord29

title: Okay if you hike a lot and download maps
content: I found that I just didn’t use this app enough to justify my subscription.  Most of the time I tried to use it I’d have no cell signal, and it was almost useless...I’d have to plan ahead, pick a trail, download the map over WiFi...for it to work when I was hiking.  I also was unhappy because there was NO way to manage my subscription and I got auto-renewed even though I didn’t want to, even though I had the renewal date in my calendar and made an effort to prevent renewal. The stupid subscription did not show up in my Apple account subscriptions page as active or expired...when I went to the website it referred me to the app.   From the App account settings it sends you to the Apple Subscriptions page which Did NOT show the stupid subscription.  Customer service wasn’t helpful.  I had to contact my credit card company to decline the charge.
author: Mr thizzle

title: Unreliable, but usually pretty good
content:
I have been an alltrails+ subscriber for four years. I use it for all kinds of hiking, and backpacking, but mostly for working on my Adirondack 46 high peaks. The app is generally well designed and easy to use, but many of the hikes contain misleading or incorrect information regarding elevation gain, and mileage. I have also had numerous examples where alltrails has failed to continue tracking and halted my activity midway through.

I really enjoyed the ability to make custom maps on alltrails+, but that functionality was recently removed from that subscription and instead placed on the much more expensive Peak membership. I have canceled my all trails subscription, and will be seeking out a different Hiking app.

I expect better consistency from a navigation app that I use to keep me on track in the backcountry, and no amount of polish or sleek app design makes that unreliability worth it.
author: Jordandejewski97

title: Amazing app
content: This app is super helpful in planning a hike!  Shows all nearby trails by popularity, difficulty level, trail map, waypoints, photos and trails eviews.  Proved to be very accurate and usable.  We tried few easy and moderate trails and thoroughly enjoyed them.  One improvement in UI is it loses current position marker when you lock the phone.  You have to go back to navigate screen to refresh current location.  I primarily used in locations that had network.  if you are planning to go to remote locations,  it is better to download offline map (supported in paid pro subscription).  Alltrails app helped more than once when we went on the wrong path.  I was able to quickly consult the trail map and backtrack to correct path
author: MaxR01

title: Maps and pictures not loading
content:
Just recently noticed the pictures and some maps are not loading at all. Thought it was my iPad but it’s doing the same on my phone as well

One thing I really wish was changed is the altitude and mileage tracker on the bottom of the topography maps. One, it’s small to begin with because it’s on a phone screen and your finger hides most of the information when you’re sliding. It should have its own slider underneath the graph so I don’t have to try to look under my finger to see information. Two, I hate that the mileage points are not evenly spaced out. It goes from 1.2 to 3.6 to 5.1. It should be broken up into half or quarter mile increments to easily calculate distances. Furthermore, I know it shows you altitude in real time in the upper left hand corner as you’re sliding on the graph so why can’t it show you mileage as well? These hanged would be UBER helpful
author: Needle And Groove

title: All trails needs improving
content: First off, I have used Alltrails for years now and it has made a lot of trails accessible in places I do not call home, which has it’s pro’s and con’s. My main qualm with the app is I feel the rating system and maps available are not always suited for the type of person using this app. When a trail is defined as “hard” there is little to explain the reason. For example, if a trail has a section that is not a defined or an unmaintained trail, but a potential passage through a scree field at 45-60 degrees with possible life threatening falls, that is not hard. Those types of trails require a different level of experience that alltrails does not mention save for the reviews from other mountaineers/hikers. I wish that alltrails would start to include more about experience people should have to feel comfortable doing different hikes.
author: Solpac91

title: Great hike get there by 8am
content: We got there at 8:40. The permit, permit site, and the discussions and video for the hike did not tell us the park would close up at 8:30 am due to volume and not open again until noon. You pay them for a permit but you cannot get in. To bad for you. A little kindness would have been good. We were 4 cars behind the ranger car shutting it down. Park opens at 8. Had to try back 3 times to finally get in at noon. We also bumped into some grumpy people coming out of the trail loop the way most go in. They got lost repeatedly and gave up. This is our second time. We downloaded the map on all trails and set it to start tracking at the beginning. Small arrows painted in a couple places on rocks plus all trails works great.
author: Grlthng

title: Worth the price for offline navigation
content: Been using this app for a while, but it came in really handy on a scout trip to Pisgah National Forest recently. We had an old fashioned map (so the scouts can learn to use it) and compass, but I was also tracking our trek in the app the whole time. We had zero cell phone reception and were deep in the woods with 2,000 feet of climbing, but the app and GPS signal worked flawlessly. Great peace of mind when being responsible for a group of 12-year olds in the woods and quite helpful to show them afterwards what they had just accomplished. Also use it regularly for my own backpacking trips and love being able to create custom routes and then still use them for tracking on the hike itself. Great app!
author: BastianILM

title: Worse since update
content: I’ve been an AllTrails subscriber for 2 years. I would not recommend this app anymore. Try any of the competitors before this one. The latest update adding a new more expensive tier has made this app significantly worse. Specifically you can no longer view waypoints (which we’re incredibly useful for planning hikes) on the app and you have to have to new most expensive tier to create your own routes. Also the stupid points of interest icons on the map make it more difficult to simply find trails. I was happy to live with some of the other common complaints with this app like the mileages often being way off and certain routes being inaccurate but I plan on testing other hiking apps and as soon as I figure out which one is better I will cancel my all trail subscription and delete it. Super disappointed, I used to recommend AllTrails to friends and other hikers.
author: Gogators07

title: Saving grace for backpacking ventures
content:
I love how you can download offline maps in any format. I personally prefer satellite maps, but if you like topographical maps, they have that too. 
I also love how you can see the elevation changes from start to finish on a 2D chart. That really gives a good perspective on how difficult the trail will be. 
It’s nice being able to track your pace too. It helps me determine how long the rest of a trail will take. 
The weather on each route is helpful too. The default weather app on your phone doesn’t allow to track weather for more desolate areas. 
It is disappointing that you have to pay in order to get those features, but I think it is well worth it if you hunt, go off roading, or backpacking. 

The only upgrade I would like is if you could create your own route on the trails that are listed. The map clearly shows all the trails available in a certain area. I wish I could pick a route from junction to junction to find out how long a niche route would take. Having to search each route gets confusing with more than 2 junctions. 
Overall it’s a great app and I would highly recommend.
author: a Ryan Seacrest Type

title: Worth the download
content:
Visiting South Dakota I used AllTrails to discover the trail suggested and navigate in my vehicle to the trailhead. Started my ride on an out and back. When I got to the end of the trail to turn around my mobile no longer had my route and said “loading” or trouble loading. Tried to get back and could not. Then had to select the ride again and record coming back.
Not sure what the glitch was. 
    The fact that other riding apps did not have Tinton Rd trail on them. AllTrails navigated me to the trailhead and the map was very accurate to stay on trail. That’s what really mattered. I am not sure if others have stated this, but in the description of the trail and the time it takes it would be helpful to include the method. For example bike, hike or run.
I would still highly recommend this app.
author: Buffalosurfer

title: Best App ever!!
content:
AllTrails has completely transformed how I explore the outdoors. Whether I’m planning a long backcountry trek or a quick hike close to home, it’s the single most reliable tool I use. The trail maps are accurate, the filters make it easy to find routes that fit my time and fitness level, and the community reviews are often spot-on about current conditions.

I especially appreciate the offline maps — they’ve saved me more than once when cell service dropped deep in the mountains. The elevation profiles, photos, and recent user updates give a real sense of what to expect before heading out.

It’s not just an app; it’s a trusted companion for anyone who loves hiking, running, or biking. Every adventure starts here now.
author: Firenze2015

title: Basic Edit of recordings and custom point to point routing would be useful
content:
Sometimes I forget to stop my navigation recording and it of course then records my drive home. My mistake, BUT I wish I could go back into the saved recording and simply omit information, just by cutting it off after a time mark or waypoint. It’s frustrating as it really messes up my stats, either I keep the insane recording where it may add 70 miles hiked in an hour or I have to delete a 20 mile hike entirely. Seems like it would be easy and I can’t believe I’m the only one who forgets to stop recording after a long day.

CUSTOM POINT TO POINT routing and navigation would be a major feature to use.  I would personally like feature that generated a trail route based on my selected start and end points and waypoints.
author: ryan c thompson

title: We love AllTrails!
content:
Paid for the very reasonably priced pro subscription after just one hike because I’ve never found an app that does what AllTrails does nearly this well. Navigation is easy, accurate and helpful and the various tools for finding trails and even making your own have opened up many fun opportunities for my wife and I.
My only real wishes are that there were a little more collaboration between AllTrails and parks, so that official trails were all available as AllTrails routes, rather than just community-sourced ones, and I would also love the custom map creation feature from the website to be usable in the app!

Nonetheless, I am very pleased with all trails and will absolutely continue using it for all of our hiking! 🌲🥾
author: ai5lefive

title: Change to filter by rating
content: I love this app but they made it worse when they recently changed the system for filtering by star rating. They used to give us the ability to filter for 5 star hikes only and it would only show 4.75 star and above. This system allowed the ability to show only the best of the best. They changed the system so we can only filter by 4.5 star and above which gives way too many options in many cases and dilutes our ability to find the best of the best hikes in a area. It is now harder/near impossible and or takes much longer. It sounds like a small change but it makes a big difference. Please change it back or allow us to filter differently. Thanks
author: TDCis1

title: The Best Thing About AllTrails
content:
Have you ever gone hiking on what you thought was a well marked trail, and got lost?  Did you wonder around for 45 minutes trying to find South on your phone’s compass, knowing exactly what time it was going to get dark?  I have.  Not any more!  

I love AllTrails because when I want to take a walk or hike, I can pull up 500 trails near me!  I can learn the location, a description, and important details, like if I can bike it as well.  When I’m ready to go, I just click on the directions so I can drive to the trailhead, and then click on the map of the trail, which shows my location, on or off the trail, at all times.  No more fear of getting lost for me, is the end result, with more time to enjoy walking in nature.  Get AllTrails.  You and your family will love it!
author: Gale Newbold

title: The best ~$30/year you can spend in the app store
content: The first time I used Alltrails, it was the free version. The hike we were attempting was very disused, because the first mile had been clear cut and the remaining trail was unmarked and extremely difficult to find among the destruction. By using the real-time GPS tracking, we were able to match out position with the red trail line in Alltrails, and found the hidden trail to an almost forgotten alpine lake. We never would have done it without Alltrails. I purchased the full version of the app later that day, and have never looked back. I maintain my membership in the Washington Trails Association because of the great trail work and advocacy they do, but Alltrails in now my constant hiking and camping companion!
author: pinto32

title: Garbage
content:
If there’s one thing this app can be counted on for, it’s that it WILL stop recording in the middle of your hike/ride (so why even offer it?).  
  On top of that, when you download maps (pro), it doesn’t archive them in a way that offers convenient access when you’re on the go.  In fact, often times you have to re open and load the app (killing your battery in the process), remember and look up the exact trail you are on, and finally go to “my map” to view. 
  The app seems to be working really hard when you open it (understandably). I wish there was a way to bypass going through the app when all you may wish to do is peek at the map that you already downloaded. Boo!  :(
author: ColettiTheKid

title: Needs improvement
content:
Updated review June 7,2021.
Raising back to three stars. The crashing has gotten better. It still crashes now and then but now it doesn’t crash and fail to record my track. I’ll see what the update today does.

Updated review (dropped from 3 to 1 star): Okay, this app is useless to me. I’ve used it two times and it crashed multiple times on both occasions. I can’t count on this so it is useless to me. I really want a refund. I’m deleting it. The free version worked fine, it seems I paid for a piece of crap. Old review: I’ve been using the free version for two years with no problems. I paid for a year subscription, the first time I went out in a trail, this app crashed 3 times. Other than that, so far, it is a good app. They need to fix the crashes though. If it keeps crashing, I won’t renew my subscription.
author: makeitsoj

title: Great app, one big problem in pro version
content:
This is a fantastic app and really useful for hiking. It would be a wholehearted recommendation if it wasn't for one problem I keep running into.

The main reason for buying the pro version is offline maps access. Most trails I do are not where data coverage is available. So offline maps are critical.

Hiwever, once downloaded, they just go away (expire?) within a day or so. This is incredibly frustrating given how much effort I took to slowly download these maps in poor data areas,only to find it magically disappeared before the hike. 

I can appreciate needing to refresh mapping data. But the app should never discard downloaded maps without user consent. I was in the Himalayas and it would take multiple days to download a map of a trek, only to see it disappear a day or to later.

Also the process of selecting a custom nap for offline download requires substantial data which makes it almost impossible to select in low bw areas. This is likely not an app problem, but if the selection UI can somehow use very low detail data to just select region, that would be great.

Mostly just please fix offline map expiry problem!
author: yet another hiker

title: Reliable Hiking Companion for the Tatras and Beyond
content:
I’ve been using AllTrails for two consecutive years now, and this September will be my third — once again heading back to Poland to explore Zakopane and the Tatry National Park. From Morskie Oko to countless other trails, the app has been an absolute game changer.

What sets it apart is its reliability: no ads, stable performance, and it works perfectly offline using just GPS. That made our family adventures not only more fun, but also much safer — we could hike with confidence, knowing we wouldn’t lose our way even in the mountains.

After years of use, I can say AllTrails has consistently improved our outdoor experiences. If you’re planning to hike in the Tatras (or anywhere, really), this app is a must-have.
author: shake s pire

title: Nice maps, but not editable and no apple watch support
content: I really like that this app shows hiking trails in a high contrast so that they are visible even in the bright daylight. The problem is that there is no way to submit feedback in those cases when there are mistakes on the map. Another problem is that it is not possible to download larger regions for offline use. All is designed around finding a hike and then downloading a map around that specific hike. And for this you have to be connected to the internet. One extremely frustrating aspect is that when you are searching for a hike the list of suggestions completely disregards your location. If I live in Oregon and search for let's say Eagle creek trail, the on closest to me should be on top. This could be resolved by a preference settings to show the trails near you. It would also be great if you added apple watch support.
author: Hafík

title: Free for basic use and pretty great!
content: On the free end of this app you are able to easily filter out specific trails that you are looking for and wherever you want. You have full map access, you can filter things like paved, dirt, wheel chair friendly, etc. And you can also select features like waterfalls, lakes, scenery, elevation, and more. So for most local trails it’s super awesome. There’s also always photos and reviews on each of them. On the pro side of the app you have access to features like downloading maps, off route notifications, a bunch of safety things like sharing your location, and making it ad free. Adds don’t pop up or anything but they’re normally in the corners of the screen. This app is great!
author: youremothor

title: I love AllTrails
content: I’ve been using this app for over four years now. It really helped me find all the trailheads within my vicinity and it was cool having the Maps and being able to use the navigator to record the hikes. I was kind of bummed when they took the built-in photo feature out of the navigator, but I quickly realized that it wasn’t that big a deal since once the hike was over. The app would use the GPS coordinates in the meta data of the pictures to attach the pic to the trail map. And the community has come along way, but I’m kind of disappointed at how little interaction I’ve had with other hikers on the app ever since they made their recent improvements to the community interface. I was hoping to network and make some new friends and/or hiking buddies.
author: Red Ape 420

title: Great app, worth getting the subscription!
content: We have been using this app to find trails for a few weeks now and it’s been great. Being able to download maps for offline use is a lifesaver when you are trekking through less traveled areas, and some trailheads would be impossible to find without the guidance this app provides. I do find that reviews from recent users can be misleading as everyone is at a different fitness level and looking for different kinds of adventure, but most people try to provide helpful feedback that helps us decide what trails to do with our kids and which ones to skip until they are a little older. Overall totally worth the 30 bucks/year!
author: 30isthenew15

title: Great app with a few flaws
content:
Over all I love this app and I think most of the other 5 star reviews already mentioned the pros of it. Here are the things on the usability side that I wish they can improve
1. Offline maps only load when I am offline, this is very annoying when I am with not so great cell signal. My downloaded maps wouldn’t load because the app will try to load it live first and struggle. I had to turn to airplane mode in order to see the map then switch back online to send text message or make phone calls
2. The boot time of this app is insanely bad, i had to wait for 20+ seconds in order to use it for anything because it is entirely frozen during booting. one of the slowest loading app I’ve ever seen. 

I have a wild guess that the dev or design for this app doesn’t quit get how caching works.
author: Num9527

title: Great app. Could use some improvements.
content:
Great app. Could use improvements such as more choices in ways of organizing saved trails. Saved files need to be able to be ordered and switched, whether chronologically, alphabetically, by distance etc. depending on individual preferences. 

It would be nice to be able to see visually and immediately when you open a saved folder what trails have already been completed versus the ones that haven’t, like a 2-column type layout. Or be able to reorganize trails that have already been completed to the bottom of the list of saved trails. Just needs to be more choices for categorization and organization of saved trails. As a visual person the way the app is set up now I do not find to be optimal or the most effective.
author: babkababushka

title: Constant Prompts for Reviews, Tag Friends, Etc.
content:
First off - it’s fairly mediocre for MTB, but my main gripe is that the app never stops prompting you to review things, tag your friends, upgrade to an ever MORE premium version than the one you’re already paying for. There is just an incredible amount of friction to do even the simplest thing. Are you starting a trail? Not so fast! Did you just finish a trail? Not until you’ve tapped through ten screens and their unskippable animations. 

There are also no loading indicators for anything, which seems exceedingly optimistic for an app that is going to be used on data 99% of the time. I am constantly having to open/close the app until trails show up rather than a blank screen with no spinner, no error message, no indication that anything is happening at all.

That app is as sleekly designed as it is entirely unenjoyable to use.
author: GrinninColossis

title: Left me lost
content: I got this app specifically for a mtb trail that is on private land that has 32 miles of trail and is rated among the best trail systems in Texas.  It’s very heavily ridden.  Unfortunately, the map only included a portion of the trail system and once I got lost I found that I was miles off of the map on AllTrails so I couldn’t figure the way back.  These trails are directional so going in reverse and a slow climb against someone else coming down a quick decent is not an option.  Since it doesn’t have a monthly fee, I wasted the fee for an entire year for a map that doesn’t help me.  I have also had significant issues trying to get my Apple Watch to open the app.  It keeps telling me to open on my phone first, even though it was opened on my phone first.  I’ve gotten it to open on my watch while testing a few times, but when I want it in a hurry before starting a ride, no luck.
author: Steven 2002 mtb

title: Update is terrible!
content: I have the pro version and before this recent update I was always able to look up trails- even when I didn’t have reception!  Now I have to look them up before I go and download them beforehand. A little annoying because sometimes we will change our mind and choose a different trail in the area. Also the red map lines are now written over the names of the trails! Really frustrating! Sometimes the names of hikes don’t match up to the route drawn, so I always like to zoom in and double check. Especially when hiking in the smokies. I also can’t read the distance points on the maps anymore. The red lines are written over those too. Please fix this!!!!! I have been a pro member for 3 years and which to continue being one.
author: atlantaree

title: Honest company
content: I don’t usually leave reviews but was really super pleased with their customer service. I accidentally forgot to cancel my 7 day subscription (because I had to log in on a web browser even though I had upgraded to plus on the app so not sure why it wasn’t available to manage directly in my iPhone subscriptions as instructed by the app itself) and was refunded without any hassle when I asked. As someone that lives in London, I don’t have much use for the app and really only intended to use it for one day so I was super relieved and grateful to not have to cover that expense!! The app itself is great as well—only used it for one day in the Grand Canyon but was super helpful especially considering I didn’t have phone service! Thank you!
author: Ana Rb

title: Good for finding trails, not recording hikes
content:
Probably the best app for finding good reviews of hikes. Unfortunately the recording leaves a lot to be desired. 1. HUGE power drain - just did a 3hr/5.5mile hike and my apple watch used 70% battery. It usually lasts all day no issue. Strava recording drains far less. 2. Found it paused about 1.5 miles in, but it was paused at .8 miles. Even if I did accidentally click pause, there was no way to tell until I noticed it hadn't been increasing numbers when I checked two times. I'd expect it to alert me to resume when it sensed movement. 3. After resuming from the pause, the GPS only updated my location when I opened the app or looked at my watch. So the rest of the hike has my track playing connect the dots every fork in the path when I checked the map. I stopped recording when we finished the loop, but it didn't record gps there so it ended about a mile short. Overall, a trail labeled 5.4miles (partners garmin says 5.5) registered as 3.3 on here. 4. This was all on the paid version of the app.

Update to respond to developer response:
1. Just lost a star. I reported an issue, you ignored it and have generic troubleshooting on an app store review. 
2. I sent support an email BEFORE writing that review, hoping to sort this issue out. It's been over a week and I haven't gotten a reply yet. 
3. It's not necessary for me to do this killing of other apps, I've never had an issue like this recording with Strava for example. I'd suggest fixing your app so it performs better.
author: GChaprnka

title: App crashes after roughly 5 seconds
content:
App repeatedly crashes a few seconds after launch today. It paused my hike twice but didn’t crash (app closes completely) when used two days ago. Powered down and restarted iPhone but that didn’t help. Searched App Support, which says I should send a crash report… but app crashes before I can do so. Signed in to AllTrails website as last ditch effort to find a trail and am surprised to see Someone Else’s Profile, including location of their deer blind set-up. Additionally, website doesn’t recognize that I have a paid subscription so I’m continually getting windows asking me to sign up as I try to sort/filter local trails. Literally can’t find anything “AllTrals”working today. I’m really running out of reasons to continue with AllTrails.

UPDATE: Deleted and reinstalled app on iPhone and it is working now. (Hopefully this info helps someone else.)

I still see someone else’s profile on AllTrails website so it seems the two issues are exclusive from one another.
author: TPZ2010

title: Easy to use for beginners but limited and not reliable
content: I have gone through a love/hate relationship with this app over the years. I used to use it as my main hiking app but moved to Gaia when they started forcing you to rate every hike. It is still a good app for finding nearby trails, but is not reliable for navigation and can direct you off trail. And the forced rating thing probably contributes to the dubious ratings. (On the occasions when I do use it I just click on a random rating for the hike so I can dismiss the screen and I know plenty of people who do something similar.) The paid version isn’t worth it because if you want offline navigation there are MUCH better options. I will repeat advice you will find a lot in the hiking community: Use the free version of All Trails for trail ideas, but don’t rely on it for navigation because it is not reliable. Instead get a paid version of a real navigation app for use on the trail.
author: Lightly Salted

title: Terrible
content: I paid for the membership mainly for the Apple Watch features, but it is completely useless.  First of all, you have to have your phone with you and have the app open on your phone which is a complete non-starter.  The Apple Watch app should be completely independent for this to be useful/valuable.  Second, it is almost impossible to get the app to even open on the watch (I had to force close the app on the watch and the phone, then open them at the same time… basically you have to get lucky for it to even work).  If you are lucky enough to get the Watch app to open, the top 1/4th of the map screen is blurred for no apparent reason AND the bright green trail line isn’t even visible.  It also drains the battery on your phone like crazy (not exactly what you want when you’re doing a multi day hike and need your phone to last as long as possible).  For me, this app is absolutely useless and I don’t understand how it got awarded best app of the year by Apple. It certainly is not.
author: dfeivelson

title: Good stuff, needs iPad app!
content:
I love AllTrails, great application and website. Use it all the time to do research on new hikes and enjoy adding conditions/photos from my experiences to pay it forward. I don’t do much to track hikes through AllTrails, which seems to be where most users are complaining. 

I can’t give it 5 stars, though, because it’s missing a dedicated iPad app! This is a wildly popular app, and I’m sure I’m not the only person who travels with an iPad instead of a laptop. The browser experience is less ideal on tablets, and the iPad app just displaying the phone app is a pretty clumsy execution.

I know adding iPadOS to your dev plate might be a hassle, but this is where I do my trail research while traveling. Not having any of the advantages a tablet brings over a phone is just a disappointment these days, but everything else is top notch
author: Tofuslasher

title: Awesome but can be improved
content:
I love this app and have been using it for years. 
Improvements needed:
1) They recently changed it so when you click on a trailhead on the map view, the little thumbnail no longer shows the elevation gain, it only shows the distance. I’m almost positive it used to show both. Distance and elevation gain are the two major factors I’m trying to quickly scan through to find my hikes. Please fix the thumbnails to show these two very important pieces of information!
2) When I’m searching the map view for hikes, and there is a cluster, WHY does it have to zoom way in? This is sooo annoying. I’m constantly having to zoom out. I want to click on the trailhead and see the red line (the route) in relation to the map view of the area. The app always zooms in so far that you have to back it out in order to see the outline of the route.
author: Mbeach85

title: Find trails and never get lost.
content:
A great app for discovering trails while traveling. Being able to see where you are located along the trail is the most useful feature. 
Wishlist: 
1) I wish the app would tell me which trail I’m on when I find one. I’ve visited parks with many trails… and sometimes I’m not at a trailhead to know which trail I’ve discovered. The app should be able to tell me which trail I’m on and where I am.
2) many hiking areas have multiple trails and some overlap.  The app separates each one by name….it would be less confusing to show trails overlapping not isolated. Perhaps separated by color?
3) when searching for trails in a specific park or conservation area the app often suggests trails elsewhere. That’s confusing when visiting a place for the first time. Just show me the trails in the geographic area I’ve tried to designate.
author: Forest Figure Sculptor

title: Not all updates are good
content: I very rarely write app reviews, but felt like I had to. I’ve had AllTrails for years, and absolutely loved it! From local trails in upstate NY to major hikes in the Rockies, AZ, CA, etc. Interface, usability, scanning through pictures, summaries of trails, map overviews and downloads were all amazing. The latest update has made the app less user friendly with respect to a few features — can’t easily scan through all photos of a trail and when looking, my phone actually slows down; the save your place map feature is not as user friendly as the options from before, since when I open a map of a hike I’m planning, I want to see the actual route and not a zoomed out map that includes my current location. This is something that I’ve seen a few other devoted users post, so please consider restoring some of the original features.
author: poe783

title: One little gripe, otherwise the best rail app
content:
This is a great app and I recommend any hiker use it. I’ve used it on four continents in at least 10 countries and it’s been great. My only complaint is the relationship between looking at a trail and looking at the map of trails around that trail. 

Sometimes I search for a specific location and I can only see one trail in that location. There should be a way to search for hikes around a trail. In other words, if I’m in a specific trail looking at it, there should be an easy button that says show me the map around this trail or something to that effect. That way I can see what other trails are immediately in the vicinity. 
Today, the functionality makes me go to the main map and scroll around until I find the location and that is cumbersome and irritating.
author: Nickname here you go

title: Why is a trail review is asked for in the middle of the hike?
content:
I am new to AllTrails. While on the first hike just when I needed to check my location in order to navigate around an obstacle a pop up screen is suddenly asking me to rate the hike and add a photo. I was not allowed to continue navigating until I complied. I would be happy to rate the hike maybe after it was completed but please don’t require a rating while I’m on the trail.
Later…
AllTrails has promptly replied to my comment which I really appreciate. They assured me that a rating request should not happen during the hike. Like I said , I’m a newbie to AllTrails so I’ll wait and see what happens. Subsequent hikes with AllTrails have been great with a rating request at the end of the hike but I’m still being locked out until I comply with their request.
Don’t get me wrong, I still like AllTrails.
author: ~_~gr

title: Bait and Switch on Lifetime Pro
content: If you purchased a few years ago like me, you may now be experiencing the push to upgrade to Pro. Reached out to customer support and they were argumentative and combative after I submitted the documentation they request. I provided my receipt from original purchase as well as a screen shot of my expired apps to show that no where on the receipt did it say it was a 3 year subscription and it also never auto renewed or expired like my other subscriptions. After submitting the documentation, the rep was rude and stated that the receipt didn’t say it was for a lifetime membership. It did not. It all did it say it was for a 3 year membership and the app wasn’t treated like a subscription app like all of my forgers (ie My Fitness Pal). It’s not my fault they started off with a bad business model, but it is their fault that they did and now aren’t honoring. I recommend you use Gaia GPS or one of the other apps. The offline maps for Gaia are better and no bait and switch with the subscription.
author: OphieK

title: This app truly has everything
content:
I have used this app on hikes in multiple countries on multiple continents. I’m astonished at how it has seemingly every hiking trail in the world on it. And it has saved my life a few times when it has shown me the way after some trail markers had disappeared. 

Most importantly are the great features of downloading offline maps (for when the Internet is low, as often happens on distant hikes), as well as information on specifics on the trails. 

Finally, this app gives great opportunities to scope out and plan future hikes easily, based on either location or any other criteria you want to search under.  My favorite is the map option where I can just scan the area and see which trails are available near me.
author: KSmith4964

title: Can no longer search my saved activities
content: This app has never been perfect - trails are crowd sourced and not always official trails. You should always refer to official trail maps for reference. The mileage and elevation gain are usually off compared to my Garmin. I use All Trails primarily to record my hikes, and up until recently, my saved activities could be found in the “saved” tab, where I could search easily for the name of the activity. I did this ALL time to refer back to how long a particular hike took me, what the elevation gain was, etc. With a new update to that app, that feature is now gone. Now the only way to search for an activity I’ve previously recorded is to use a browser, which is ridiculous. This update makes the app almost useless to me, as I can use Gaia GPS for saving and finding recorded activities instead. I hope All Trails fixes this quickly!
author: Beckyphry

title: Changes & removing trail
content:
This app allows trail names to be changed, trail information distance shortened or non existent, routes changes and / or modified. They allow whomever with whatever motivation to be rogue content advisors. Which I feel impacts a hiker bc  the information becomes inaccurate. They remove content of trails without explanation - which is not accurate with other sites including government websites. As a local to an area I have witnessed All Trails do harmful map and trail distortions and manipulative content modifications that as a local avid hiker finds to be 100% unacceptable. The maps should show All Trails - in oder to be worthy and honorable of its name. So this app is a farce. I do not recommend.
I hope in time this once decent resource goes away for its lack of due diligence.
author: MV in Clark County

title: Good app, but with a major flaw
content:
I appreciate the variety of maps available, and especially the active community with comments, often very recent, which help greatly in planning and knowing about expected trail conditions. The serious flaw is that on the map for each trail, it does not show any of the surrounding trails. So you can be looking at one possible hike, and not know that there are several others right nearby, or not understand where this hike is in relationship to other hikes that you may have already done. What makes this even more annoying is that there is no map view that provides an overview of all the trails in an area. You have to somehow search by the name of trails, or give a location, and it gives a list of all the different trails nearby. Except that many times the trails are simply different sections of the same trail, which wouldn’t be a problem if the map showed them both together, but it doesn’t. It only shows section a as hike a, and section b as high b, with no information showing the relationship. I find this to be greatly annoying and very inconvenient. OnX-Backcountry addresses this issue very nicely. On every map you can see all the surrounding trails, and you can tap on that trail to go look at it as well. I am going to be switching my subscription.
**** addendum in response to developer response: Thanks for the response. It is nice that there are pins showing nearby trailheads, however it would be still more useful to see all the nearby trails. Most importantly because they often interconnect. It is very frustrating when you are on one trail, and the network of surrounding trails is not visible on the map.  Frustratingly, all of the trails are in fact marked on the base maps with dotted lines, but there are no names nor is there any other identifying information(Such as distances or elevation gain etc.). Many times a hike may consist of starting on one “trail”, and connecting to other “trails“. It would be very helpful to see the trails all together. This is a feature that On-X Backcountry offers.
author: zebulon303

title: Wish it didn’t crash
content:
I love this App when it works. In the last year I have logged close to 600 miles through it. However, there would be more if it didn’t unexpectedly crash. Thankfully it “Saves you place” for you so if you catch that it’s not tracking you, you can restart. 

Crashes during hikes most often happen when I take photographs. Unfortunately, that is a huge part of why I walk so many miles. So that is a problem. It has gotten to the point where sometimes I choose not to take pictures because I don’t want the app to crash. 

That also means that instead of being present in the moment while I walk, I am worrying about an app that should run silently and reliably in the background. 

Finally, downloading maps, which is critical for any off grid hikes, exacerbates the crashing. To the point that when I let the app download the map from last night’s hike, I could no longer keep it open long enough to see my stats. The only solution when the app repeatedly crashes on launch is to delete the app and its data from my phone. Then reload it and sign into my Pro account. 

The fact that despite all of these shortcomings, frustrations, and bugs, I still use it for every hike, should indicate how potentially great this app could and should be.
author: rsnyder

title: I use AllTrails religiously!
content:
I seriously love this app. It’s the best for anything from planning multi-day backpacking trips to spontaneous trail runs. 

One update I would LOVE to see would be the option to tag other AllTrails users in my hikes! It would be so fun for the social aspect—having a log of who went with you where. It would also be sweet if when you were tagged you had the option to add your friend’s recorded stats. Sometimes you forget to hit record or resume, so how awesome would it be to have a backup recording from your friend so no trail goes unlogged?

Also... it wouldn't hurt to have a different cycle of photos to show up on the loading screen. Anyone else get a kick out of the current picture of a girl that looks like she’s headed to a dainty sorority picnic rather than a hike in the mountains...? 😂
author: Sammie Francis

title: Always closes while hiking
content: I put in 200 miles last year with this app (likely much more) but the app is always closing in the background. I went to troubleshoot on the website and they only offer the solution to “use navigator to make sure it’s doing enough activity in the background” which I do. It is ridiculous to expect users to keep the app on their screen with the screen open for the whole hike when your phone battery can be a lifesaver. Please update this bug. I’ve used this app with an iPhone 8+ as well as an 12 pro max with the same issues on both devices. Running the most up to date iOS at all times. Please fix. Until then I mostly have to use competitor’s apps. It also takes multiple tries to even get the app to boot up half the time. Please help, there is a lot potential for this app if it could be fixed.
author: thesecityskies

title: No Brainer! Hike YOUR best trails.
content:
I love paper maps and the mystery/surprise of following a new or unknown trail. However All Trails is a lifesaver for strenuous and long hikes ANYWHERE! 
I started hiking the White mountains this summer and there are literally thousands of trails up hundreds of summits. AllTrails is helping me find the most scenic routes that match my ability.  I can browse trail length and difficulty to find whatever I feel like on a given day.
You can download the AllTrails map on your phone so you will know if you’re on your planned route even if you have no cell service. Or you can print a PDF of your route and put it in a plastic baggie before you go.
  If I you have service, you can decide to shake your plan up and read reviews and ratings for crossing trails.
author: tmurph612

title: Intro to hiking must
content: Went out to Denver for a hiking trip. Had hiked a couple trains in the Smokey’s before so knew enough to take hiking boots but wasn’t ready for the vast selection and variations in trails. Friend recommended all trails once I got out there. Discovered it was possibly the next best thing since sliced bread. Got home opened all trails realizing I had tons of trails near me that I never really knew about. Great to know before going somewhere whether I can bring my dog or not. Also time durations are pretty accurate if you hold pace and don’t take any breaks. Don’t forget to record your hikes, allows you to make notes so you can put things like ‘when you think you’re at the top, you still have 1 mile to go.’ Or a note about mud or hiking poles. It sounds silly but you’ll be glad you do it.
author: ripchord29

title: Okay if you hike a lot and download maps
content: I found that I just didn’t use this app enough to justify my subscription.  Most of the time I tried to use it I’d have no cell signal, and it was almost useless...I’d have to plan ahead, pick a trail, download the map over WiFi...for it to work when I was hiking.  I also was unhappy because there was NO way to manage my subscription and I got auto-renewed even though I didn’t want to, even though I had the renewal date in my calendar and made an effort to prevent renewal. The stupid subscription did not show up in my Apple account subscriptions page as active or expired...when I went to the website it referred me to the app.   From the App account settings it sends you to the Apple Subscriptions page which Did NOT show the stupid subscription.  Customer service wasn’t helpful.  I had to contact my credit card company to decline the charge.
author: Mr thizzle

title: Unreliable, but usually pretty good
content:
I have been an alltrails+ subscriber for four years. I use it for all kinds of hiking, and backpacking, but mostly for working on my Adirondack 46 high peaks. The app is generally well designed and easy to use, but many of the hikes contain misleading or incorrect information regarding elevation gain, and mileage. I have also had numerous examples where alltrails has failed to continue tracking and halted my activity midway through.

I really enjoyed the ability to make custom maps on alltrails+, but that functionality was recently removed from that subscription and instead placed on the much more expensive Peak membership. I have canceled my all trails subscription, and will be seeking out a different Hiking app.

I expect better consistency from a navigation app that I use to keep me on track in the backcountry, and no amount of polish or sleek app design makes that unreliability worth it.
author: Jordandejewski97

title: Amazing app
content: This app is super helpful in planning a hike!  Shows all nearby trails by popularity, difficulty level, trail map, waypoints, photos and trails eviews.  Proved to be very accurate and usable.  We tried few easy and moderate trails and thoroughly enjoyed them.  One improvement in UI is it loses current position marker when you lock the phone.  You have to go back to navigate screen to refresh current location.  I primarily used in locations that had network.  if you are planning to go to remote locations,  it is better to download offline map (supported in paid pro subscription).  Alltrails app helped more than once when we went on the wrong path.  I was able to quickly consult the trail map and backtrack to correct path
author: MaxR01

title: Maps and pictures not loading
content:
Just recently noticed the pictures and some maps are not loading at all. Thought it was my iPad but it’s doing the same on my phone as well

One thing I really wish was changed is the altitude and mileage tracker on the bottom of the topography maps. One, it’s small to begin with because it’s on a phone screen and your finger hides most of the information when you’re sliding. It should have its own slider underneath the graph so I don’t have to try to look under my finger to see information. Two, I hate that the mileage points are not evenly spaced out. It goes from 1.2 to 3.6 to 5.1. It should be broken up into half or quarter mile increments to easily calculate distances. Furthermore, I know it shows you altitude in real time in the upper left hand corner as you’re sliding on the graph so why can’t it show you mileage as well? These hanged would be UBER helpful
author: Needle And Groove

title: All trails needs improving
content: First off, I have used Alltrails for years now and it has made a lot of trails accessible in places I do not call home, which has it’s pro’s and con’s. My main qualm with the app is I feel the rating system and maps available are not always suited for the type of person using this app. When a trail is defined as “hard” there is little to explain the reason. For example, if a trail has a section that is not a defined or an unmaintained trail, but a potential passage through a scree field at 45-60 degrees with possible life threatening falls, that is not hard. Those types of trails require a different level of experience that alltrails does not mention save for the reviews from other mountaineers/hikers. I wish that alltrails would start to include more about experience people should have to feel comfortable doing different hikes.
author: Solpac91

title: Great hike get there by 8am
content: We got there at 8:40. The permit, permit site, and the discussions and video for the hike did not tell us the park would close up at 8:30 am due to volume and not open again until noon. You pay them for a permit but you cannot get in. To bad for you. A little kindness would have been good. We were 4 cars behind the ranger car shutting it down. Park opens at 8. Had to try back 3 times to finally get in at noon. We also bumped into some grumpy people coming out of the trail loop the way most go in. They got lost repeatedly and gave up. This is our second time. We downloaded the map on all trails and set it to start tracking at the beginning. Small arrows painted in a couple places on rocks plus all trails works great.
author: Grlthng

title: Worth the price for offline navigation
content: Been using this app for a while, but it came in really handy on a scout trip to Pisgah National Forest recently. We had an old fashioned map (so the scouts can learn to use it) and compass, but I was also tracking our trek in the app the whole time. We had zero cell phone reception and were deep in the woods with 2,000 feet of climbing, but the app and GPS signal worked flawlessly. Great peace of mind when being responsible for a group of 12-year olds in the woods and quite helpful to show them afterwards what they had just accomplished.
