My one tip would be to always download the map Layers before u loose reception this way it will load & work perfect. If u don’t do this then it might not load & u can get lost out there. I like the recording option, the fact u can connect it to ur health app etc. just bring a solar charger or battery pack with you cause the recording eats thru my battery life.  I would not use any other app as we love this one.
author: GAJAM2020

title: Great informative hiking app!
content: Being from somewhere where hiking isn’t as available or popular to CO, I loved being able to find hikes by map, distance, difficulty, or features. Access to trail reviews and photos, especially recent ones, is so helpful in planning. The ability to record your trail progress is great, too, both for memories and to track your personal stats. My only suggestion would be to design the app better for an iPad screen (shows about iPhone screen size on the iPad), but that’s pretty inconsequential as both the iPhone app and website are very easy to use. If you want tons of hike information in one place, you’ve come to the right place!
author: Megan_E_S

title: Wish the map actually showed the trails
content: I have paid for other trail subscriptions through other companies and I feel like this one is really lacking in one area. At least for a paid subscription you should be able to see trail outlines when viewing a map of all the trails in an area, not just a circle defining a trail is arbitrarily in that area. All of the trails should be visible in the full scale map with more detail shown the further you are zoomed in. I should be able to see not just a dot of the trailhead on the main map but also the trail and with the ability to click the trail. This makes it much easier to understand where a trail will go without needing to click on every single trail to understand if it’s the trail that goes up over the ridge or up to the lake in the area. Until this feature is added, I won’t be satisfied with the app.
author: Blipblipblop

title: Pro Version is Glitchy
content:
At the beginning of the year my husband upgraded to the pro version because we would be doing longer and more difficult hikes. 

Before our hike we would download the map and made sure it was downloaded, but once we got on trail it would show that the map didn’t download. In the case that it would download, if we would go a while, let’s say an hour without looking at the map, the app would shut off. So we would have to open the app again and reopen the map to figure out where we were. There was actually an instance where we were constantly needing to refer back to the map, but the app would keep closing. It was a frustrating to have to let the app load and then reopen the map. 

I like to use app to look for trails, but using the pro version in our experience has become frustrating.
author: Norma_ca

title: Phone app is good... watch app is useless
content:
I like the phone app for finding trails but it still should be so much better. For instance if I lose connection and reconnect, it doesn't record the distance traveled between the lost connection and the reconnection. It would be safe to make some assumptions or use step data from Health and fill in the blanks. 

The watch app is useless. They should be embarrassed. More often then not it gets stuck trying to connect to phone. If lucky enough to connect, it will usually lose connection (and I'm using the newest phone AND ultra 2). What's the point of downloading apps and not being able to also send them to my watch. I don't want to be looking at my phone. And as a subscriber this is doubly frustrating. Will likely cancel subscription and look for alternatives.
author: Fitnessmentor

title: LOSE THE TILT
content:
Update 7JUN22: The development team appears to have fixed whatever glitch was causing the excessively slow loading. I’ve since updated this from a two star to a four star. I just hope this doesn’t happen again prior to my backpacking trip this summer. 

————————————————————————

This app used to be super awesome and very user friendly (still is). Now after a few updates they felt it necessary to add a z-axis as if someone is going to open this is SOCET and lay some shapefile with DTED. With this addition is makes a beautiful app near worthless as the time it takes to process is unreasonable especially when actually on the trail for which the app was intended. Even if you download the map!!! Sad to see another useful tool destroyed by some desk jockey.
author: Patrick16273

title: Best for hiking in the NH White Mnts
content: I love this AP. I have used it extensively in New Hampshire and in Scotland UK and it worked great. There are limits as you need a good GPS signal to follow your progress live but that is true of any GPS enabled device. I always take my Garmin GPS and paper maps and compass as back ups as the Garmin usually always gets a signal and maps don’t need a signal! , but have been using the back ups less and less with All Trails becoming my main system for hiking and planning routes. Worked great in Scotland for a hike of Mount Suilven. I plan to add a Bad Elf external GPS Receiver in the future to improve the signal for All Trails when in dense forested areas of the White Mnts. Overall All Trails is a great AP with up to date maps for hiking all over the globe and I highly recommend it.
author: Green1956

title: Not worth it anymore
content: I’ve been an AllTrails+ subscriber for years and this app has taken me to some truly unique places. Thing is, it was already pretty expensive at $35/year and other apps (even free ones like Apple Maps) have become too competitive to justify the price. Now, they’ve locked some of the best features that I used to enjoy as an AllTrails+ subscriber behind a drastically more expensive $80/year subscription tier. It’s just not worth it anymore. It’s blatantly obvious that their number one priority is driving profit for the handful of private equity firms that have become their majority shareholders. They’ve been ignoring the bugs and frustrating UX issues for years as they put their effort into advertising merch and ensuring every single screen prompts you to upgrade your already expensive membership. Sorry, y’all lost the plot and members are going elsewhere.
author: Poot Lovato III

title: Poor app design
content:
Awful dark patterns intended to trick you into signing up for their paid subscription, they force you to create an account even for the "free" version for absolutely no reason, not to mention this app is terrible at what it is intended to do--finding trails! Doesn't provide basic park info (such as hours), search and filtering are painful to use, and the few external links there are about the parks are put in non-selectable text areas so the links can't be used! Skip this app.

Update: the developer responded to my review with an outright lie. You CANNOT dismiss their popular and keep using the app! You get forced into creating an account after being mislead into thinking the app doesn't need one, all by using really underhanded and misleading tactics and then they still try and force the user into a subscription. I'm still shocked that Apple allows such terrible business practices in their App Store, they really shouldn't.
author: Dash Rantic

title: AT Review
content:
I’m sitting here with my Garmin and IPhone 11 and wondering how Garmin survives with 1990’s screen navigation-makes Balckberry look like iPhone 14. My Garmin Inreach has Sat Text/SOS and that’s pretty much the only reason to carry it other than duplicate position/route recording. Conversely AT is so intuitive and easy to use.  Most local routes I can set up to record while walking from the car to trail head.  I screen capture routes and send to family for SARS if I’m
Injured or lost (send iPhone location as well).
I had Strava for awhile but never was able to record on it though it has a function you can compare your speeds with others on Strava for the same route-see “ladder below”.
I have a number of suggestions to improve AT without criticism (mostly):

Route ladder by age (see Strava comment)
Personal best on repeated routes
Tot miles by route per week/month/year/total
Current maps load and shift locations slowly 
Self design routes on phone, not on op top only 
Mark times @ summit/marked way pts vs by mile
Many “verified completed” routes are incorrect 
Frequent routes have diff gain/elevation recorded
author: carpemontem

title: Needs much improvement!!!!!
content: I used this app to through hike the Sheltowee Trace Trail and in most places along the trail the red line does not precisely follow the trail. Also there is no arrowhead to show your direction of travel, which is a critical flaw in this app. There is no ability to measure distance between where you are and a user defined point, another critical flaw for this type of an app. Where there is a divergence in the trail for a high water route, it picks one, even if it is not the main route. There should be a notification, so that you can make an educated choice. In many places where the trail is confusing, it is often accompanied by poor GPS accuracy, but app does not alert you to this. There is no great app that has all the needed features, so I ended up using several apps. Some of the info that this app provides is not available elsewhere.
author: Marianne2010

title: I love it but it lies
content: I generally love AT. It provides accurate maps, is great then the trail is not marked, tracks moving time vs total time without the need to pause, and the live feature and updates they have done to it are great since I do a lot of solo hiking as a woman. The weather updates are a really plus because it’s hard to find accurate weather information for a trail. I also really like the plus feature that allows you to create your own trail. The most frustrating part about AT is the distances are not accurate. You should always anticipate the mileage will be more than what it says and you cannot compare the mileage you have completed to the mile marker on the map to calculate how much further you have.
author: LovesPolar

title: Dangerously inaccurate app
content: First time using AllTrails, we used it on a 30 mile hike in Western Colorado. According to AllTrails, we had 7 miles left on the last day. This could not have been further from the truth. We had to backpack 15 miles the last day. Depending on AllTrails, we thought the last day was manageable. We did backpack 15 miles the last day but only because we absolutely had to get home that day. It was miserable and exhausting. If the inaccuracy was greater or if we were not as fit or if there was no water along the way, alltrails’ inaccuracy would have caused serious problems. I will never depend on AllTrails again and I am telling all of my hiking friends the dangers of using this app. Drop the money on a Garmin, do not depend on this app. To alltrails, if your map is inaccurate with distance then do not provide the distance. There is no shame in not having all the issues worked out, just don’t pretend otherwise.
author: trenton9637208472926

title: So disappointed
content:
This app which started as a great concept to review and find new trails had  become a data hungry cash grab. This app requires a profile linked to a email so they can collect data and sell, not to mention it has a premium paid subscription as well, I paid for the subscription but found I didn’t need or use any of the services it provided. In honest printing and downloading maps is annoying and not easily defined within the app. I also will just say this, it lets you look at the map, but without signing in so they can collect data the app won’t let you look at any hikes in detail. It’s unethical and completely useless. Use google and a good old fashioned  map and compass. 

Since this app has been released I have only seen a gross increase in traffic on the trail, making it almost impossible to find solitude and serenity in the wilderness. So I shame this app and all who use it should be weary
author: khleb2

title: Awesome App…perhaps one improvement
content: This is THE best app for hikers scouting nearby - or wherever, for that matter - trails to hike, bike or walk. Good detail, lots of good and helpful comments from other hikers/bikers, navigates to trail head (about 85% accurate in my experience) and will track your route along the trail. How could it be any better…?  It would be very helpful if there was info on access to trail head. Example: when my wife and I were hiking in Idaho, this app showed us lots of cool trails BUT quite a few of them were inaccessible unless you had an some off-road worthy vehicle. We did not, so we had to abandon those hiking plans after we got in the area and realized we could not get to the trail head.
author: noushapsidnbbz

title: Slow and Terrible UX
content: This app is super slow even on a new iphone 13 pro with a fast internet connection. The user experience design is really aggravating - mainly that when you're looking around the map and you zoom in to click on a trail marker in order to see a preview of a trail, the trail turns red - great - but you'll need to zoom out to see the whole trail... which automatically deselects the trail you've selected and shows you a different trail based on your new zoom level. It's beyond frustrating and completely idiotic. Especially for an app you pay some 40$ / year for. Who thought that behavior / interaction was a good idea? Its been this way for a long time and I can't believe this has passed through generations of updates and decision makers. PLEASE FIX. Thanks! :) I'll probably switch to another GPS app because I cant take it anymore.
author: Blee2003

title: Beginner camper/ hiker / traveler
content: Man oh man!!! I love the outdoors BUT I’m the type that goes into the woods and hopes to find something cool (usually do) but not without doing some serious off trailing type of hiking.   So I took to this app in hopes that I would find more appealing spots and wow am I impressed!    Basically made me want to travel around the country and currently on a trip to Portland to see a few hikes and camp sites!   Do not be fooled by lame 3 star reviews because they didn’t get their coffee this morning.... haters!   Honestly you won’t find a better app and!!! And and! (I don’t have pro) but if I did (I probably will) I would never think of complaint over $2! I’d pay that forever because people gots to eat y’all 🙏🏽 blessed and happy camping!
author: Ericke90

title: Two really annoying issues
content:
Love this app and like seeing where the developers are taking it. One problem I cannot escape is the custom maps downloads take a really long time, and your phone has to stay on (not locked). I don’t always have 15+ minutes to wait for these to download for offline use. If the phone locks or the app closes, the download starts over. I’ve had to resort to using other apps for these when on the go. 

The other issue is how long this app takes to open. I’m on an iPhone 7 and the app takes a minute or so to open. Really frustrating when you’re trying to make quick decisions on the move. Seems like a silly thing to complain about, but I’m using this app a few times a week. The inability to get to geolocated maps quickly has pushed me into other apps for this purpose.
author: Wrinkledpants

title: No I don’t want to share your video before I can download my own activity 🙄
content:
I’ve used AllTrails for years to keep track (pun intended) of my hikes and other activities and have downloaded every one’s route as a file for my own records. 

Now I note with a recent update that I can either live record and share this before presumably being able to download my own hike route, or if I don’t want to share a live recording then I can no longer download my route. What?!

It’s only an image of the route of my activity and yet now it seems to be stuck behind a paid subscription. Why can I no longer download this without oversharing publicly some partial 3D video?! This is massive overreach. 

I no longer want to share the photos and trail names and various other data points I’m sure AllTrails loved in my hundreds of previous activities. Maybe I’ll just take my data to another app that doesn’t force me to share these rubbish little videos. 

I suppose the point is to force me into a paid membership but I don’t want or need that. 

I’d love to hear from AllTrails that it’s just a glitch and I’ll be able to download my route as a simple file, or else I’ll have to move over to another app and delete my hundreds of photos from AllTrails. Do let me know!
author: DDDDDDDWWWWWWWWWW

title: Use almost daily - great with one persistent annoyance
content:
I use this app almost daily, as I take my dog out on hikes 5-7 times a week. For what I want, it works almost perfectly…
EXCEPT it forces you to rate the trail upon conclusion of an activity. To me, this is an extremely annoying and inefficient feature. And from what I can tell, it’s totally mandatory and there’s no way to disable it. I hate this feature. Your options are either to click through multiple pages and rate a trail for some stupid reason, or to ignore it and then have it block your screen with a rating reminder later when you try to use the app again

The only feature request I can think of for this app is to remove this useless rating feature.
author: Bumblebtna

title: Great but buggy
content: AT has the best community of hikers submitting trails and waypoints for sure, and when the app works it is awesome! However it is not bulletproof at all. Crashes occasionally on even a new iPhone and the watch app is pretty much unusable - crashes and unsyncs often, only way to resync is to restart the phone app and even then...(it seems to have something to do with the size of the AllTrails maps if you are not connected to Internet because it crashes when you try to load in a map - wish it could just be set to show stats. Map on phone current pace and stuff on watch). If the devs work out the bugs it will be a great if expensive subscription. Until then, recommend just browsing website for trails and using another GPS app for backcountry navigation when you are away from internet access.
author: growltiger23

title: Finger Rock trail(#42) to Mount Kimball
content: This is an all day ordeal that will require a 3 liter bladder for hydration. The 5 miles up is over 4000’ elevation gain. The distance & gain are similar to Mount Wrightson which is in Madera Canyon, an hour south. This hike allows a walk along Pusch Ridge to Pima Saddle. Hike back down thru Pima Canyon for over 12 miles. A car shuttle is needed to complete this loop. The loop took us 11 hours including lunch and picture taking. Start at sunrise to insure completion by sunset. Make sure to bring headlamps just in case. There are a few spots where you can take a wrong turn. Look for the cairns. At the Pima Saddle metal sign you can go up for great views. The path down heads West & is easy to miss due to a rock slab. The difficulty is similar to hiking Bright Angel trail to Indian Gardens & back the same day.
author: Nick Naming

title: For Every Hiker and Walker
content:
I use this app often, whether planning an outing in a particular area, or just being curious for another time. I have various saved trips for areas I will be in, or have been to, and it’s easy to look the trails over and decide which one looks good for a day.
I really like the ease of navigation, pertinent information, and the attractive full-feature layout of each trail. 
All Trails gets beginners and novices out, on to more trails with personal reviews and photos, and professional maps and data. Everything from parking suggestions to current trail conditions to distance and elevation gain help to make things easier from start to finish.
author: Ksargent1216

title: EDIT: no more crashing BUT…
content:
EDIT: app doesn’t seem to crash so maybe that has been fixed, BUT WHY DOES A FILTERED SEARCH NOT SAVE AFTER CLICKING INTO A TRAIL?? When doing a search and applying filters, it resets 99% of the time. You must open all filters and “re-apply” to narrow down hikes you’d be interested in. Updated to 3 stars for functionality while hiking, but when you live in an area with 100s of trails having to re-apply filters constantly is ANNOYING!!!! Still nothing done since prior review. 

App looks good, has a good purpose, but crashes and resets to main screen every time I’m search outside my location. Like 10 miles outside my location. Fix bugs and it might be worth it…
author: NewMHPInvestor12

title: Unsure on the gps distance but good app
content: This is solid! Being able to see the trail without old school maps is amazing. It does chew up the battery on the phone. You may want to bring a power bank to be safe. I am skeptical about the distance. I’ve run 3 gps at once. This is always .2-.3 longer on 5 or more miles. Now, phones are not as accurate as a whole, as they don’t seem to get the hairpin turns. I have seen people post garmin distances that match with what I’m saying. .2-.3 seems like nothing but that might be the distance from you to water or your legs surviving to the car. All in all, this is great for the local hikes. Get a solid watch for all the major details.
author: dg5753

title: Great for trail discovery and conditions
content: Love this app, it’s been so useful at discovering new trails, conditions, and keeping me on track. There aren’t really any downsides to it, but if it could be improved I wish there would be a way to indicate you are actively using it so the app wouldn’t have to constantly reload. I can’t tell you how many times I sit and stare at the splash screen waiting for the app to open when I never wanted to close it in the first place. With the most recent update the load times have improved a lot, but why does it have to reload while I’m still using it? The Gaia app, in comparison, doesn’t have to reload every time you open it. Gaia doesn't trail info however. That’s really my only complaint.
author: MickerMau5

title: App restarts every time
content:
I paid for pro so I could use the app as a map to keep me on track on a hike. Problem is, each time I look at the phone the app starts up with a long splash screen and then forgets where I was and just shows the favorites screen. So I select the trail, open the map, find my location each time from scratch! 

The company blames this on Apple and tells me to let the app record my track as I hike to help keep it active enough so that iOS doesn’t shut it down. Not a solution. And a terrible work around for backpacking trips where battery life is important. I simply want to check progress once and a while while I hike. But I spend most of my battery on waiting for the app to reload.

Plenty of apps with now background usage open back up to the last known state. This is a bug that should be addressed.
author: JPeterman210

title: Great App! More people need this!
content:
I’ve been using AllTrails for about 5 years now. I’ve lived in 3 different states while I’ve had this app and it never disappoints.
There are so many trails that it tells you about that you wouldn’t have known otherwise!
My only complaint (and maybe I just don’t know the app well enough)
Is that it some trails that say that it’s medium end up being very difficult and some that say that they’re easy end up being medium.
I understand that there is an elevation portion to the app, sometimes, I just wish that there was an option of the numbers turning red if it’s elevated enough where you wouldn’t typically feel comfortable hiking it.
author: ialwayscry

title: Great tool!!! Just don’t rely on it Alone
content:
I’ve been backpacking for about 35 years (except during my time in the military), so I grew up navigating with maps, compasses, and terrain reading. That said, I actually enjoy having a piece of outdoor tech like AllTrails in my kit. It’s great for discovering routes, finding trailheads, and helping keep you on the trail when things get confusing.

That said, it’s not perfect. I’ve noticed the mileage can be off. On a recent trip the valley I was hiking to was measured at about 8.1 miles, but when my Garmin and AllTrails both showed 8 miles, I still hadn’t even reached the saddle yet. This has happened more than once.

I also recently ran into a snow conditions issue. The trailhead was completely dry so I left my snowshoes in the car, but about 5–6 miles in I hit 2–3 feet of snow. That was fun! 

I like the app and use it regularly, but people should still carry a map and compass and know how to use them, especially for backpacking.

One feature I’d love to see added is the ability to add grids like UTM or MGRS overlay for better backcountry navigation.

Great tool—just not a replacement for experience and training.
author: Hunter sage jasmen

title: If it works, it’s great….but that is becoming more rare
content:
This is a great website and when the app works, it makes hiking great! Finding routes and reviews that make the outdoors enjoyable is lovely. Hence the 2 stars. 

But for the last year this app is slow, buggy and unreliable. Downloading maps for offline use is almost always unusable and switching tabs often leads to 45+ second delays or flat out crashing. Example is we went to Costa Rica and downloaded our maps prior in the USA after much patience. Once we arrived, the app was not usable in any mode (WiFi or airplane). We could not see any of our routes or use the app which is appalling if you pay extra for that feature, which we do. But even if you downloaded this for free, the app has become unreliable and unusable requiring a complete overhaul or a significant update.
author: Ethiokiddo77

title: Ups and Downs
content: I recently went Pro as I finally invested in an Apple Watch and was very disappointed with the functionality. The map is basically useless as it can’t be manipulated and the start/pause doesn’t work at all… I finally had to get my iPhone out of my pack and just use that. The new UI is also non-intuitive; you have to dig to get to the controls and having to figure out the “hold to stop” feature was really annoying. The other Pro feature I was excited about was the “off trail alert” …. Again, this does nothing in the Apple Watch so I hade no idea we were off our intended loop until I happened to unlock my phone. My whole reason for going Pro was so I didn’t have to keep my phone out, but I have no choice. Feeling very much like this was a bait and switch…
author: 911Fixer

title: Top tier app
content:
All trails is honestly one of the best designed apps out there. Very intuitive and very helpful for finding new trails. Works all over the world as I've used it in; the USA, Thailand, Malaysia, and Vietnam. Shows all trails around and gps helps keep you on the correct trail. Search filters make it easy to find the perfect trail and everything I've listed so far comes free. No purchases are necessary to effectively use the app but it looks like there might be some cool features. Honestly can't recommend this app enough.
Ps expect the trails to be a little longer than shown, though I actually enjoy this because it makes it easier to convince friends to go on longer hikes😏
author: did got hj

title: Good tra information but issues with battery draining
content:
Generally I love this app on my iphone. It helps me pick hiking trails and I love being able to download maps. The routes are always super accurate. The new trail preview feature is pretty cool. 

I do have an issue with trying to record hikes using the app. I tried a couple of times to use the tracking feature with my apple watch. It's cool that you can see a little map on your watch.  However, on long hikes my battery on both my watch and my iphone get totally drained. I don't know if there's a fix for this, but it was really frustrating to run out of power at the halfway point. Luckily my partner still had a functioning phone or I would have been very worried.
author: whatshupp

title: Just do it
content: So clutch!! Well worth the money if you’re into hiking/biking/trail running/ etc…This app tells you everything you need to know (length, difficulty, elevation gain, directions to the trailhead) about all of the trails in the area, wherever you are. You can also look at other peoples reviews, so you can get up-to-date info on the trail conditions. And always download the trail you’re going to do ahead of time for offline availability! Even when you have no service, you’re able to see exactly where you are on (or off) the trail. This app has saved me on poorly marked trails so many times, and I’ve discovered so many new hikes by browsing this app. 5/5.
author: Cross eyed crow

title: Took Us Waaay Out if the Way
content:
Went hiking into the Bisti Badlands of New Mexico. It was so cool to clearly see the red line marking the trail. Well, it was supposed to be the trail. 
We had just a short time frame for this hike & the red line lead us into a box canyon with the “easy” trail needing us to scramble over some 30 foot sandstone rocks. 
On close examination of the map, like really close we could see the little dotted line of the Bisti Trail, but we were no where close. The app eventually caught up to the trail after going way off the requested trail. 
We never had time to see what we wanted to see & it was not easy, so not impressed with this Pro feature so won’t be buying it. However we could see where we were & the Bisti Trail once we were back on it so that was helpful in finding our way back.
author: Photog60

title: Love this app it’s essential for trails!
content: I’ve been using this app now for a few months and man is it great! I’ve been doing trails solo and this app has saved me multiple times from getting off the trail and finding my way back! You are able to pull up the trail and pin point where you are and what direction your facing even! There’s also a feature called lifeline that will contact who you put in and update them on your location and how you’re doing once signal is available. Absolutely believe this app is a life saver and essential for going out on any trails. Really anywhere I travel this app finds nearby trails I would have no clue about. An amazing app and I highly recommend it for any outdoor activities.
author: Brawn07

title: The Map in My Pocket
content: I often do road trips and when I land in an unfamiliar area it’s sometimes difficult to find some good out-of-the-way places to find some solitude. All Trails took care of that. It provides a list of local trails that I can filter to find exactly what I’m looking for. The app will help guide me to the trailhead and after downloading the trail info, will keep me on the trail and show me my location on the trail. If I get off the trail, I get an “off route” alert which is very helpful in those areas where trails are not marked well. I believe that because of All Trails I’ve been to places known only to the locals and to places that even many of the locals don’t know about!
author: The Osprey's Talons

title: Great hiking app for your phone
content:
This app is fantastic for hitting the trails. Let’s you know right where you are so you never head off trail. Recording your route is great for going back and figuring out pacing based on what sort of terrain you were tackling. Not sure about the calorie counter as it was hundreds of calories off of my watch, but that’s not what you’re using this app for anyways. 

Would be 5-stars if the watch app also showed maps like some of the other apps out there. Instead it is basic record route and some analytics. Would be nice to have those maps on my watch so I don’t have to pull out the phone every time, when I just need a quick check of where I’m at.

Overall, a fantastic app worth every penny of the subscription for the pro elements.
author: Phil Cannel

title: Kind of insulting
content:
Update: Peak kind of just feels like a slap in the face. Heat maps are now locked behind a paywall. A feature that a lot of people probably didn’t use or know existed is being sold as a new feature. Still. I geo location of user photos in app. And creating routes, which is available for free on a browser or browser mode on your phone is now an extra feature for the app. 

I miss photo maps. If this was removed to protect delicate environments I get it though. I did use it to find campsites or see what conditions looked like on specific parts of a trail. 

For some reason I am accidentally pausing my activity mid hike. I am grateful for the updates to the UI to end a hike though. I wish I had to do one more swipe up maybe to get to the pause option. Some other way to make it a little harder to pause unintentionally.
author: Shawnnim

title: All Trails keeps me on the trails!
content:
Overall this a fantastic app.  I use it for ideas on local hikes and in the mountains!  I carry a map and compass for the mountains as a back up but primarily this is my go to.  A couple of concerns / questions which I find many other users are having.   
1) bring back the old record system.  It’s much easier especially when  most people drive a few hours to get to the trail or after a long hike and you don’t need the extra headache of thinking over the simple start and end recording. 
2) My Alltrails app will state I have hiked more miles than a regular map.   I know I will wander a few extra feet but not 2 extra miles.  Any clue why this is happening?   I have the phone in my pocket but that shouldn’t cause the difference. 
3). Lifeline needs more improvement on both ends.  The end user doesn’t know if you ended the hike because of no signal. Causes unnecessary concerns. 
4). Is there a way to fix it to start and end hikes without signal.  

Mostly please let me know why it adds more mileage !
Overall the app is fantastic!!

title: Nation wide hiker
content: I travel for work all over the US and downloading this app was one of the greatest things I’ve ever done. No matter where I go, I can always open the app and find an awesome new place to explore that I never would have found otherwise. The reviews are helpful and most trail difficulty ratings are pretty accurate. I don’t ever get lost because i can always compare the path I’ve taken with what’s on the map. That’s especially helpful when some trails aren’t always heavily marked. The only negative is how badly tracking my trail drains my battery, but that’s the nature of the beast with a constant GPS ping. I would highly recommend using the app the next time you are looking for a new place to explore!
author: Rainbow brite 28

title: UID getting less intuitive
content: While I love AllTrails, each update seems to make the user interface design less intuitive. Now when you open it, instead of a red button to just start if you don’t want to choose a set course, now it takes multiple clicks to get there. First, click on navigation. Behind “Where should we go?”/the possible trails, you have a tab marked “start without a route. Then you “choose your activity.” Only then you get a start button. There is nothing intuitive about navigating this navigation menu series — and now it takes 5 clicks to do what used to take one. I dread to see what they come up with next — and ho along it will take to figure out while standing at the trail head.
author: GLH123

title: Considering discontinuing my subscription
content:
Dislikes:
1. Can’t set a default activity type. Every time I save a trail  I have to remember to change the activity from hiking to off road. I am usually tired and want to head straight home after a ride and want save the trail quickly.
2. Too many acknowledgements when taking a photo. Should take you to the photo app immediately. Should not ask you if you want to take a photo after you select photo.
3. Way, way too slow at startup. I usually start it up and find something else too do when I open the app. 
4. Wish directions feature would provide an alternate trail starting point when available. Entering a trail at original starting point can add a ridiculous amount travel time getting to the trail.
5. Zooming function is slow, recenter function is inconsistent, and tracking current drive is inconsistent. Sometimes the app doesn’t follow my drive after I recenter. Sometimes recenter retains the last zoom setting and sometimes it doesn’t.

Likes:
1. Easy too use for planning trips 
2. Downloadable maps. A must for any app like this.
3. A good variety of downloadable maps.
4. I like being able to add waypoints in case I want to return to a trail in the future.
author: rivfam

title: Beautiful scenery
content: We were actually told about this place by a vehicle we were passing when driving to a waterfall we had on our list to view. The people told us “you’ve got to do this place” and maaan are we glad we did. The hike was very easy and we’re both in our early 60’s and had our 4.5 lb Yorkie that loooves walking trails with us. Be sure to look for cleared out turnoffs close to the end of the main trail. They lead you to beautiful bluffs and overlooks that really make this trail even more worth the trip. Next time we are in the Otto, NC area…we’ll definitely go again. It was very windy and a little overcast on the day we went, but again, very much worth it!!!
author: Norman's & Brodie

title: Good for very basics
content:
I’ve alwayss used this app, at least 10 years now! I decided to pull the trigger on the premium a few months back, which I hoped more from. Exploring trails around on the map view is very difficult, you can’t select any specific trail (you have to figure out where the entire route starts to be able to view), you can’t plan your own route of trails, they don’t have some common trails labeled/mapped, doesn’t don’t mention if they allow bikes/pets/ etc.

If you are using this app to find a free app for basic pre-mapped route with no specifics, this is definitely the best free version app you can get. I’ve been using for many years but as I become more experienced and the selection of this kind of app grows, this is no longer my first choice trail app. :(
author: breckel h

title: Great app, horrible connection problems
content:
I have been using this ad for a solid two weeks. I have gone on probably 15+ walks and runs using the tracking in the app to record my activity.

Consistently, the application seems to lose connection and fails to reconnect on its own to continue recording the activity. It pops up a notification message within the application, but does not send a notification to the phone. I can’t really understand why company would produce an application that is supposed to track activities that would be done in remote places, such as mountains and things like that, and have an application that fails to record the activity the moment that it experiences a hiccup in connection.

Complete waste of time using this application for the period that I did. I should’ve just kept using Strava.
author: RobLentz

title: Worst App
content: This is quite possibly the most infuriating app I have used in a long time. When I downloaded it years ago I thought it was my phone storage face that caused me issues but now I have significantly more storage space and I still run into regular problems. I downloaded a lot of off-line maps before traveling on vacation to Virginia where I plan to do several hikes. None of the maps ended up working could not get the application to function and this is an ongoing problem. I’m even subscribed as a pro customer and it has yet to have any impact on making it more user-friendly. I’m a tech person I understand how apps work and yet I cannot seem to get this to function well. I know it has a lot of great reviews but I won’t be using it again. I’m canceling my membership and deleting the app for good I’ve given it to many tries to continue hoping it will improve.
author: LaylaRae3

title: Amazing!!
content: If you travel and you know where you’re going to hike, this is the app for you. It’s worth the purchase. Download the maps before your hike and you’ll never be lost. I like being able to see what other people see on their hikes and determine if it’s worth going to. I like to drive to different cities throughout California and while I’m there I always look for hiking spots. This app is great and spot on. Even the places that are “hikable” but are now private property. I appreciate that little warning. It’s the little things that make this app what it is. Even if you don’t buy the yearly subscription just being able to look and read other hikers reviews make it worth having in my phone.
author: Yup_Morris

title: Would love a more detail rating system!
content: I love All Trails! A great hiking resource to have anywhere in North America. My one suggestion or even gripe is the rating system. How can I even compare the majestic hikes of Yosemite or Sequoia to my unremarkable, but still great, local trails in Southeastern PA? A 5 star scale seems like it doesn’t leave enough of a range to accurately account for the breadth, variety, and quality of the trails out there. It would be cool to have a 10 star scale, or better yet, ways that you can rate certain aspects of each trail (e.g. scenery on a scale of 1-5, trail upkeep/maintenance on a scale of 1-5, trail exposure on a scale of 1-5, etc!). That may allow for users to pick up on the regional nuances of each trail without needing to do a deep dive into the written reviews.
author: FeministForge

title: Have a request for accessing trail info
content:
Since I live in an area with limited online access, I often search for a trail the night before hiking. It would really help if a trail I had pulled up stayed on the active screen until the next morning. So often I get to a trail head, try to open the previously accessed trail and the app resets itself to the Home Screen. Then the best I can do is just select Navigate and lose access to a saved map. 
Great app for discovering and following trails, have even used app to help drive to remote trailhead. 
Really like ability to crop saved hikes, often forget to turn app off until am driving away
author: Jnlyn5

title: No iPad app still
content: I love AllTrails. Been using it for about a decade for everything from an afternoon walk in the park to week long backpacking expeditions. I often like to go my own route, and would use the web version to map my routes. I was ecstatic when I saw they had finally updated the app to support custom mapping/routing in app. I was caught a bit off guard when I realized you now needed to pay $80 vs $30 per year for this feature that had been on web for years, but I figured why not. Planning routes/trails on my phone isn’t ideal, but maybe I can use my iPad to do it now. Nope, $80 per year and no iPad support still. You still have to use the less than ideal web based platform on iPad. At $80 per year, I think you can add support for iPads so we can plan our routes on a large screen and follow it on our phones. Extremely disappointed iPad support is still not a thing.
author: johnyvvv14

title: Great app - good UX - missing a feature or two
content: I do a lot of hiking, rucking and running (trails and road). Most weeks, I clock 75+ miles. I also travel a lot for work. I’ve taken to using a combination of AllTrails and Strava to discover surprising routes (or maybe just surprising to a tourist) everywhere from the San Gabriel Mountains to the national parks on Kyushu to Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. It’s been great everywhere. My only grievance is that I wish there were a filter to identify trails that were amenable for folks with a fear of heights. There’s a number of people in my family who have full blown panics when confronted with sharp drops (most of which I wouldn’t even take note of) and I’d love to be able to sort for hikes that were only on valley floors, etc.
author: Doc Adam PDX

title: Decent for beginners, frustrating when functions feel forced
content:
I’ve used this app for several years. It can be a great way beginners to find hikes and gauge difficulty in terms of elevation gain and mileage.

I’m cancelling my subscription and moving to a different app because somewhere along the line (frankly I can’t remember when) this app started trying to force me to do things I don’t want to do.

My most frequent use of this app in the field is just to glance at it to make sure the blue gps dot is still on the red trail. I do not care to track my hike. To me it feels an unnecessary influx of data when I’d just like to spend time in nature more disconnected. But every time my screen locks, the app navigates away from the map I can freely use on my own to check my progress and reopens instead on the page that tries to get me to track my hike. Really quite annoying, especially in a scenario where I’d like to use tech as little as possible. A quick and easy glance has now turned into navigating through several screens each time my phone locks.

The second feature I highly dislike is the forced review system. At the conclusion of my hike, the app tries to bully me into leaving a review. I can’t navigate to the rest of the app until I either leave a review or force quit the app. If I am paying for this app, I should not be required to leave a review. 

These frustrations have been simmering for quite some time but AllTrails still seemed like the easiest option. Finally I was talking to a friend about it who recommended a free alternative. Just as high quality mapping, freely downloadable maps without a subscription, no forced reviewing. All the features you want to have in a tech-based map, none of the features you don’t need or want out there. I’d highly recommend googling for this free alternative.
author: Anonymous123456789876543212345

title: Great App For Finding Trails You Want and Don’t Want
content: This is a really great app for trail blazing and for some of us very useful for sizing up what you are getting yourself into before setting out to explore.  One glitch that I find annoying is the request after every recording to rate the trail.  While you can simply close that out, it is just annoying.  Other than day to day trail differences (wet vs. dry, etc.), if I have been there and rated it, asking for another rating...just not necessary.  If I wanted to change or update my rating of the same trail, I should be able to elect that option without being forced to answer that after saving every recording.  Otherwise a great app.  Maybe I am missing something but cannot get that feature to disappear.
author: Jawboner

title: Essential for any hiker — especially in Arizona and beyond!
content:
I absolutely love the AllTrails app! I primarily use it for exploring the beautiful trails of Arizona, from the Superstition Mountains to Sedona’s stunning red rock landscapes. The detailed maps, elevation profiles, and real-time GPS tracking make it incredibly easy to plan and navigate hikes, whether I’m tackling a challenging summit or looking for a casual scenic walk.

One of the best features is the ability to filter trails by difficulty, distance, and user ratings, which has helped me discover some hidden gems I wouldn’t have found otherwise. The offline maps have also been a lifesaver when hiking in remote areas with no cell service.

I’m also gearing up for a trip to Oregon, and AllTrails has already helped me map out some incredible hikes in places like Crater Lake and the Columbia River Gorge. Knowing I have a reliable app to guide me on unfamiliar trails gives me so much confidence.

If you love the outdoors, whether you're hiking, biking, or just looking for new places to explore, this app is a must-have. Highly recommend! 🌿🏔️🚶‍♂️
author: just hike

title: Auto-renew without any prior notification… shady
content:
Why doesn’t AllTrails send a reminder a few days or weeks in advance to let users know their subscription is about to auto-renew? That seems like a basic courtesy.
I wasn’t aware that my subscription was still active because it didn’t show up under my Apple subscriptions. Without any reminder or visibility in the app, there was no way for me to know I was still being charged. That feels really unfair.
When I finally realized and tried to cancel, it took multiple steps to even find the option, something I could only do on the website, not the app. Why make that so difficult?
I actually like the AllTrails app a lot, but this kind of practice feels shady and disappointing. A company that values its users shouldn’t rely on tactics like this to keep subscriptions going
author: Rent in Hermosa

title: Please fix the “finish” button
content:
I don’t know where else to put this but can you PLEASE change the “finish” button to a type where you have to hold it to finish a trail.  It should operate like the pause button does.  I’ve lost two tracks this week alone because I’ve accidentally tapped finish instead of resume when on a trail.  Either make it a push/hold type button or enable a back button after it’s pressed because it pops up the trail review stuff and I’m not ready for that.  Let me go back to the previous screen or make finish button like I said.

Other than that, the app is great and the pro features are fantastic!
author: mynicknameisnotyournickname

title: App works again and I’m a happy hiker
content: I’ve used this app for years and it has helped me discover my love for the outdoors. I left a one star review after I was impacted by the problem other recent 1 star reviews mention,  App crashes leaving it nearly unusable. That wasn’t fair to the developers. That was the only problem it’s had in my years of using it.  After uninstalling and reinstalling the app it worked solid again. This app does deserve 5 stars. It’s probably the most useful tool the average hiker can have. I venture into the wilderness off trail quite a bit and this ensures I can always find my way back to the start point. Thanks developers 🤙🏼🤙🏼
author: Clnbuds

title: Fantastic Maps and App!
content:
AllTrails is awesome! The customized “AllTrails” maps are perfect for what I need. They combine street info with most topo and trail info so you can research and find trailheads much easier than before. The ability to trace the elevation profile of a hike trail is very nice. I also found the recorder only uses a small amount of battery on my iPhone. After a 4 hour hike 75% of my battery remained. 

You need to be a Pro subscriber to use the maps offline but that is more than reasonable given this app’s functionality. Be sure to check downloaded maps in offline mode by going into airplane mode before you leave. 

Highly recommended!
author: rdevillers

title: Great app, sadly lost features
content: I’ve used this app many times to navigate local trails and get details as to how to get to the trails. It also connects to my Garmin data so I can see my stats even if I didn’t use my phone to track the trail. The only reason it is missing a star is because I’ve had a paid membership for three years now. Sometime recently they added their “peak” membership and it took away some of the features I previously had, which was the ability to view hourly weather throughout the day on the trail. I used the feature a lot because I hike with my dogs and in the summer it’s difficult to know if the trails will be cool enough if I’m driving up to the mountain trails.
author: tonyav16

title: Used to be good, now it’s being overly monetized
content: This app used to be good. Now its features are being gradually replaced with forced ads, overt and intrusive attempts to upgrade users to the premium subscription, and features are removed from free to then be moved to premium only. It’s getting to the point where it’s not worth using because you can get the same features plus more on other applications. If you force me to get your premium to preserve features, you need to offer equal or better options than the competition. OnX is a similar price subscription and offers far more like topo maps and route planning. Its clear they’re pushing for paid users so much because they’re losing subscribers, but the reason they’re losing subscribers is BECAUSE the premium is sub par. Innovate or die, it’s way of the market.
author: unhapppy_user

title: From hero to zero
content: I used to love all trails, until I updated it... let me tell you why. Where I live all the trails are remote in the mountains where cell phone service is extremely limited. Before this month I used to be able to pull up all trails with no cell service and be able to pull up maps and see where I was. Majority of the trails I hike are bushwhacks so it makes it super easy to find where I am on the map when I could use this app in conjunction with a map and compass. But sadly now I cannot. I even looked into buying a subscription again but read in recent reviews that still doesn’t work. 😩please fix this problem!!
author: ballsucker

title: Navigate feature bug
content:
I like their new update, however there is a bug that needs fixed: it lets you select your activity when you record it through “navigate” (great update!) but when you’re done recording, the activity always defaults to hiking so you have to manually edit the activity if you were not hiking (annoying). Please fix and thank you for continually improving the app. 

Also, I live in Seattle, a major city filled with tech savvy nerds, yet the routes around here listed on All Trails are filled with outdated, closed, and random listings. Who is vetting and updating your routes? This app would be so much better if I didn’t have to do quite so much of my own digging and vetting for the good stuff. Especially since I pay for the pro membership.
author: Lisa_bo_bisa

title: Great idea. Poor execution.
content: Some major flaws of this app. It requires cellular or WiFi connection. Most hikes I have done do not have cell coverage. Another major flaw, when following directions on how to get to a hike, after arrival it completely dismisses the hike you are planning to do. You need to open the app again and look for your hike again. Another flaw, while recording, if you stop to take pictures or for whatever reason, it stops recording!!! This has happened to me many times and it happened again at today’s hike. Lost my trail. I had to open the app again and look where I was on the trail layers. It was as if you were dropped in a trail 3/4 of the way, but had no recollection of what you have already done. I’m AllTrails Pro subscriber. Deeply regretted.
author: love_okay

title: Improvement thoughts
content:
The app is great for the most part... Here are some thoughts that may or may not make it better.

1-Filtering options, I would like to see better filtering options, i.e. filter by miles/distance, filter by star reviews, filter by easy - hard when looking at the “list” screen...etc

2-Higher miles on the filters. Currently it tops out at 20 miles trails. If I’m looking for something that is 30, 40, 50+ miles I have to click on every trail to find a longer trail.

3-Campsite/RV park location(s) at the trail head or close to it. If I’m traveling out of state for a backpacking trip, it would be nice to know where sites are located at. Makes planning the trip easier.

4-Wish users of the app would add in more “water” information. I plan long trips around creeks, streams, lakes, and rivers so I don’t have to carry as much water with me. Knowing which trail has water and how far down the trail it is, is a deciding factor for choosing the trail.

Just my thoughts...other then that the app is pretty user friendly, works well (until I lose signal), and makes planning a bit easier.
author: Gastankii

title: Love this app!
content: A must have for the back woods explorer or trail seeker. Fantastic App! shows all trails nearby, less traveled trails, remote or the nice parks. Map feature is fantastic and one click link to your navigation to the trail head is really nice! This app is spot on and even works good in spotty service.. I haven’t had to do the offline yet but what a great feature. Use the navigate and save your hike run walk.. useful info to show route, time, elevation, calories burned, your stats and workouts, pause feature for the runners trying to keep min/miles .. Fun app! And a Very useful tool to navigate trail systems. Shows pretty much all of the side trails also. Two Thumbs up!
author: Cptaln

title: Maps not correct or just not updated.
content: Most hikes you research and want to do isn’t on this app. I only use this app to track my mileage. I use Google Maps to track everything else. Yes, google maps even with no service works better than this app. Early on I knew not to trust this app and luckily I stayed out of dangerous scenarios. DO NOT trust this app. Also, app randomly stops working sometimes and the elevation gain resets when it wants as well. I bought a membership right away too so it’s not just a free app malfunction. Please be aware and don’t trust your life with this app. Have other outlets or just know what you’re doing and where you are going.
author: Ben Sergent

title: A Must Have
content: All Trails is an absolute must have tool for adventurists and outdoor enthusiasts. Whenever we travel, I am always on all trails before we go and saving my favorite trails to a list. I also love that I can sort by so many different filters and discover dog friendly trails (and ones that aren’t so we know to leave him home) The GPS to take you the the beginning of the trail head is amazing as Apple Maps has taken us way off base before. I love this app and I highly recommend if you love hiking or trail walking, bike riding or just scenic views. There are plenty of lookout points in the app for those who can’t hike or bike or for those uncooperative weather days!
author: TxGirl92

title: Search UI confuses me
content: I’ve used the app extensively over the last two weeks on a road trip to Acadia national park. The app was great for all the hikes we did. Two things that confused/irritated me: when I searched for hikes and used filters, how to properly navigate between the details of a hike and back to the search results isn’t obvious, so many times I thought by closing the details I’d get back to the results of my filtered search but was instead greeted by the full unfiltered map. Second, when you start a loop not where AllTrails decides the trail head is, but at a different starting point (say, parking lot), then it doesn’t properly account for that when reporting how many miles you have left.
author: justvivid

title: 2 decade long road running falls in love with trails
content:
This app is great. I have been running competitive/ consistently since 2005. Love running from 5ks up to marathon and last few years I have become head over heals for ultras and crazy races. However outside of races I would almost always train on roads. I discovered some awesome trails near my new home and brought be back to high school cross county days. This app allows me to
See Trail options I would have never been aware of even ones I have driven by for over a year. I once had a goal of running every road in my town. Now through this app my new goals is to Run every trail in the local trail systems.
author: Youth pastor Chris

title: do not recommend
content:
I do not recommend this app and am cancelling my Pro subscription. After having used it heavily for a week in the mountains, it is just frustrating. A couple of the features I wanted most and paid for in Pro-- like printing maps -- are only available on your desk top. (There's no cell service where we are, so its critical) And you have to go through several convoluted steps to get a picture of what the trail is like and where it is and how to get to the trailhead. 

The reviews are helpful, but the description on the app is weak: Poor or nonexistent directions (except to export to Google maps which is insufficient) poor general descriptions of the trail. We are in a popular hiking area, so there is no reason for weak information. Frankly the guidebooks from the Tourist Info booth were consistently much better. 

Back to paper guide books and old school topo maps until I can find a better app.
author: Walkersrq

title: AI Overview
content:
A truly great app for years. I’ve used it and loved it for hiking and backpacking all around California. However, they are now introducing ai overviews for the trails and I don’t think I can trust them. I can’t trust that the information I get from AllTrails is safe or reliable if a very dumb and useless computer is trying to give me that information. I am definitely canceling my paid subscription specifically because of this.

Update: AllTrails responded saying that I should contact them if I find any incorrect information. I will not be relying on them for information in the first place, so I can’t do that. Getting incorrect information can ruin a day, a longer backpacking trip, or can even lead users into dangerous situations. I hope that AllTrails will do the decent thing and get rid of the untrustworthy and useless ai integration.
author: duecewain

title: I love at least the idea of this app.
content:
AllTrails tries to do everything I want it to do. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always succeed. For example, it’s sort of a mess to use on my first gen Apple Watch Ultra. My watch is constantly getting disconnected from my phone, but only for AllTrails. And then when the trail is finished, my watch never gets the memo. Every single time, I have to restart my watch to get all trails to quit running in the background. Frustrating.

It does work very well on my iPhone, though. I haven’t decided if I will renew my AllTrails+ subscription. I love being able to download maps before a trip. But the watch thing is annoying. Precise GPS tracking was my primary motivation for purchasing the Ultra. Wish AllTrails worked better with it.
author: Kevanjt

title: Latest app updates make it almost unusable
content:
First - they moved the completed and activities tabs to your profile, ok, nbd but by doing so they also removed the search function. One thing I liked to do was compare how I did to previous time, or find trails I’ve done before where I didn’t do the map as it is listed but that’s what I want to repeat. I’m not going to scroll hundreds of activities to find it.

Second - the elevation calculation is nonsense until you complete the trail, it use to calculate it. I liked knowing what I’ve done for those really long trails were I’m trying to only complete part of it. So now I have to rough calculate it based on the map - super useful for trails that have rolling hills or whatnot. 

Whatever “minor bugs” that were fixed seemed to be more acceptable than the changes they pushed.
author: JammyPandy

title: Attention outdoor enthusiasts!
content: I love this app! I’ve always been a hiker and know my trails in the mountains (I live in NH), but I’ve discovered so many different paths that I didn’t know existed around my area! I really love the map feature as it allows you to zoom into your specific area to see trails or expand your search by zooming out. AND you can record your walk!? I just discovered this feature lol I guess I wasn’t using the app to its full potential! That’s when I decided to write a review. It’s nice to have a free app that does it all. I obviously recommend this to people with all skill levels of adventuring. I’m off to find a new trail today with my pups!          :D
author: MaineResident420maang

title: Horribly slow and super annoying startup
content: I’ve been using this app for awhile now and like its feature set and they provide frequent and useful feature updates. My only complaint is that every single time you start the app it initializes your trail data, which can be very frustrating. Particularly if you had the app closed to save battery life and need to make some quick routing decisions. I’m baffled as to why the process is so inordinately slow because there are numerous technical strategies that can be employed to short circuit the process and quickly determine whether an initialization/sync is in order. How about letting the user decide if they want to initialize/sync at that time instead of making them wait, sometimes minutes? (Question: If the mobile app is used on one device with only an occasional visit to the web app - what exactly needs to be initialized/synced every single time?)
author: trendpundit

title: Great trails, needs watch app
content:
I have to say, I’ve bought the subscription for pro features and I don’t regret it. They’ve made an excellent platform for a huge number of trails. Really well done. 

But the app itself on the iPhone is ok. As far as I know there’s no way to JUST see the map , with your location and direction. They have this’s small map, but the screen has several other items on that distract the eye. It would be great to just have the trail and your location on a whole dedicated screen. 

The other point is this app NEEDS a better Apple Watch app. I’d really rather glance at my wrist to look at the trail and my location. That way I could just leave my phone in my backpack, or even at home. You already have a ui for the map, trail, and location, it just needs to be on the watch now.
author: FernandoTTA

title: Great App! More people need this!
content:
I’ve been using AllTrails for about 5 years now. I’ve lived in 3 different states while I’ve had this app and it never disappoints.
There are so many trails that it tells you about that you wouldn’t have known otherwise!
My only complaint (and maybe I just don’t know the app well enough)
Is that it some trails that say that it’s medium end up being very difficult and some that say that they’re easy end up being medium.
I understand that there is an elevation portion to the app, sometimes, I just wish that there was an option of the numbers turning red if it’s elevated enough where you wouldn’t typically feel comfortable hiking it.
author: ialwayscry

title: Great tool!!! Just don’t rely on it Alone
content:
I’ve been backpacking for about 35 years (except during my time in the military), so I grew up navigating with maps, compasses, and terrain reading. That said, I actually enjoy having a piece of outdoor tech like AllTrails in my kit. It’s great for discovering routes, finding trailheads, and helping keep you on the trail when things get confusing.

That said, it’s not perfect. I’ve noticed the mileage can be off. On a recent trip the valley I was hiking to was measured at about 8.1 miles, but when my Garmin and AllTrails both showed 8 miles, I still hadn’t even reached the saddle yet. This has happened more than once.

I also recently ran into a snow conditions issue. The trailhead was completely dry so I left my snowshoes in the car, but about 5–6 miles in I hit 2–3 feet of snow. That was fun! 

I like the app and use it regularly, but people should still carry a map and compass and know how to use them, especially for backpacking.

One feature I’d love to see added is the ability to add grids like UTM or MGRS overlay for better backcountry navigation.

Great tool—just not a replacement for experience and training.
author: Hunter sage jasmen

title: If it works, it’s great….but that is becoming more rare
content:
This is a great website and when the app works, it makes hiking great! Finding routes and reviews that make the outdoors enjoyable is lovely. Hence the 2 stars. 

But for the last year this app is slow, buggy and unreliable. Downloading maps for offline use is almost always unusable and switching tabs often leads to 45+ second delays or flat out crashing. Example is we went to Costa Rica and downloaded our maps prior in the USA after much patience. Once we arrived, the app was not usable in any mode (WiFi or airplane). We could not see any of our routes or use the app which is appalling if you pay extra for that feature, which we do. But even if you downloaded this for free, the app has become unreliable and unusable requiring a complete overhaul or a significant update.
author: Ethiokiddo77

title: Ups and Downs
content: I recently went Pro as I finally invested in an Apple Watch and was very disappointed with the functionality. The map is basically useless as it can’t be manipulated and the start/pause doesn’t work at all… I finally had to get my iPhone out of my pack and just use that. The new UI is also non-intuitive; you have to dig to get to the controls and having to figure out the “hold to stop” feature was really annoying. The other Pro feature I was excited about was the “off trail alert” …. Again, this does nothing in the Apple Watch so I hade no idea we were off our intended loop until I happened to unlock my phone. My whole reason for going Pro was so I didn’t have to keep my phone out, but I have no choice. Feeling very much like this was a bait and switch…
author: 911Fixer

title: Top tier app
content:
All trails is honestly one of the best designed apps out there. Very intuitive and very helpful for finding new trails. Works all over the world as I've used it in; the USA, Thailand, Malaysia, and Vietnam. Shows all trails around and gps helps keep you on the correct trail. Search filters make it easy to find the perfect trail and everything I've listed so far comes free. No purchases are necessary to effectively use the app but it looks like there might be some cool features. Honestly can't recommend this app enough.
Ps expect the trails to be a little longer than shown, though I actually enjoy this because it makes it easier to convince friends to go on longer hikes😏
author: did got hj

title: Good tra information but issues with battery draining
content:
Generally I love this app on my iphone. It helps me pick hiking trails and I love being able to download maps. The routes are always super accurate. The new trail preview feature is pretty cool. 

I do have an issue with trying to record hikes using the app. I tried a couple of times to use the tracking feature with my apple watch. It's cool that you can see a little map on your watch.  However, on long hikes my battery on both my watch and my iphone get totally drained. I don't know if there's a fix for this, but it was really frustrating to run out of power at the halfway point. Luckily my partner still had a functioning phone or I would have been very worried.
author: whatshupp

title: Just do it
content: So clutch!! Well worth the money if you’re into hiking/biking/trail running/ etc…This app tells you everything you need to know (length, difficulty, elevation gain, directions to the trailhead) about all of the trails in the area, wherever you are. You can also look at other peoples reviews, so you can get up-to-date info on the trail conditions. And always download the trail you’re going to do ahead of time for offline availability! Even when you have no service, you’re able to see exactly where you are on (or off) the trail. This app has saved me on poorly marked trails so many times, and I’ve discovered so many new hikes by browsing this app. 5/5.
author: Cross eyed crow

title: Took Us Waaay Out if the Way
content:
Went hiking into the Bisti Badlands of New Mexico. It was so cool to clearly see the red line marking the trail. Well, it was supposed to be the trail. 
We had just a short time frame for this hike & the red line lead us into a box canyon with the “easy” trail needing us to scramble over some 30 foot sandstone rocks. 
On close examination of the map, like really close we could see the little dotted line of the Bisti Trail, but we were no where close. The app eventually caught up to the trail after going way off the requested trail. 
We never had time to see what we wanted to see & it was not easy, so not impressed with this Pro feature so won’t be buying it. However we could see where we were & the Bisti Trail once we were back on it so that was helpful in finding our way back.
author: Photog60

title: Love this app it’s essential for trails!
content: I’ve been using this app now for a few months and man is it great! I’ve been doing trails solo and this app has saved me multiple times from getting off the trail and finding my way back! You are able to pull up the trail and pin point where you are and what direction your facing even! There’s also a feature called lifeline that will contact who you put in and update them on your location and how you’re doing once signal is available. Absolutely believe this app is a life saver and essential for going out on any trails. Really anywhere I travel this app finds nearby trails I would have no clue about. An amazing app and I highly recommend it for any outdoor activities.
author: Brawn07

title: The Map in My Pocket
content: I often do road trips and when I land in an unfamiliar area it’s sometimes difficult to find some good out-of-the-way places to find some solitude. All Trails took care of that. It provides a list of local trails that I can filter to find exactly what I’m looking for. The app will help guide me to the trailhead and after downloading the trail info, will keep me on the trail and show me my location on the trail. If I get off the trail, I get an “off route” alert which is very helpful in those areas where trails are not marked well. I believe that because of All Trails I’ve been to places known only to the locals and to places that even many of the locals don’t know about!
author: The Osprey's Talons

title: Great hiking app for your phone
content:
This app is fantastic for hitting the trails. Let’s you know right where you are so you never head off trail. Recording your route is great for going back and figuring out pacing based on what sort of terrain you were tackling. Not sure about the calorie counter as it was hundreds of calories off of my watch, but that’s not what you’re using this app for anyways. 

Would be 5-stars if the watch app also showed maps like some of the other apps out there. Instead it is basic record route and some analytics. Would be nice to have those maps on my watch so I don’t have to pull out the phone every time, when I just need a quick check of where I’m at.

Overall, a fantastic app worth every penny of the subscription for the pro elements.
author: Phil Cannel

title: Kind of insulting
content:
Update: Peak kind of just feels like a slap in the face. Heat maps are now locked behind a paywall. A feature that a lot of people probably didn’t use or know existed is being sold as a new feature. Still. I geo location of user photos in app. And creating routes, which is available for free on a browser or browser mode on your phone is now an extra feature for the app. 

I miss photo maps. If this was removed to protect delicate environments I get it though. I did use it to find campsites or see what conditions looked like on specific parts of a trail. 

For some reason I am accidentally pausing my activity mid hike. I am grateful for the updates to the UI to end a hike though. I wish I had to do one more swipe up maybe to get to the pause option. Some other way to make it a little harder to pause unintentionally.
author: Shawnnim

title: All Trails keeps me on the trails!
content:
Overall this a fantastic app.  I use it for ideas on local hikes and in the mountains!  I carry a map and compass for the mountains as a back up but primarily this is my go to.  A couple of concerns / questions which I find many other users are having.   
1) bring back the old record system.  It’s much easier especially when  most people drive a few hours to get to the trail or after a long hike and you don’t need the extra headache of thinking over the simple start and end recording. 
2) My Alltrails app will state I have hiked more miles than a regular map.   I know I will wander a few extra feet but not 2 extra miles.  Any clue why this is happening?   I have the phone in my pocket but that shouldn’t cause the difference. 
3). Lifeline needs more improvement on both ends.  The end user doesn’t know if you ended the hike because of no signal. Causes unnecessary concerns. 
4). Is there a way to fix it to start and end hikes without signal.  

Mostly please let me know why it adds more mileage !
Overall the app is fantastic!!

title: Nation wide hiker
content: I travel for work all over the US and downloading this app was one of the greatest things I’ve ever done. No matter where I go, I can always open the app and find an awesome new place to explore that I never would have found otherwise. The reviews are helpful and most trail difficulty ratings are pretty accurate. I don’t ever get lost because i can always compare the path I’ve taken with what’s on the map. That’s especially helpful when some trails aren’t always heavily marked. The only negative is how badly tracking my trail drains my battery, but that’s the nature of the beast with a constant GPS ping. I would highly recommend using the app the next time you are looking for a new place to explore!
author: Rainbow brite 28

title: UID getting less intuitive
content: While I love AllTrails, each update seems to make the user interface design less intuitive. Now when you open it, instead of a red button to just start if you don’t want to choose a set course, now it takes multiple clicks to get there. First, click on navigation. Behind “Where should we go?”/the possible trails, you have a tab marked “start without a route. Then you “choose your activity.” Only then you get a start button. There is nothing intuitive about navigating this navigation menu series — and now it takes 5 clicks to do what used to take one. I dread to see what they come up with next — and ho along it will take to figure out while standing at the trail head.
author: GLH123

title: Considering discontinuing my subscription
content:
Dislikes:
1. Can’t set a default activity type. Every time I save a trail  I have to remember to change the activity from hiking to off road. I am usually tired and want to head straight home after a ride and want save the trail quickly.
2. Too many acknowledgements when taking a photo. Should take you to the photo app immediately. Should not ask you if you want to take a photo after you select photo.
3. Way, way too slow at startup. I usually start it up and find something else too do when I open the app. 
4. Wish directions feature would provide an alternate trail starting point when available. Entering a trail at original starting point can add a ridiculous amount travel time getting to the trail.
5. Zooming function is slow, recenter function is inconsistent, and tracking current drive is inconsistent. Sometimes the app doesn’t follow my drive after I recenter. Sometimes recenter retains the last zoom setting and sometimes it doesn’t.

Likes:
1. Easy too use for planning trips 
2. Downloadable maps. A must for any app like this.
3. A good variety of downloadable maps.
4. I like being able to add waypoints in case I want to return to a trail in the future.
author: rivfam

title: Beautiful scenery
content: We were actually told about this place by a vehicle we were passing when driving to a waterfall we had on our list to view. The people told us “you’ve got to do this place” and maaan are we glad we did. The hike was very easy and we’re both in our early 60’s and had our 4.5 lb Yorkie that loooves walking trails with us. Be sure to look for cleared out turnoffs close to the end of the main trail. They lead you to beautiful bluffs and overlooks that really make this trail even more worth the trip. Next time we are in the Otto, NC area…we’ll definitely go again. It was very windy and a little overcast on the day we went, but again, very much worth it!!!
author: Norman's & Brodie

title: Good for very basics
content:
