I’ve alwayss used this app, at least 10 years now! I decided to pull the trigger on the premium a few months back, which I hoped more from. Exploring trails around on the map view is very difficult, you can’t select any specific trail (you have to figure out where the entire route starts to be able to view), you can’t plan your own route of trails, they don’t have some common trails labeled/mapped, doesn’t don’t mention if they allow bikes/pets/ etc.

If you are using this app to find a free app for basic pre-mapped route with no specifics, this is definitely the best free version app you can get. I’ve been using for many years but as I become more experienced and the selection of this kind of app grows, this is no longer my first choice trail app. :(
author: breckel h

title: Great app, horrible connection problems
content:
I have been using this ad for a solid two weeks. I have gone on probably 15+ walks and runs using the tracking in the app to record my activity.

Consistently, the application seems to lose connection and fails to reconnect on its own to continue recording the activity. It pops up a notification message within the application, but does not send a notification to the phone. I can’t really understand why company would produce an application that is supposed to track activities that would be done in remote places, such as mountains and things like that, and have an application that fails to record the activity the moment that it experiences a hiccup in connection.

Complete waste of time using this application for the period that I did. I should’ve just kept using Strava.
author: RobLentz

title: Worst App
content: This is quite possibly the most infuriating app I have used in a long time. When I downloaded it years ago I thought it was my phone storage face that caused me issues but now I have significantly more storage space and I still run into regular problems. I downloaded a lot of off-line maps before traveling on vacation to Virginia where I plan to do several hikes. None of the maps ended up working could not get the application to function and this is an ongoing problem. I’m even subscribed as a pro customer and it has yet to have any impact on making it more user-friendly. I’m a tech person I understand how apps work and yet I cannot seem to get this to function well. I know it has a lot of great reviews but I won’t be using it again. I’m canceling my membership and deleting the app for good I’ve given it to many tries to continue hoping it will improve.
author: LaylaRae3

title: Amazing!!
content: If you travel and you know where you’re going to hike, this is the app for you. It’s worth the purchase. Download the maps before your hike and you’ll never be lost. I like being able to see what other people see on their hikes and determine if it’s worth going to. I like to drive to different cities throughout California and while I’m there I always look for hiking spots. This app is great and spot on. Even the places that are “hikable” but are now private property. I appreciate that little warning. It’s the little things that make this app what it is. Even if you don’t buy the yearly subscription just being able to look and read other hikers reviews make it worth having in my phone.
author: Yup_Morris

title: Would love a more detail rating system!
content: I love All Trails! A great hiking resource to have anywhere in North America. My one suggestion or even gripe is the rating system. How can I even compare the majestic hikes of Yosemite or Sequoia to my unremarkable, but still great, local trails in Southeastern PA? A 5 star scale seems like it doesn’t leave enough of a range to accurately account for the breadth, variety, and quality of the trails out there. It would be cool to have a 10 star scale, or better yet, ways that you can rate certain aspects of each trail (e.g. scenery on a scale of 1-5, trail upkeep/maintenance on a scale of 1-5, trail exposure on a scale of 1-5, etc!). That may allow for users to pick up on the regional nuances of each trail without needing to do a deep dive into the written reviews.
author: FeministForge

title: Have a request for accessing trail info
content:
Since I live in an area with limited online access, I often search for a trail the night before hiking. It would really help if a trail I had pulled up stayed on the active screen until the next morning. So often I get to a trail head, try to open the previously accessed trail and the app resets itself to the Home Screen. Then the best I can do is just select Navigate and lose access to a saved map. 
Great app for discovering and following trails, have even used app to help drive to remote trailhead. 
Really like ability to crop saved hikes, often forget to turn app off until am driving away
author: Jnlyn5

title: No iPad app still
content: I love AllTrails. Been using it for about a decade for everything from an afternoon walk in the park to week long backpacking expeditions. I often like to go my own route, and would use the web version to map my routes. I was ecstatic when I saw they had finally updated the app to support custom mapping/routing in app. I was caught a bit off guard when I realized you now needed to pay $80 vs $30 per year for this feature that had been on web for years, but I figured why not. Planning routes/trails on my phone isn’t ideal, but maybe I can use my iPad to do it now. Nope, $80 per year and no iPad support still. You still have to use the less than ideal web based platform on iPad. At $80 per year, I think you can add support for iPads so we can plan our routes on a large screen and follow it on our phones. Extremely disappointed iPad support is still not a thing.
author: johnyvvv14

title: Great app - good UX - missing a feature or two
content: I do a lot of hiking, rucking and running (trails and road). Most weeks, I clock 75+ miles. I also travel a lot for work. I’ve taken to using a combination of AllTrails and Strava to discover surprising routes (or maybe just surprising to a tourist) everywhere from the San Gabriel Mountains to the national parks on Kyushu to Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. It’s been great everywhere. My only grievance is that I wish there were a filter to identify trails that were amenable for folks with a fear of heights. There’s a number of people in my family who have full blown panics when confronted with sharp drops (most of which I wouldn’t even take note of) and I’d love to be able to sort for hikes that were only on valley floors, etc.
author: Doc Adam PDX

title: Decent for beginners, frustrating when functions feel forced
content:
I’ve used this app for several years. It can be a great way beginners to find hikes and gauge difficulty in terms of elevation gain and mileage.

I’m cancelling my subscription and moving to a different app because somewhere along the line (frankly I can’t remember when) this app started trying to force me to do things I don’t want to do.

My most frequent use of this app in the field is just to glance at it to make sure the blue gps dot is still on the red trail. I do not care to track my hike. To me it feels an unnecessary influx of data when I’d just like to spend time in nature more disconnected. But every time my screen locks, the app navigates away from the map I can freely use on my own to check my progress and reopens instead on the page that tries to get me to track my hike. Really quite annoying, especially in a scenario where I’d like to use tech as little as possible. A quick and easy glance has now turned into navigating through several screens each time my phone locks.

The second feature I highly dislike is the forced review system. At the conclusion of my hike, the app tries to bully me into leaving a review. I can’t navigate to the rest of the app until I either leave a review or force quit the app. If I am paying for this app, I should not be required to leave a review. 

These frustrations have been simmering for quite some time but AllTrails still seemed like the easiest option. Finally I was talking to a friend about it who recommended a free alternative. Just as high quality mapping, freely downloadable maps without a subscription, no forced reviewing. All the features you want to have in a tech-based map, none of the features you don’t need or want out there. I’d highly recommend googling for this free alternative.
author: Anonymous123456789876543212345

title: Great App For Finding Trails You Want and Don’t Want
content: This is a really great app for trail blazing and for some of us very useful for sizing up what you are getting yourself into before setting out to explore.  One glitch that I find annoying is the request after every recording to rate the trail.  While you can simply close that out, it is just annoying.  Other than day to day trail differences (wet vs. dry, etc.), if I have been there and rated it, asking for another rating...just not necessary.  If I wanted to change or update my rating of the same trail, I should be able to elect that option without being forced to answer that after saving every recording.  Otherwise a great app.  Maybe I am missing something but cannot get that feature to disappear.
author: Jawboner

title: Essential for any hiker — especially in Arizona and beyond!
content:
I absolutely love the AllTrails app! I primarily use it for exploring the beautiful trails of Arizona, from the Superstition Mountains to Sedona’s stunning red rock landscapes. The detailed maps, elevation profiles, and real-time GPS tracking make it incredibly easy to plan and navigate hikes, whether I’m tackling a challenging summit or looking for a casual scenic walk.

One of the best features is the ability to filter trails by difficulty, distance, and user ratings, which has helped me discover some hidden gems I wouldn’t have found otherwise. The offline maps have also been a lifesaver when hiking in remote areas with no cell service.

I’m also gearing up for a trip to Oregon, and AllTrails has already helped me map out some incredible hikes in places like Crater Lake and the Columbia River Gorge. Knowing I have a reliable app to guide me on unfamiliar trails gives me so much confidence.

If you love the outdoors, whether you're hiking, biking, or just looking for new places to explore, this app is a must-have. Highly recommend! 🌿🏔️🚶‍♂️
author: just hike

title: Auto-renew without any prior notification… shady
content:
Why doesn’t AllTrails send a reminder a few days or weeks in advance to let users know their subscription is about to auto-renew? That seems like a basic courtesy.
I wasn’t aware that my subscription was still active because it didn’t show up under my Apple subscriptions. Without any reminder or visibility in the app, there was no way for me to know I was still being charged. That feels really unfair.
When I finally realized and tried to cancel, it took multiple steps to even find the option, something I could only do on the website, not the app. Why make that so difficult?
I actually like the AllTrails app a lot, but this kind of practice feels shady and disappointing. A company that values its users shouldn’t rely on tactics like this to keep subscriptions going
author: Rent in Hermosa

title: Please fix the “finish” button
content:
I don’t know where else to put this but can you PLEASE change the “finish” button to a type where you have to hold it to finish a trail.  It should operate like the pause button does.  I’ve lost two tracks this week alone because I’ve accidentally tapped finish instead of resume when on a trail.  Either make it a push/hold type button or enable a back button after it’s pressed because it pops up the trail review stuff and I’m not ready for that.  Let me go back to the previous screen or make finish button like I said.

Other than that, the app is great and the pro features are fantastic!
author: mynicknameisnotyournickname

title: App works again and I’m a happy hiker
content: I’ve used this app for years and it has helped me discover my love for the outdoors. I left a one star review after I was impacted by the problem other recent 1 star reviews mention,  App crashes leaving it nearly unusable. That wasn’t fair to the developers. That was the only problem it’s had in my years of using it.  After uninstalling and reinstalling the app it worked solid again. This app does deserve 5 stars. It’s probably the most useful tool the average hiker can have. I venture into the wilderness off trail quite a bit and this ensures I can always find my way back to the start point. Thanks developers 🤙🏼🤙🏼
author: Clnbuds

title: Fantastic Maps and App!
content:
AllTrails is awesome! The customized “AllTrails” maps are perfect for what I need. They combine street info with most topo and trail info so you can research and find trailheads much easier than before. The ability to trace the elevation profile of a hike trail is very nice. I also found the recorder only uses a small amount of battery on my iPhone. After a 4 hour hike 75% of my battery remained. 

You need to be a Pro subscriber to use the maps offline but that is more than reasonable given this app’s functionality. Be sure to check downloaded maps in offline mode by going into airplane mode before you leave. 

Highly recommended!
author: rdevillers

title: Great app, sadly lost features
content: I’ve used this app many times to navigate local trails and get details as to how to get to the trails. It also connects to my Garmin data so I can see my stats even if I didn’t use my phone to track the trail. The only reason it is missing a star is because I’ve had a paid membership for three years now. Sometime recently they added their “peak” membership and it took away some of the features I previously had, which was the ability to view hourly weather throughout the day on the trail. I used the feature a lot because I hike with my dogs and in the summer it’s difficult to know if the trails will be cool enough if I’m driving up to the mountain trails.
author: tonyav16

title: Used to be good, now it’s being overly monetized
content: This app used to be good. Now its features are being gradually replaced with forced ads, overt and intrusive attempts to upgrade users to the premium subscription, and features are removed from free to then be moved to premium only. It’s getting to the point where it’s not worth using because you can get the same features plus more on other applications. If you force me to get your premium to preserve features, you need to offer equal or better options than the competition. OnX is a similar price subscription and offers far more like topo maps and route planning. Its clear they’re pushing for paid users so much because they’re losing subscribers, but the reason they’re losing subscribers is BECAUSE the premium is sub par. Innovate or die, it’s way of the market.
author: unhapppy_user

title: From hero to zero
content: I used to love all trails, until I updated it... let me tell you why. Where I live all the trails are remote in the mountains where cell phone service is extremely limited. Before this month I used to be able to pull up all trails with no cell service and be able to pull up maps and see where I was. Majority of the trails I hike are bushwhacks so it makes it super easy to find where I am on the map when I could use this app in conjunction with a map and compass. But sadly now I cannot. I even looked into buying a subscription again but read in recent reviews that still doesn’t work. 😩please fix this problem!!
author: ballsucker

title: Navigate feature bug
content:
I like their new update, however there is a bug that needs fixed: it lets you select your activity when you record it through “navigate” (great update!) but when you’re done recording, the activity always defaults to hiking so you have to manually edit the activity if you were not hiking (annoying). Please fix and thank you for continually improving the app. 

Also, I live in Seattle, a major city filled with tech savvy nerds, yet the routes around here listed on All Trails are filled with outdated, closed, and random listings. Who is vetting and updating your routes? This app would be so much better if I didn’t have to do quite so much of my own digging and vetting for the good stuff. Especially since I pay for the pro membership.
author: Lisa_bo_bisa

title: Great idea. Poor execution.
content: Some major flaws of this app. It requires cellular or WiFi connection. Most hikes I have done do not have cell coverage. Another major flaw, when following directions on how to get to a hike, after arrival it completely dismisses the hike you are planning to do. You need to open the app again and look for your hike again. Another flaw, while recording, if you stop to take pictures or for whatever reason, it stops recording!!! This has happened to me many times and it happened again at today’s hike. Lost my trail. I had to open the app again and look where I was on the trail layers. It was as if you were dropped in a trail 3/4 of the way, but had no recollection of what you have already done. I’m AllTrails Pro subscriber. Deeply regretted.
author: love_okay

title: Improvement thoughts
content:
The app is great for the most part... Here are some thoughts that may or may not make it better.

1-Filtering options, I would like to see better filtering options, i.e. filter by miles/distance, filter by star reviews, filter by easy - hard when looking at the “list” screen...etc

2-Higher miles on the filters. Currently it tops out at 20 miles trails. If I’m looking for something that is 30, 40, 50+ miles I have to click on every trail to find a longer trail.

3-Campsite/RV park location(s) at the trail head or close to it. If I’m traveling out of state for a backpacking trip, it would be nice to know where sites are located at. Makes planning the trip easier.

4-Wish users of the app would add in more “water” information. I plan long trips around creeks, streams, lakes, and rivers so I don’t have to carry as much water with me. Knowing which trail has water and how far down the trail it is, is a deciding factor for choosing the trail.

Just my thoughts...other then that the app is pretty user friendly, works well (until I lose signal), and makes planning a bit easier.
author: Gastankii

title: Love this app!
content: A must have for the back woods explorer or trail seeker. Fantastic App! shows all trails nearby, less traveled trails, remote or the nice parks. Map feature is fantastic and one click link to your navigation to the trail head is really nice! This app is spot on and even works good in spotty service.. I haven’t had to do the offline yet but what a great feature. Use the navigate and save your hike run walk.. useful info to show route, time, elevation, calories burned, your stats and workouts, pause feature for the runners trying to keep min/miles .. Fun app! And a Very useful tool to navigate trail systems. Shows pretty much all of the side trails also. Two Thumbs up!
author: Cptaln

title: Maps not correct or just not updated.
content: Most hikes you research and want to do isn’t on this app. I only use this app to track my mileage. I use Google Maps to track everything else. Yes, google maps even with no service works better than this app. Early on I knew not to trust this app and luckily I stayed out of dangerous scenarios. DO NOT trust this app. Also, app randomly stops working sometimes and the elevation gain resets when it wants as well. I bought a membership right away too so it’s not just a free app malfunction. Please be aware and don’t trust your life with this app. Have other outlets or just know what you’re doing and where you are going.
author: Ben Sergent

title: A Must Have
content: All Trails is an absolute must have tool for adventurists and outdoor enthusiasts. Whenever we travel, I am always on all trails before we go and saving my favorite trails to a list. I also love that I can sort by so many different filters and discover dog friendly trails (and ones that aren’t so we know to leave him home) The GPS to take you the the beginning of the trail head is amazing as Apple Maps has taken us way off base before. I love this app and I highly recommend if you love hiking or trail walking, bike riding or just scenic views. There are plenty of lookout points in the app for those who can’t hike or bike or for those uncooperative weather days!
author: TxGirl92

title: Search UI confuses me
content: I’ve used the app extensively over the last two weeks on a road trip to Acadia national park. The app was great for all the hikes we did. Two things that confused/irritated me: when I searched for hikes and used filters, how to properly navigate between the details of a hike and back to the search results isn’t obvious, so many times I thought by closing the details I’d get back to the results of my filtered search but was instead greeted by the full unfiltered map. Second, when you start a loop not where AllTrails decides the trail head is, but at a different starting point (say, parking lot), then it doesn’t properly account for that when reporting how many miles you have left.
author: justvivid

title: 2 decade long road running falls in love with trails
content:
This app is great. I have been running competitive/ consistently since 2005. Love running from 5ks up to marathon and last few years I have become head over heals for ultras and crazy races. However outside of races I would almost always train on roads. I discovered some awesome trails near my new home and brought be back to high school cross county days. This app allows me to
See Trail options I would have never been aware of even ones I have driven by for over a year. I once had a goal of running every road in my town. Now through this app my new goals is to Run every trail in the local trail systems.
author: Youth pastor Chris

title: do not recommend
content:
I do not recommend this app and am cancelling my Pro subscription. After having used it heavily for a week in the mountains, it is just frustrating. A couple of the features I wanted most and paid for in Pro-- like printing maps -- are only available on your desk top. (There's no cell service where we are, so its critical) And you have to go through several convoluted steps to get a picture of what the trail is like and where it is and how to get to the trailhead. 

The reviews are helpful, but the description on the app is weak: Poor or nonexistent directions (except to export to Google maps which is insufficient) poor general descriptions of the trail. We are in a popular hiking area, so there is no reason for weak information. Frankly the guidebooks from the Tourist Info booth were consistently much better. 

Back to paper guide books and old school topo maps until I can find a better app.
author: Walkersrq

title: AI Overview
content:
A truly great app for years. I’ve used it and loved it for hiking and backpacking all around California. However, they are now introducing ai overviews for the trails and I don’t think I can trust them. I can’t trust that the information I get from AllTrails is safe or reliable if a very dumb and useless computer is trying to give me that information. I am definitely canceling my paid subscription specifically because of this.

Update: AllTrails responded saying that I should contact them if I find any incorrect information. I will not be relying on them for information in the first place, so I can’t do that. Getting incorrect information can ruin a day, a longer backpacking trip, or can even lead users into dangerous situations. I hope that AllTrails will do the decent thing and get rid of the untrustworthy and useless ai integration.
author: duecewain

title: I love at least the idea of this app.
content:
AllTrails tries to do everything I want it to do. Unfortunately, it doesn’t always succeed. For example, it’s sort of a mess to use on my first gen Apple Watch Ultra. My watch is constantly getting disconnected from my phone, but only for AllTrails. And then when the trail is finished, my watch never gets the memo. Every single time, I have to restart my watch to get all trails to quit running in the background. Frustrating.

It does work very well on my iPhone, though. I haven’t decided if I will renew my AllTrails+ subscription. I love being able to download maps before a trip. But the watch thing is annoying. Precise GPS tracking was my primary motivation for purchasing the Ultra. Wish AllTrails worked better with it.
author: Kevanjt

title: Latest app updates make it almost unusable
content:
First - they moved the completed and activities tabs to your profile, ok, nbd but by doing so they also removed the search function. One thing I liked to do was compare how I did to previous time, or find trails I’ve done before where I didn’t do the map as it is listed but that’s what I want to repeat. I’m not going to scroll hundreds of activities to find it.

Second - the elevation calculation is nonsense until you complete the trail, it use to calculate it. I liked knowing what I’ve done for those really long trails were I’m trying to only complete part of it. So now I have to rough calculate it based on the map - super useful for trails that have rolling hills or whatnot. 

Whatever “minor bugs” that were fixed seemed to be more acceptable than the changes they pushed.
author: JammyPandy

title: Attention outdoor enthusiasts!
content: I love this app! I’ve always been a hiker and know my trails in the mountains (I live in NH), but I’ve discovered so many different paths that I didn’t know existed around my area! I really love the map feature as it allows you to zoom into your specific area to see trails or expand your search by zooming out. AND you can record your walk!? I just discovered this feature lol I guess I wasn’t using the app to its full potential! That’s when I decided to write a review. It’s nice to have a free app that does it all. I obviously recommend this to people with all skill levels of adventuring. I’m off to find a new trail today with my pups!          :D
author: MaineResident420maang

title: Horribly slow and super annoying startup
content: I’ve been using this app for awhile now and like its feature set and they provide frequent and useful feature updates. My only complaint is that every single time you start the app it initializes your trail data, which can be very frustrating. Particularly if you had the app closed to save battery life and need to make some quick routing decisions. I’m baffled as to why the process is so inordinately slow because there are numerous technical strategies that can be employed to short circuit the process and quickly determine whether an initialization/sync is in order. How about letting the user decide if they want to initialize/sync at that time instead of making them wait, sometimes minutes? (Question: If the mobile app is used on one device with only an occasional visit to the web app - what exactly needs to be initialized/synced every single time?)
author: trendpundit

title: Great trails, needs watch app
content:
I have to say, I’ve bought the subscription for pro features and I don’t regret it. They’ve made an excellent platform for a huge number of trails. Really well done. 

But the app itself on the iPhone is ok. As far as I know there’s no way to JUST see the map , with your location and direction. They have this’s small map, but the screen has several other items on that distract the eye. It would be great to just have the trail and your location on a whole dedicated screen. 

The other point is this app NEEDS a better Apple Watch app. I’d really rather glance at my wrist to look at the trail and my location. That way I could just leave my phone in my backpack, or even at home. You already have a ui for the map, trail, and location, it just needs to be on the watch now.
author: FernandoTTA

title: Excellent App and Customer Service
content: I got this app to use as a tool  for helping me get back in shape. I had several questions and contacted customer service with them. They were quick to respond and as a result I have upgraded to the pro version of the app. I must say that this is well worth it, after getting separated from my trail today, after getting separated from the trail today on a long hike I was able to use the app to easily find my way back. It also helped me follow the trail, as the one I was in crossed several other trails and had about a dozen forks that were poorly marked. I recommend this app to everyone now and this is an essential tool for me to now use on my adventures.
author: The Scottie

title: So totally worth it!
content:
This app is truly amazing for quickly and easily finding any trails in any area I am going to be in. Plus I can search for trails by difficulty level to make sure that they will accommodate all the hikers going with me and their respective skill levels... Especially my own :)

I love the fact that they tell you the distance of the trail, the altitude change, as well as loads of pictures and reviews from other users so you can get a real clear idea of what the trail has to offer.

We have been in Alaska for almost 2 years now. And just the other day we went to a brand new trail to a beautiful waterfall that we would’ve never known existed without this app.
author: stanmcguire

title: I am a premium customer and cannot wait for my membership to expire!
content:
It has gotten even worse. There is now a “Peak” membership. They haven’t created any new functionality worth paying for so they took functionality, put it behind a hyper-premium paywall and doubled the price! 

Buyer beware when dealing with thieves. 

Once again, I just tried to create a hiking route using this app. I eventually gave up in utter disgust and frustration. 

It would seem logical that a user would want to use a combination of existing trails to create their own, customised route. Although there are at least 2 curated trails listed in the app in the park where I was looking, no trails appear on the map in the creation section. 

The search function to find a starting place for creating a route is almost useless. Even the curated trails fail to appear when searched for by name. 

The “smart” routing often has you walking down a road instead of a trail even after choosing “hiking” as the intended activity. 

Regardless of the route you actually take, you only get credit for the curated routes. For those, you get full credit for walking even if you only walk on a small portion of one.

So, despite the good reviews, it really is an absolutely rubbish app. If this is among the best available, buy a paper map and a compass. The cost is cheaper in terms of time, cash, and frustration.

If you interact with the help-bot, you are told the interaction is consent to their privacy policy. No, my explicit permission is acquiescence to your privacy policy. The bot tells me the company takes my privacy very seriously but with regard to my interaction with the company through it, their seriousness extends to “lump it.”
author: Mb5001

title: Freezes too much
content: The older versions of this app were much better. The new one freezes too much and crashes and is unreliable. I have emailed all trails asking for a refund and they won’t respond. I don’t really understand why they changed this app, the community functions seem to cause a lot of glitches, I don’t really want other people knowing where I am hiking and I really don’t care where other people are hiking so this is a useless feature to me. I guess this is a good feature if somebody is a stalker but that doesn’t really apply to me. The older version of the app was pretty good but don’t waste your money on the new version, it is completely unreliable and freezes/crashes within seconds.  I switched over to GAIA GPSAnd it works much better, especially if you are looking for a simple act it will record where you have walked so you don’t get lost.
author: nickname_#%*]=

title: [updated]New navigation has crucial bad usability
content:
I love all trails and its app, but the updated navigation is terrible. I hiked a couple of times, and every time, the recording was paused unintentionally. So the recording messed up. This is because the pause button is sensitive, and the button position is easily touched, especially for the latest iPhone user.  I hope this will be improved soon.

[updated]
This happens only in a specific environment. And even in my background, the problem does not occur if the tap is perpendicular to the screen. Swipe-like touch makes pause without hold function. The alltrails team may fix it when they can identify these specific environmental issues.
author: Aaaaasfghhcddyh

title: Great App!
content:
The AllTrails app is more than just a trail-finder—it’s a gateway to stillness, awe, and divine presence. Every time I use it, it feels like I’m unrolling a sacred map curated just for my soul’s journey. Whether I’m chasing waterfalls, breathing in forest air, or listening to the whispers of the wind on a quiet path, AllTrails makes it easy to find the perfect space to connect—both with nature and with God.

The app is beautifully designed, user-friendly, and incredibly helpful. I love that I can filter for trails by length, difficulty, and even whether they’re pet-friendly. The offline map option has been a game-changer when cell service drops, allowing me to stay rooted in the moment instead of stressing about directions.

I’ve discovered hidden gems near home I never knew existed, and now I always feel equipped to seek adventure, healing, and peace—wherever I go. This isn’t just an app. It’s a companion for anyone longing to be present, to feel alive, and to remember what matters most.

Thank you, AllTrails, for helping me find beauty again, one step at a time.
author: Elamorgana

title: Frustrating app experience
content:
At the beginning of a recent trek, AllTrails was acting very erratically. The app would not correctly download the trail map regardless of numerous attempts, yet, my hiking partner had no problem. The app kept shutting down for unknown reasons, yet, my hiking partner, again, had no problem. For the sake of argument, we have identical equipment - including battery charge and signal strength at the time. One-half hour of stats for a 3 1/2 hour hike were lost. 
Also, for some unknown reason this app created a mirror image of the hike record. Editing one record automatically edits it’s clone.  I feel confident that if I deleted one (either) copy, I’d probably delete the other.  I’m not about to test that!

Finding online help to resolve this issue was impossible.  Needless to say, with a high degree of frustration, I maintain a double record of a trek erroneously shortened. (To maintain a corrected record of the hike stats, I recorded my partners stats.)
author: EdFromMcUNg

title: App refreshes itself and you lose the map.
content:
Maybe it's just me, but this application is refreshing itself almost every time I switch to another one. I would look at a trail, switch to Google Maps to compare, come back and all is gone, blank frames trying to refresh. Also happens when there's no service. Another problem is that if I set filters for only moderate and hard trails, exiting the app will reset these... It's as if nothing is persistent in the app. While the trails are all nice, the app needs polishing. Will buy when bugs are ironed out.

Update a few years later:

This app is going down the drain. None of the concerns I wrote about were ever addressed. Moreover, it is riddled with full screen nags now. Functions are being taken away and difficulties imposed. Dropping two stars down.
author: Simple Infinity

title: This app changes hiking for the better
content: Use of this app makes such a monumental change in thinking and prep for my hikes. I use this all the time and download all the maps ahead of time and it’s so incredibly handy to know where I’m going. I still carry paper maps, of course, but this app makes navigation on the trail so much easier than its ever been in the past. Think you might have missed a turn? Check the app. Forget which way the car is? Check the app. Download relevant maps ahead of time and carry a portable battery to make sure your phone doesn’t die, and this app will change your life. Love it.
author: State of Sound Studios

title: You are better than Google Maps, but you could still learn a thing or two from them.
content:
I love AllTrails for its detailed coverage of, well, all trails. I love how easy it is to see the whole trail from an arial view so I can plan my hike. I’m impressed with the level of detail and how well the GPS tracks me on the trail even when I’m out of cellular range.

But I don’t love that I can’t browse a map, find something that looks interesting, and drop a couple of pins to figure out the distance and elevation gain between those points. I either have to extrapolate from the map data, or I record it when I walk and then save it in my history. Those options are little help for planning.
author: jenystaiman

title: Inaccurate elevation gained, poor Apple Watch support
content: I have a paid AllTrails account and really wanted to use this while hiking via my Apple Watch. The plus is the map on the watch is useful. Unfortunately, UI on watch is kind of a mess (hard to pause and resume hiking tracking on the watch, you seem to need to pull out your phone to do it reliably). Also, every time you lower your wrist and then check your watch, it goes back to the main screen instead of the screen you selected (like the map). Finally, the dealbreaker was that it is terrible at measuring steps or using GPS to track distance. My computed pace was hilariously wrong (jumped from 20m to 2 hours per mile) and elevation gained was 3x greater than my actual gain. It’s a shame this app is so buggy on the basic features that would make it useful.
author: BBrinck

title: I’m down with AllTrails
content: I wondered at first if AllTrails was really worth the sub price… I have used it enough to this point to say that the price is justified. It’s just a great, useful app. I personally love the feature where you can get a general weather overview for your hike when you set the date and time. It’s just an easy to use app, and has great up to date trail reviews and updates on trails that are always helpful. I use it to keep track of my hikes, to give and receive reviews/updates on hikes, and it has also helped with navigating and staying on the correct trail several times! Highly recommend AllTrails to anyone.
author: Dreynolds206

title: Extremely disappointed
content: I upgraded to the pro version of AllTrails because the AllTrails app won’t allow you to download trail maps unless you do. So under the impression that downloading maps meant I would have them for offline use, I paid for pro. After all why would you have a trail app that you couldn’t access trail maps offline when a lot of trails have no service. Anyway, I downloaded about 20 maps for Yosemite National Park after upgrading to pro thinking I would have all the trail info I need for my trip, but no dice! No maps worked when I got there because apparently downloading the map doesn’t mean you can access it offline. Needless to say I was extremely disappointed and also feel that forcing people to upgrade to pro to “download trail maps” is false advertisement because downloading something means you should have it for offline use. I would like a refund.
author: wyatt222

title: Best app out there for hikers
content:
You can read up on hikes and download the trail map before you go. The tracker lets you know if you have gone off trail. Only downside is using the tracker uses up a lot of battery, but that’s the case with any gps tracker. But you can also just check the trail map periodically without using the tracker and make sure you’re still on the right path. You won’t ever get lost as long as you have the map downloaded and have enough juice in your phone!
Its also great to read the reviews before your adventure to check on trail conditions and any hazards.
This is a must-have for serious hikers!
author: AubreyET

title: Do they even use it themselves?
content:
I really want to like this app, but it’s nearly unusable. I wish they would do user testing and try basic use cases like: “download all the hiking trails near me”, “find off-road driving trails near XYZ location”, or “what trails can I hike from this location” or “show me routes to get from where I’m at now to XYZ location”. The search tools are nearly unusable. Navigation is passable but far from a good user experience. 
Also the app places its needs above users, really tries to force users to rate every single trail so it can build its database. I often kill the app just to get back to the Home Screen because it’s so poorly architected. 
Lots of complaints from someone who wants to like the app, but is pretty disappointed in the design evolution. Do better please.
author: cj1749372

title: Gamify Your Encounter with Nature
content: I wanted to like this app and I signed up for a subscription through a sale advertised on Instagram.  In the few months I’ve used it I feel overwhelmed by the gamification of my nature walk experience.  The app constantly bothers me with requests for sharing my hikes with friends or randos.  It wants me to review my hike, upload photos, link my health metrics, review the app… and now, upgrade to a new, MORE EXPENSIVE premium version.  I just want a mapping app that helps me stay on trail and records my hikes, that’s all.  This app wants me to keep staring at my phone screen during my hike and turning my solitary moment in nature into an advertisement to the world and advertisements towards me… even though I paid for the subscription.  I will be deleting.  These creeps just want your money, they don’t care about hiking or nature.  My recommendation - HIKE FAR AWAY FROM THIS TRASH.
author: michaljo

title: Almost feels like cheating
content: Having the app is such a great companion when hiking. So many times it’s prevented me from taking the wrong turn and having to backtrack or worse getting lost. Setting waypoint for hikes, that you repeat is a great benefit. The app seems to work even with poor signal and for 35 bucks a year it’s pretty decent value. And of course there’s the database of hikes that you can search for places that you’ve never been before as well as discovering things right in your own backyard. i’ve also used it for bushwhacking and navigating to a destination through the woods with no trails. It’s a great tool for that as well.
author: Bearsfeat2

title: Stop forcing your social agenda, privacy not clear
content: I feel very uneasy with your recent push to make so much of my experience public. The change to the “public profile” nonsense is the first change ever that makes me want to cancel. I DO NOT want to connect with anyone else nor do I want any of my info shared or searchable. It is not totally clear if I’m public or not public so I have to change my name in the app now to be sure I have anonymity. You lure me to create a review after I use the app (please add a cancel button to the “finish” / “resume” pop up btw that thing is weird) which I’m pretty sure posts publicly. You need a single radio button that lets the users stay 100% private. Many people don’t want a social profile for safety reasons, this obvious push feels invasive. And ditto on the number of pop ups.
author: KLaRock

title: No way to upgrade to pro if Touch ID doesn’t work on your phone
content:
I would like to upgrade to Pro but the ONLY way to do it is with Touch ID. No other option, nothing in FAQ about it, no way to contact support for help. I have a screen protector in my phone so Touch ID doesn’t work. So no way to get PRO - see developer response below - that worked. Like that it looks like I can record over a trail map that comes up as being close to my home. 

But when I tried to save and download that map, I saw it downloading but have no idea how to bring it up offline - can’t find out where these downloads are kept or how to access them
author: Artichoke 25

title: Recommend All Trails!
content:
I used the Map My Run app for over a decade, but when they sold to another company, the features went away and the settings available declined. 

I had used the All Trails app about 6 years ago but decided to stick with Map My Run. 

Moved to a different state and decided to try All Trails again. It really makes not only finding new trails easy, but when everything is covered with snow you can still stay on it. Pictures you take on the hike are linked to the record, so when you send to friends they can better appreciate the experience. 

The app also keeps highlights of hikes as a personal challenge to work for.  I’ve logged almost 1300 miles this year, but am still trying to better the elevation I did when I was trying it out 6 years  

I have used the app for several years and like the way I can track my miles year after year (1335 last year). I send my family my daily hikes with pictures so they can see I’m still alive.
Strongly recommended!
author: sdbrauer

title: Hikes do not integrate with Apple health
content:
This should be a five star app. But there are two big problems holding it back.

1) Although it records your distance during hikes, it does not integrate with the Apple health app. So you do not get credit for any calories burned, or your distance traveled, unless you also use a second app to track those items at the same time. 

You shouldn’t have to use two apps to collect that data. The AllTrails app should be able to export that data into Apple Health for you.

2) The base app does not let you download any maps for off-line use.

That is a basic need of any hiking app, because most of the time when you are hiking in remote areas you do not have a cell phone signal. So the app does not work unless you can have an off-line map.

But the only way that AllTrails will let you have an off-line map, is if you subscribe to their yearly pro service for $20.

If you go on dozens of hikes a year, the subscription price is a fine value. But if you only go on one or two hikes year, this one price fits all mentality is too much. 

They need to have an option of letting you just pay for the maps you need rather than forcing you into a year-long subscription when all you want is one map.
author: JOATEON

title: All time best hiking and backpacking tool
content: I’ve used all trails for years and it does exactly what you need it to. If you like to hike or you’re a weekend backpacking warrior it’s perfect. I’ve downloaded tons of maps that still work even with no cell connection because it goes off gps. It also has a ton of cool ways to filter trails if you want a loop trail, an out and back, if you wanna see a water fall or a lake and a ton of other stuff. For real I just really appreciate the people that have made this app, because it’s saved me many many times, definitely worth it even if you don’t wanna pay for the premium version.
author: EthanOutside

title: Cancellation was not easy
content: I was curious about this, and decided to try the free trial. I downloaded the app on my iPhone, and created an account. After a day, i decided it wasn’t for me. I also didn’t like how they only offer a year subscription, rather than monthly. I went into my subscriptions on my phone, and it wasn’t there. I tried numerous times where I finally thought I was successful. Then I was charged. It finally took me going online to their website- which I had never been on. So their steps for how to cancel are not accurate. Now I have a year membership that I do not want. If you are on the fence like I was, don’t do this. Cancelling your subscription was not easy. I screen shot again when it said it was cancelled, but I’m still wondering if I will get charged again next year. I’ve never left a bad review, but this truly deserves it.
author: SunsetBlonde1989

title: Perfect for adventuring families
content: I am an avid outdoorsman and family man and this tool is an invaluable tool in my adventure belt. I take my kids out all the time and using this tool to map out and get the best route for my kids to get an epic adventure is hands down the easiest way i have found. I have only bought three apps, and have always used the free version of apps. The free version of this one is great, but I think it is definitely worth the subscription for the extra tools available. Traveling or local use, you can’t go wrong with such a rock solid tool. I’ve used this for three years now and it has gotten me to some absolutely amazing places. Definitely a must.
author: Dr dingle

title: Love both the phone and watch apps
content: Have been using the app for a while now and really love the ability to find local hikes quick and simple. The breadcrumb trail on the map is perfect. Integration with the Apple Watch is nice. There was a recent update for the watch app that introduced the compas feature which I am enjoying using. They did away with the map on the watch which for me worked a quarter of the time. Yes you could see the trace but most of the time the map wasn’t visible, just had a grid pattern with a colored line on it. Have to say tho it was nice to have the map on my wrist when it worked. Fix that so the map is visible 100% of the time, I would give it 5 stars!
author: caq77

title: Amazing App with One Major Flaw
content:
This app is absolutely fantastic. It will help you find amazing local trails and review them for others. It has wonderfully detailed maps and excellent trails all over the world.

However, the amount of battery this app consumes is outrageous. On a 3-4 hour hike, my battery typically starts to die rapidly. It didn’t use to be like this, but on my iPhone 15
Pro it’s absolutely killing my battery. I looked at the battery app on my phone to discover that AllTrails is using up about 33% of my battery on its own, and this was previously not the case.

Not sure what happened, but the app is still easily worth the 100$ asking price. It’s just unfortunate how hard it’s draining my battery currently. 

Oh, and the Apple Watch support is kind of terrible and worthless. My Apple Watch frequently gets “desynced” from my phone (they display different miles and times). The watch needs your iPhone as well, but it would be amazing to have support without needing your phone.

Bring a solar charger on any hike that’s around 9+ miles and you’ll be fine. Although, the performance and battery life consumption used to be better!
author: Cesium06

title: Help, something got broken with the latest update
content: I normally love the app and have logged over 800 miles of hikes — the latest update is terrible and renders the app virtually useless. You cannot bring up a map without cell service, even for a trail downloaded in advance. After opening and closing the app maybe 10 times, turning my phone on and off, etc., it did finally let me record free-form, without loading the trail — I wasn’t able to see any of the maps I had downloaded or any information about the trail. Also, the app will no longer run in the background — every time I opened the camera or another app, AllTrails crashed and more often than not, the recording stopped and had to be restarted. This is on an iPhone 11. Hopefully it gets fixed soon!
author: andreab718

title: Oh! The Places We’ll Go!!! THANKS ALL TRAILS !
content: I stumbled upon this app and it is been a LOT of fun for plotting and planning. I like having my favorites and the ability to create lists to keep them sorted and organized by state. I did a short hike in West Virginia and really used up a lot of my cell phone battery. I am going to see how to just use the GPS only to conserve on that. Also going to upgrade to the PRO as well. So I can print out maps and reference the hike that way. I’m going on vacation to Rapid City South Dakota in August and I am really looking forward to doing some hikes around the Black Hills and Spearfish Canyon, Mount Rushmore, etc and sharing those experiences with my friends and on All Trails! Happy Trails! 🌸🧗‍♀️🚵‍♀️🌄🌅
author: wildflower🌻

title: Almost Perfect!
content:
Absolutely love this app! Makes getting out there so much easier and safe. It would be a great addition to add a feature that senses when you’ve began moving again on the trail, just like it gives you an alert when you’re off-route (which is incredible by the way!). Sometimes I pause it to eat a snack and totally forget to restart it. :( 

A super cool addition just for enjoyment would be a way to have a goal tracker. Such as a hiking miles or elevation gain goals for the month. That’s just extra but I know I would love it!! Thanks for the work on this amazing produc. I use it religiously on my days off. :)
author: Ohh V

title: Basic Trail Info/Support Lacking
content:
I had hoped to use this app and bought into the Pro version. But I’ve come to learn it’s not what I thought it would be. 

While it has basic trail info (stats, other user info, etc) it’s help feature is severely lacking. You have to email them, and if you have lots of questions this can take days. Plus they keep referring you to their FAQ web page, or their web videos. I don’t want to “read” everything. I want a human to ask a question to and be done, not have to go to another page because the first page doesn’t answer my question. Their Support admitted they are a small organization: I say if you’re going to play with the big boys, then you need to be able to keep up. Emailing doesn’t cut it.

Having said that, if they improve on their support I think this could be a really good app. I just don’t think at this point they’re ready.
author: mount10hiker

title: Deleted trails and argumentative customer “service”
content:
ADDENDUM: Your response to my review completely made my point!! Instead of trying to figure out how to fix a problem, you continued to argue your point. My point was: crucial trails are missing from at least one hiking area I know of. It renders Alltrails useless for hiking in Forest Park, Portland. Those trails need to be added back in to the Alltrails layer of your maps. I have just downloaded and begun to use Gaia because their maps do include all of the appropriate trails in that area. If you decide to take action to correct the problem rather than argue, let me know. (My Pro subscription will not be renewed if I can’t trust your maps to include crucial trails, which happen to have names which include “road” or “drive” in them. 

 At some point in the last year, for some reason certain trails— which are labeled as roads, but no longer used as roads, only trails— have been removed from the Alltrails layer and can’t be used to plot any mapping routes (pro account) for offline use or even used to calculate distances because although they are included in the “roads” layer and a few other layers, there are no mileage indicators. You can’t make an offline map using the “roads” layer and even if you could, you have to map it using the freehand mapping tool and plot it little bit by little bit if you don’t want the curvy trails to be recorded as a straight line. A route can’t be plotted automatically using these trails because Alltrails suddenly decided to treat them as non-trails. When I contacted customer service, they were of no help with this. They merely kept insisting that I was mistaken and these trails had never been shown as trails, which is totally false since I’ve plotted many routes along them since I started using Alltrails a number of years ago. 1) Train your customer service people to figure out how something could be improved, not spend their time arguing their point. They did tell me to just use the roads version, which wasn’t helpful. 2) Please put back my trails!!!
author: SCUBACHARI

title: Super useful
content: I love being able to create my own routes wherever I want to go. I’ve created maps for off trail, for biking, for long backpacking trips. What’s really great is the community let’s you know where they found great campsite, and that’s usually one of the hardest things to figure out when you’re going to a new location. Being able to put In waypoints, being able to switch from AllTrails, to USGS maps, to Satellite are features I use consistently. I run a small nonprofit in NC (The American Adventure Service Corps- Lake Norman) that takes kids 8-18 into our wild places and AllTrails is super useful to our mission! Highly recommended.
author: davedenny3

title: Learning to hate this app
content:
1. Used it last week to identify an 8 mile hike. The app shows it by one trail name and as a loop. The loop is actually a set of trails but All Trails does not show this in any way. Had no service on the trail and I had no way of knowing that I was supposed to link to other trails so had to take it out and back so I missed a good portion of the planned hike At least allow us to view all of the trail segments 2. There is no way to look for POIs THAT ARE NOT PARKS. Example, if I know of a good watering hole but not the park name next to it. Would like to use All Trails to choose random watering holes/places to eat and tell me what trails are nearby
3. The website prompts you to open the app over and over and over again. Sometimes you just eant to be on the website!
author: Zpad2

title: Watch app is bad
content:
The app itself is ok outside of freezing and stopping without telling you pretty frequently. I wish there was a feature that would just fill in the gap with your average pace when that happens.

The watch app is terrible however. Always freezing and the compass is useless. It used to be great when it showed the map but they got rid of that for whatever reason and replaced it with a compass that tells you the wrong direction more times than not when it’s not frozen. I wish I could just have the map back on it. 

The whole point of being outside is to be off my phone but I have to constantly check it to make sure it’s still recording or check directions. It was infinite times better when the map was available on the watch.
author: qtrain6

title: PLEASE fix Apple Watch maps
content:
Wearables are so important with hiking. If one uses two hiking poles, you can’t hold your phone the entire hike.  That’s why I invested in the higher AllTrails subscription and an Apple Watch Ultra 2. 

With the Apple Watch Ultra 2, the waypoint on the AllTrails map frequently jumps off the trail. On top of that, zooming in for precision turns is not possible and can get confusing. (I’d rather not have to pull out my phone).  I did open a ticket with AllTrails and haven’t heard back yet regarding the waypoint and GPS being way off. If this problem gets fixed I will update my rating.  I really want this to work!

Other than that important item, this is a fantastic app for planning and hiking; assuming you hold your phone in your hand while hiking.
author: TheChris615

title: Subscription Fees Monthly or Yearly
content:
I’m not paying an ever increasing amount of money for anything as trivial as this. I swear to God Apple should force you to reveal what the actual cost of the app is before the download starts. If I download an app and then it tells me there’s a phony trial period then it’s subscription city, I’m deleting the app and I’m never giving you money and I’m going to all but slander you and your app to anyone who might be interested in it. 

IDK if you’re homeless and you spend all your time in the woods you MIGHT get value from your money here. 

I’m not saying subscription fees for an app like this is a legit scam, but it is usurious in the sense that you will inevitably be paying for something that you aren’t using. They know how many people have forgotten that they pay for this each month and don’t use the app anymore. It’s probably their favorite number. Gross.
author: The Fear of Music

title: I really like the app
content:
The app is pretty great. I use it a fair amount and never have any issues. 
One little thing I think that could be added, is maybe a way to show either the begging AND ends of trails. Sometimes I know the area where the trail ends but no clue where it starts and with longer trails it could be 15-30 miles in any direction where it starts. But if you could have a pin at the end also or add a setting to show the beginnings or ends of trails or maybe even pins for some notable steals like like on the trail where you can click on the pin near the lake, and it’ll show you which trail leads you there.
author: Anyone you want it to be

title: Can’t trust this app
content:
I read the Developer response and did what they said, it cut out in a strange city where I didn’t know where I was going. All I can say is, if you trust this app it will get you killed!

I got lucky, I was close to home and knew the trail, but this app cuts out and you can’t use downloaded maps. All trails cut out while I had good cell reception, so I tried to use the map I had downloaded. When I tried to use the map I had downloaded all that came up was a red line over a blank page. I was in the Marine Corps Infantry and attached to Special Operations, so I know how important it is to have a map and a GPS you can trust, AllTrails isn’t it. The other thing is I’m going to a remote part of Utah, the other GPS app has it, AllTrail doesn’t. What I’ve found is AllTrail cuts out a lot, and it doesn’t have maps for remote areas, what good is it. The worst part is I got suckered into paying $20 for Pro.
author: SemperFi1/5

title: Bricked my phone, twice
content: When it works it’s great. On two separate occasions, out on a trail, it has completely bricked my phone. The app freezes up and I am unable to exit, force quit, force restart, anything. Completely rendered my phone useless on two occasions. No way to call, text, navigate, email, etc… Left me without navigation I stupidly depended on this app. The only way I was able to recover my phone was to let the battery naturally completely drain to the point of shutdown. If it had a full charge that could be days. The only way I could draw power to speed up this process was waking the phone up as it was frozen halfway asleep and then I could wake to use power to up the brightness. THIS HAPPENED TO ME TWICE WITH THIS APP! No other app has ever rendered my phone completely useless. Unreal that an app used for navigation in the wild would do this.
author: meeeezbo

title: Accurate and reliable
content: My favorite hiking app! I live in the blue ridge mountains of North Carolina, so my hiking options are pretty unlimited. I am horrible at putting trail maps into perspective so I love that they put the estimated time it takes. Even though it’s usually way longer than it takes me, it’s nice to know before you go. I also love the active gps, it tells you where you are on the trail even when your service cuts out. This has been a life saver for me as I always think I’m going the right way. The pictures are awesome too! Especially when you don’t know what it’s going to be like at that time of year.
author: 2019aliah

title: Great maps, NOT user friendly
content:
I am not sure I understand all the great reviews.  The maps are superb.  But I think it is confusing and awkward to use.   I generally don’t know what trail I am going to go on when we leave the house and cel phone range. I live in Colorado and would just like to download the entire state.   I don’t care if that takes 10 GB.  But you cannot do that.  

Also once I have downloaded an area with the strange process they gave me (tracing a LARGE hiking route to capture the whole area) then once I start on a route I would expect it to realize what route I am on and show that like “Hiking rainbow lake trail”.   It does not do that.   

I also find it quite buggy.   Hangs up a lot when downloading trails.  FYI I have a new modern i Phone.  Also it is supposed to allow my wife to download the same files, but it never seems to work quite right.   Her resolution is way less than on my identical phone.   Why?   

Last, I have found it to lose signals sometimes so you have gaps in your traced route.  

Overall I love the map details.   But both my wife and I find that it needs some serious improvement.
author: Robegul

title: Easy, quick, helpful!
content: This app just makes it easy for finding ideas on where to hike and getting beta on the current conditions of the trails. My only frustration is that while on trail, the app often closes all the way to the start when I have my phone’s screen off. I often have to wait for the app to load and then reselect the trail all over again to see where I am. Most tracking apps just keep that page and you can immediately see your location when you unlock your phone. It’s a good 20secs waiting for this app to reload and then 3 touches to direct it back to where I was. Other than that annoyance I really like it.
author: Wyred11

title: Needs and Orange Indicator
content:
Very useful app that I’ve used for years now. However, I think this app could get better and more interactive/informative by having somewhere early in the trail description if there is hunting nearby to alert hikers to wear Orange! 
I’ve been looking at a few trails that were found by this app in my state and several of them are near hunting grounds with trailheads that clearly state and warn hikers/bikers to have Orange on you along with the hunting season times. 
Please find a way to have this feature in there. I know this app has been used by many novice hikers now and I’m sure many do not have Orange vests/hats in their cars at all times like I do (crazy nut-case).
Happy trails to everyone!
author: AMWF2021

title: Lia
content: Hands down one of the best apps you could have if you like the outdoors or travel. They provide places and information about it through maps and other people experiences. This app is for people of all activists I use hiking/ walking myself. All the maps I’ve used to guide me have been extremely accurate and easy to follow. Everything you can do for free. You can upgrade to plus if you’d really like. I never thought about it until today so I could download my maps incase I were to lose service but I go alone. I’ve been on several trails I would’ve never found without this app.
author: LiaLob

title: Alltrails will make your PRIVATE 3rd party activities PUBLIC
content:
TLDR: Alltrails makes every activity public by default, even if it’s coming from a linked 3rd party where the activity is private. Nothing clearly shows this when linking 3rd parties, you better read the fine print and check the settings!
—
One day I linked alltrails to my garmin account in hopes of getting routes from alltrails to my garmin smartwatch. That wasn’t a thing, and I forgot about it.

It turns out that when you connect alltrails to garmin, alltrails gets access to all your activities & recordings, even if they’re private. Alltrails also publishes the recordings on their own platform but makes them ALL PUBLIC by default even if they were originally PRIVATE on garmin. Yeah, that completely disregards common sense about user privacy. As a result hundreds of my private garmin activities (think running through my neighborhood) were publicly available to anybody under my alltrails account.

I found out after nearly a year of this and messaged support. They were completely dismissive and essentially told me that I had accepted the ToS and that the behavior was normal and that I had signed up for it and didn’t configure my privacy settings. I can’t argue with that, I didn’t read the fine print and didn’t review settings before connecting the two services.

But it baffles me that they somehow think it’s okay to publish private activities from a 3rd party as public and that this is the DEFAULT behavior of the system. A proper privacy practice is that everything is private by default, period. If I want my stuff public, I’ll make it so. Somehow, that doesn’t bother them.

So one star for not caring about user privacy and for awful and dismissive customer support.
author: Whoodatss

title: Well worth a subscription
content:
I started using All Trails when I took up solo hiking, and it has been well worth it. I always download a copy of the map before every hike. Sometimes trails aren’t well defined in my area, and All Trails gives me peace of mind that I’m literally on the right path. I also share my hike with family every time I go out so they know exactly what trail I’ve taken, which makes me and them feel more confident when I hike on my own. 
My only complaint would be that it is really easy to accidentally turn on tracking on your hike. And that’s it. That is the only complaint I have about this app.
author: Haunted Daffodil

title: I’d have given 5 stars but...
content: I keep having issues with my location. It has my location as a completely different state and I keep getting an error message saying I need to have a data connection to change it, which I do AND I’m on Wi-Fi as well. Furthermore I’m trying to search for a very specific trail by name and I cannot find it on here. I’m wondering if it has something to do with my location..? I’ve searched by town, state and trail name. Other than the issues I’m having today I have gotten a lot of use out of this app. I have found many interesting trails near my house that I didn’t even know existed.
author: Deathmetaljess

title: Most useful app
content: AllTrails has been a total game-changer for me. I’m old-school and always use paper maps for long-distance hikes (still vital), but the motivation I got here has been astounding. I thought I’d hiked them all in my area and AllTrails got me back out exploring and tracking my progress. I use it on every walk and hike, swim and kayaking adventure and love looking back on my favorite memories! My whole family uses it now too, and it has saved me ton of time in finding my back in remote areas. I’ve even been tracking every mile my dog has hiked in his 6 years with me so far. I can’t say enough good things!
author: Andi Sunday

title: My Go-To for Hiking
content: Ive never even thought about using another app. All Trails always has what I’m looking for. Whether it’s a long hike, short walking trail, somewhere to bike, a waterfall or swimming hole—everything, everywhere. Ill even go visit friends and pull up some quick hikes in their state. And then the downloadable offline map is HUGE. My biggest fear is getting lost and Ive never gotten lost using All Trails’ maps. It shows you other’s reviews and photos of the trails, the weather in that area, parking options—it’s phenomenal honestly. I always find the kind of activity and views Im looking for. 10/10 recommend besties;))
author: Katrnia_grace17

title: Was great at one point, but not now.
content:
I’ve used AllTrails for 6 year and logged over 1200 miles. The last two weeks my downloaded maps are no longer working. Today I drove 45 minutes down a dirt road to get to a hike you needed a map just to start. To my surprise, my downloaded map is just green. No directions for anything. Happened in glacier national park two weeks ago.  Had to drive 45 minutes back into town to get cell reception, start my tracking, then drive back just so I had a clue what direction to go. Very disappointed with all the new updates and how poorly the app has been the last year. Going to start trying other apps to see if they are more reliable. 

Thanks for many good years.
author: Dandman311

title: Excellent App and Customer Service
content: I got this app to use as a tool  for helping me get back in shape. I had several questions and contacted customer service with them. They were quick to respond and as a result I have upgraded to the pro version of the app. I must say that this is well worth it, after getting separated from my trail today, after getting separated from the trail today on a long hike I was able to use the app to easily find my way back. It also helped me follow the trail, as the one I was in crossed several other trails and had about a dozen forks that were poorly marked. I recommend this app to everyone now and this is an essential tool for me to now use on my adventures.
author: The Scottie

title: So totally worth it!
content:
This app is truly amazing for quickly and easily finding any trails in any area I am going to be in. Plus I can search for trails by difficulty level to make sure that they will accommodate all the hikers going with me and their respective skill levels... Especially my own :)

I love the fact that they tell you the distance of the trail, the altitude change, as well as loads of pictures and reviews from other users so you can get a real clear idea of what the trail has to offer.

We have been in Alaska for almost 2 years now. And just the other day we went to a brand new trail to a beautiful waterfall that we would’ve never known existed without this app.
author: stanmcguire

title: I am a premium customer and cannot wait for my membership to expire!
content:
It has gotten even worse. There is now a “Peak” membership. They haven’t created any new functionality worth paying for so they took functionality, put it behind a hyper-premium paywall and doubled the price! 

Buyer beware when dealing with thieves. 

Once again, I just tried to create a hiking route using this app. I eventually gave up in utter disgust and frustration. 

It would seem logical that a user would want to use a combination of existing trails to create their own, customised route. Although there are at least 2 curated trails listed in the app in the park where I was looking, no trails appear on the map in the creation section. 

The search function to find a starting place for creating a route is almost useless. Even the curated trails fail to appear when searched for by name. 

The “smart” routing often has you walking down a road instead of a trail even after choosing “hiking” as the intended activity. 

Regardless of the route you actually take, you only get credit for the curated routes. For those, you get full credit for walking even if you only walk on a small portion of one.

So, despite the good reviews, it really is an absolutely rubbish app. If this is among the best available, buy a paper map and a compass. The cost is cheaper in terms of time, cash, and frustration.

If you interact with the help-bot, you are told the interaction is consent to their privacy policy. No, my explicit permission is acquiescence to your privacy policy. The bot tells me the company takes my privacy very seriously but with regard to my interaction with the company through it, their seriousness extends to “lump it.”
author: Mb5001

title: Freezes too much
content: The older versions of this app were much better. The new one freezes too much and crashes and is unreliable. I have emailed all trails asking for a refund and they won’t respond. I don’t really understand why they changed this app, the community functions seem to cause a lot of glitches, I don’t really want other people knowing where I am hiking and I really don’t care where other people are hiking so this is a useless feature to me. I guess this is a good feature if somebody is a stalker but that doesn’t really apply to me. The older version of the app was pretty good but don’t waste your money on the new version, it is completely unreliable and freezes/crashes within seconds.  I switched over to GAIA GPSAnd it works much better, especially if you are looking for a simple act it will record where you have walked so you don’t get lost.
author: nickname_#%*]=

title: [updated]New navigation has crucial bad usability
content:
I love all trails and its app, but the updated navigation is terrible. I hiked a couple of times, and every time, the recording was paused unintentionally. So the recording messed up. This is because the pause button is sensitive, and the button position is easily touched, especially for the latest iPhone user.  I hope this will be improved soon.

[updated]
This happens only in a specific environment. And even in my background, the problem does not occur if the tap is perpendicular to the screen. Swipe-like touch makes pause without hold function. The alltrails team may fix it when they can identify these specific environmental issues.
author: Aaaaasfghhcddyh

title: Great App!
content:
The AllTrails app is more than just a trail-finder—it’s a gateway to stillness, awe, and divine presence. Every time I use it, it feels like I’m unrolling a sacred map curated just for my soul’s journey. Whether I’m chasing waterfalls, breathing in forest air, or listening to the whispers of the wind on a quiet path, AllTrails makes it easy to find the perfect space to connect—both with nature and with God.

The app is beautifully designed, user-friendly, and incredibly helpful. I love that I can filter for trails by length, difficulty, and even whether they’re pet-friendly. The offline map option has been a game-changer when cell service drops, allowing me to stay rooted in the moment instead of stressing about directions.

I’ve discovered hidden gems near home I never knew existed, and now I always feel equipped to seek adventure, healing, and peace—wherever I go. This isn’t just an app. It’s a companion for anyone longing to be present, to feel alive, and to remember what matters most.

Thank you, AllTrails, for helping me find beauty again, one step at a time.
author: Elamorgana

title: Frustrating app experience
content:
At the beginning of a recent trek, AllTrails was acting very erratically. The app would not correctly download the trail map regardless of numerous attempts, yet, my hiking partner had no problem. The app kept shutting down for unknown reasons, yet, my hiking partner, again, had no problem. For the sake of argument, we have identical equipment - including battery charge and signal strength at the time. One-half hour of stats for a 3 1/2 hour hike were lost. 
Also, for some unknown reason this app created a mirror image of the hike record. Editing one record automatically edits it’s clone.  I feel confident that if I deleted one (either) copy, I’d probably delete the other.  I’m not about to test that!

Finding online help to resolve this issue was impossible.  Needless to say, with a high degree of frustration, I maintain a double record of a trek erroneously shortened. (To maintain a corrected record of the hike stats, I recorded my partners stats.)
author: EdFromMcUNg

title: App refreshes itself and you lose the map.
content:
Maybe it's just me, but this application is refreshing itself almost every time I switch to another one. I would look at a trail, switch to Google Maps to compare, come back and all is gone, blank frames trying to refresh. Also happens when there's no service. Another problem is that if I set filters for only moderate and hard trails, exiting the app will reset these... It's as if nothing is persistent in the app. While the trails are all nice, the app needs polishing. Will buy when bugs are ironed out.

Update a few years later:

This app is going down the drain. None of the concerns I wrote about were ever addressed. Moreover, it is riddled with full screen nags now. Functions are being taken away and difficulties imposed. Dropping two stars down.
author: Simple Infinity

title: This app changes hiking for the better
content: Use of this app makes such a monumental change in thinking and prep for my hikes. I use this all the time and download all the maps ahead of time and it’s so incredibly handy to know where I’m going. I still carry paper maps, of course, but this app makes navigation on the trail so much easier than its ever been in the past. Think you might have missed a turn?
