Check the app. Forget which way the car is? Check the app. Download relevant maps ahead of time and carry a portable battery to make sure your phone doesn’t die, and this app will change your life. Love it.
author: State of Sound Studios

title: You are better than Google Maps, but you could still learn a thing or two from them.
content:
I love AllTrails for its detailed coverage of, well, all trails. I love how easy it is to see the whole trail from an arial view so I can plan my hike. I’m impressed with the level of detail and how well the GPS tracks me on the trail even when I’m out of cellular range.

But I don’t love that I can’t browse a map, find something that looks interesting, and drop a couple of pins to figure out the distance and elevation gain between those points. I either have to extrapolate from the map data, or I record it when I walk and then save it in my history. Those options are little help for planning.
author: jenystaiman

title: Inaccurate elevation gained, poor Apple Watch support
content: I have a paid AllTrails account and really wanted to use this while hiking via my Apple Watch. The plus is the map on the watch is useful. Unfortunately, UI on watch is kind of a mess (hard to pause and resume hiking tracking on the watch, you seem to need to pull out your phone to do it reliably). Also, every time you lower your wrist and then check your watch, it goes back to the main screen instead of the screen you selected (like the map). Finally, the dealbreaker was that it is terrible at measuring steps or using GPS to track distance. My computed pace was hilariously wrong (jumped from 20m to 2 hours per mile) and elevation gained was 3x greater than my actual gain. It’s a shame this app is so buggy on the basic features that would make it useful.
author: BBrinck

title: I’m down with AllTrails
content: I wondered at first if AllTrails was really worth the sub price… I have used it enough to this point to say that the price is justified. It’s just a great, useful app. I personally love the feature where you can get a general weather overview for your hike when you set the date and time. It’s just an easy to use app, and has great up to date trail reviews and updates on trails that are always helpful. I use it to keep track of my hikes, to give and receive reviews/updates on hikes, and it has also helped with navigating and staying on the correct trail several times! Highly recommend AllTrails to anyone.
author: Dreynolds206

title: Extremely disappointed
content: I upgraded to the pro version of AllTrails because the AllTrails app won’t allow you to download trail maps unless you do. So under the impression that downloading maps meant I would have them for offline use, I paid for pro. After all why would you have a trail app that you couldn’t access trail maps offline when a lot of trails have no service. Anyway, I downloaded about 20 maps for Yosemite National Park after upgrading to pro thinking I would have all the trail info I need for my trip, but no dice! No maps worked when I got there because apparently downloading the map doesn’t mean you can access it offline. Needless to say I was extremely disappointed and also feel that forcing people to upgrade to pro to “download trail maps” is false advertisement because downloading something means you should have it for offline use. I would like a refund.
author: wyatt222

title: Best app out there for hikers
content:
You can read up on hikes and download the trail map before you go. The tracker lets you know if you have gone off trail. Only downside is using the tracker uses up a lot of battery, but that’s the case with any gps tracker. But you can also just check the trail map periodically without using the tracker and make sure you’re still on the right path. You won’t ever get lost as long as you have the map downloaded and have enough juice in your phone!
Its also great to read the reviews before your adventure to check on trail conditions and any hazards.
This is a must-have for serious hikers!
author: AubreyET

title: Do they even use it themselves?
content:
I really want to like this app, but it’s nearly unusable. I wish they would do user testing and try basic use cases like: “download all the hiking trails near me”, “find off-road driving trails near XYZ location”, or “what trails can I hike from this location” or “show me routes to get from where I’m at now to XYZ location”. The search tools are nearly unusable. Navigation is passable but far from a good user experience. 
Also the app places its needs above users, really tries to force users to rate every single trail so it can build its database. I often kill the app just to get back to the Home Screen because it’s so poorly architected. 
Lots of complaints from someone who wants to like the app, but is pretty disappointed in the design evolution. Do better please.
author: cj1749372

title: Gamify Your Encounter with Nature
content: I wanted to like this app and I signed up for a subscription through a sale advertised on Instagram.  In the few months I’ve used it I feel overwhelmed by the gamification of my nature walk experience.  The app constantly bothers me with requests for sharing my hikes with friends or randos.  It wants me to review my hike, upload photos, link my health metrics, review the app… and now, upgrade to a new, MORE EXPENSIVE premium version.  I just want a mapping app that helps me stay on trail and records my hikes, that’s all.  This app wants me to keep staring at my phone screen during my hike and turning my solitary moment in nature into an advertisement to the world and advertisements towards me… even though I paid for the subscription.  I will be deleting.  These creeps just want your money, they don’t care about hiking or nature.  My recommendation - HIKE FAR AWAY FROM THIS TRASH.
author: michaljo

title: Almost feels like cheating
content: Having the app is such a great companion when hiking. So many times it’s prevented me from taking the wrong turn and having to backtrack or worse getting lost. Setting waypoint for hikes, that you repeat is a great benefit. The app seems to work even with poor signal and for 35 bucks a year it’s pretty decent value. And of course there’s the database of hikes that you can search for places that you’ve never been before as well as discovering things right in your own backyard. i’ve also used it for bushwhacking and navigating to a destination through the woods with no trails. It’s a great tool for that as well.
author: Bearsfeat2

title: Stop forcing your social agenda, privacy not clear
content: I feel very uneasy with your recent push to make so much of my experience public. The change to the “public profile” nonsense is the first change ever that makes me want to cancel. I DO NOT want to connect with anyone else nor do I want any of my info shared or searchable. It is not totally clear if I’m public or not public so I have to change my name in the app now to be sure I have anonymity. You lure me to create a review after I use the app (please add a cancel button to the “finish” / “resume” pop up btw that thing is weird) which I’m pretty sure posts publicly. You need a single radio button that lets the users stay 100% private. Many people don’t want a social profile for safety reasons, this obvious push feels invasive. And ditto on the number of pop ups.
author: KLaRock

title: No way to upgrade to pro if Touch ID doesn’t work on your phone
content:
I would like to upgrade to Pro but the ONLY way to do it is with Touch ID. No other option, nothing in FAQ about it, no way to contact support for help. I have a screen protector in my phone so Touch ID doesn’t work. So no way to get PRO - see developer response below - that worked. Like that it looks like I can record over a trail map that comes up as being close to my home. 

But when I tried to save and download that map, I saw it downloading but have no idea how to bring it up offline - can’t find out where these downloads are kept or how to access them
author: Artichoke 25

title: Recommend All Trails!
content:
I used the Map My Run app for over a decade, but when they sold to another company, the features went away and the settings available declined. 

I had used the All Trails app about 6 years ago but decided to stick with Map My Run. 

Moved to a different state and decided to try All Trails again. It really makes not only finding new trails easy, but when everything is covered with snow you can still stay on it. Pictures you take on the hike are linked to the record, so when you send to friends they can better appreciate the experience. 

The app also keeps highlights of hikes as a personal challenge to work for.  I’ve logged almost 1300 miles this year, but am still trying to better the elevation I did when I was trying it out 6 years  

I have used the app for several years and like the way I can track my miles year after year (1335 last year). I send my family my daily hikes with pictures so they can see I’m still alive.
Strongly recommended!
author: sdbrauer

title: Hikes do not integrate with Apple health
content:
This should be a five star app. But there are two big problems holding it back.

1) Although it records your distance during hikes, it does not integrate with the Apple health app. So you do not get credit for any calories burned, or your distance traveled, unless you also use a second app to track those items at the same time. 

You shouldn’t have to use two apps to collect that data. The AllTrails app should be able to export that data into Apple Health for you.

2) The base app does not let you download any maps for off-line use.

That is a basic need of any hiking app, because most of the time when you are hiking in remote areas you do not have a cell phone signal. So the app does not work unless you can have an off-line map.

But the only way that AllTrails will let you have an off-line map, is if you subscribe to their yearly pro service for $20.

If you go on dozens of hikes a year, the subscription price is a fine value. But if you only go on one or two hikes year, this one price fits all mentality is too much. 

They need to have an option of letting you just pay for the maps you need rather than forcing you into a year-long subscription when all you want is one map.
author: JOATEON

title: All time best hiking and backpacking tool
content: I’ve used all trails for years and it does exactly what you need it to. If you like to hike or you’re a weekend backpacking warrior it’s perfect. I’ve downloaded tons of maps that still work even with no cell connection because it goes off gps. It also has a ton of cool ways to filter trails if you want a loop trail, an out and back, if you wanna see a water fall or a lake and a ton of other stuff. For real I just really appreciate the people that have made this app, because it’s saved me many many times, definitely worth it even if you don’t wanna pay for the premium version.
author: EthanOutside

title: Cancellation was not easy
content: I was curious about this, and decided to try the free trial. I downloaded the app on my iPhone, and created an account. After a day, i decided it wasn’t for me. I also didn’t like how they only offer a year subscription, rather than monthly. I went into my subscriptions on my phone, and it wasn’t there. I tried numerous times where I finally thought I was successful. Then I was charged. It finally took me going online to their website- which I had never been on. So their steps for how to cancel are not accurate. Now I have a year membership that I do not want. If you are on the fence like I was, don’t do this. Cancelling your subscription was not easy. I screen shot again when it said it was cancelled, but I’m still wondering if I will get charged again next year. I’ve never left a bad review, but this truly deserves it.
author: SunsetBlonde1989

title: Perfect for adventuring families
content: I am an avid outdoorsman and family man and this tool is an invaluable tool in my adventure belt. I take my kids out all the time and using this tool to map out and get the best route for my kids to get an epic adventure is hands down the easiest way i have found. I have only bought three apps, and have always used the free version of apps. The free version of this one is great, but I think it is definitely worth the subscription for the extra tools available. Traveling or local use, you can’t go wrong with such a rock solid tool. I’ve used this for three years now and it has gotten me to some absolutely amazing places. Definitely a must.
author: Dr dingle

title: Love both the phone and watch apps
content: Have been using the app for a while now and really love the ability to find local hikes quick and simple. The breadcrumb trail on the map is perfect. Integration with the Apple Watch is nice. There was a recent update for the watch app that introduced the compas feature which I am enjoying using. They did away with the map on the watch which for me worked a quarter of the time. Yes you could see the trace but most of the time the map wasn’t visible, just had a grid pattern with a colored line on it. Have to say tho it was nice to have the map on my wrist when it worked. Fix that so the map is visible 100% of the time, I would give it 5 stars!
author: caq77

title: Amazing App with One Major Flaw
content:
This app is absolutely fantastic. It will help you find amazing local trails and review them for others. It has wonderfully detailed maps and excellent trails all over the world.

However, the amount of battery this app consumes is outrageous. On a 3-4 hour hike, my battery typically starts to die rapidly. It didn’t use to be like this, but on my iPhone 15
Pro it’s absolutely killing my battery. I looked at the battery app on my phone to discover that AllTrails is using up about 33% of my battery on its own, and this was previously not the case.

Not sure what happened, but the app is still easily worth the 100$ asking price. It’s just unfortunate how hard it’s draining my battery currently. 

Oh, and the Apple Watch support is kind of terrible and worthless. My Apple Watch frequently gets “desynced” from my phone (they display different miles and times). The watch needs your iPhone as well, but it would be amazing to have support without needing your phone.

Bring a solar charger on any hike that’s around 9+ miles and you’ll be fine. Although, the performance and battery life consumption used to be better!
author: Cesium06

title: Help, something got broken with the latest update
content: I normally love the app and have logged over 800 miles of hikes — the latest update is terrible and renders the app virtually useless. You cannot bring up a map without cell service, even for a trail downloaded in advance. After opening and closing the app maybe 10 times, turning my phone on and off, etc., it did finally let me record free-form, without loading the trail — I wasn’t able to see any of the maps I had downloaded or any information about the trail. Also, the app will no longer run in the background — every time I opened the camera or another app, AllTrails crashed and more often than not, the recording stopped and had to be restarted. This is on an iPhone 11. Hopefully it gets fixed soon!
author: andreab718

title: Oh! The Places We’ll Go!!! THANKS ALL TRAILS !
content: I stumbled upon this app and it is been a LOT of fun for plotting and planning. I like having my favorites and the ability to create lists to keep them sorted and organized by state. I did a short hike in West Virginia and really used up a lot of my cell phone battery. I am going to see how to just use the GPS only to conserve on that. Also going to upgrade to the PRO as well. So I can print out maps and reference the hike that way. I’m going on vacation to Rapid City South Dakota in August and I am really looking forward to doing some hikes around the Black Hills and Spearfish Canyon, Mount Rushmore, etc and sharing those experiences with my friends and on All Trails! Happy Trails! 🌸🧗‍♀️🚵‍♀️🌄🌅
author: wildflower🌻

title: Almost Perfect!
content:
Absolutely love this app! Makes getting out there so much easier and safe. It would be a great addition to add a feature that senses when you’ve began moving again on the trail, just like it gives you an alert when you’re off-route (which is incredible by the way!). Sometimes I pause it to eat a snack and totally forget to restart it. :( 

A super cool addition just for enjoyment would be a way to have a goal tracker. Such as a hiking miles or elevation gain goals for the month. That’s just extra but I know I would love it!! Thanks for the work on this amazing produc. I use it religiously on my days off. :)
author: Ohh V

title: Basic Trail Info/Support Lacking
content:
I had hoped to use this app and bought into the Pro version. But I’ve come to learn it’s not what I thought it would be. 

While it has basic trail info (stats, other user info, etc) it’s help feature is severely lacking. You have to email them, and if you have lots of questions this can take days. Plus they keep referring you to their FAQ web page, or their web videos. I don’t want to “read” everything. I want a human to ask a question to and be done, not have to go to another page because the first page doesn’t answer my question. Their Support admitted they are a small organization: I say if you’re going to play with the big boys, then you need to be able to keep up. Emailing doesn’t cut it.

Having said that, if they improve on their support I think this could be a really good app. I just don’t think at this point they’re ready.
author: mount10hiker

title: Deleted trails and argumentative customer “service”
content:
ADDENDUM: Your response to my review completely made my point!! Instead of trying to figure out how to fix a problem, you continued to argue your point. My point was: crucial trails are missing from at least one hiking area I know of. It renders Alltrails useless for hiking in Forest Park, Portland. Those trails need to be added back in to the Alltrails layer of your maps. I have just downloaded and begun to use Gaia because their maps do include all of the appropriate trails in that area. If you decide to take action to correct the problem rather than argue, let me know. (My Pro subscription will not be renewed if I can’t trust your maps to include crucial trails, which happen to have names which include “road” or “drive” in them. 

 At some point in the last year, for some reason certain trails— which are labeled as roads, but no longer used as roads, only trails— have been removed from the Alltrails layer and can’t be used to plot any mapping routes (pro account) for offline use or even used to calculate distances because although they are included in the “roads” layer and a few other layers, there are no mileage indicators. You can’t make an offline map using the “roads” layer and even if you could, you have to map it using the freehand mapping tool and plot it little bit by little bit if you don’t want the curvy trails to be recorded as a straight line. A route can’t be plotted automatically using these trails because Alltrails suddenly decided to treat them as non-trails. When I contacted customer service, they were of no help with this. They merely kept insisting that I was mistaken and these trails had never been shown as trails, which is totally false since I’ve plotted many routes along them since I started using Alltrails a number of years ago. 1) Train your customer service people to figure out how something could be improved, not spend their time arguing their point. They did tell me to just use the roads version, which wasn’t helpful. 2) Please put back my trails!!!
author: SCUBACHARI

title: Super useful
content: I love being able to create my own routes wherever I want to go. I’ve created maps for off trail, for biking, for long backpacking trips. What’s really great is the community let’s you know where they found great campsite, and that’s usually one of the hardest things to figure out when you’re going to a new location. Being able to put In waypoints, being able to switch from AllTrails, to USGS maps, to Satellite are features I use consistently. I run a small nonprofit in NC (The American Adventure Service Corps- Lake Norman) that takes kids 8-18 into our wild places and AllTrails is super useful to our mission! Highly recommended.
author: davedenny3

title: Learning to hate this app
content:
1. Used it last week to identify an 8 mile hike. The app shows it by one trail name and as a loop. The loop is actually a set of trails but All Trails does not show this in any way. Had no service on the trail and I had no way of knowing that I was supposed to link to other trails so had to take it out and back so I missed a good portion of the planned hike At least allow us to view all of the trail segments 2. There is no way to look for POIs THAT ARE NOT PARKS. Example, if I know of a good watering hole but not the park name next to it. Would like to use All Trails to choose random watering holes/places to eat and tell me what trails are nearby
3. The website prompts you to open the app over and over and over again. Sometimes you just eant to be on the website!
author: Zpad2

title: Watch app is bad
content:
The app itself is ok outside of freezing and stopping without telling you pretty frequently. I wish there was a feature that would just fill in the gap with your average pace when that happens.

The watch app is terrible however. Always freezing and the compass is useless. It used to be great when it showed the map but they got rid of that for whatever reason and replaced it with a compass that tells you the wrong direction more times than not when it’s not frozen. I wish I could just have the map back on it. 

The whole point of being outside is to be off my phone but I have to constantly check it to make sure it’s still recording or check directions. It was infinite times better when the map was available on the watch.
author: qtrain6

title: PLEASE fix Apple Watch maps
content:
Wearables are so important with hiking. If one uses two hiking poles, you can’t hold your phone the entire hike.  That’s why I invested in the higher AllTrails subscription and an Apple Watch Ultra 2. 

With the Apple Watch Ultra 2, the waypoint on the AllTrails map frequently jumps off the trail. On top of that, zooming in for precision turns is not possible and can get confusing. (I’d rather not have to pull out my phone).  I did open a ticket with AllTrails and haven’t heard back yet regarding the waypoint and GPS being way off. If this problem gets fixed I will update my rating.  I really want this to work!

Other than that important item, this is a fantastic app for planning and hiking; assuming you hold your phone in your hand while hiking.
author: TheChris615

title: Subscription Fees Monthly or Yearly
content:
I’m not paying an ever increasing amount of money for anything as trivial as this. I swear to God Apple should force you to reveal what the actual cost of the app is before the download starts. If I download an app and then it tells me there’s a phony trial period then it’s subscription city, I’m deleting the app and I’m never giving you money and I’m going to all but slander you and your app to anyone who might be interested in it. 

IDK if you’re homeless and you spend all your time in the woods you MIGHT get value from your money here. 

I’m not saying subscription fees for an app like this is a legit scam, but it is usurious in the sense that you will inevitably be paying for something that you aren’t using. They know how many people have forgotten that they pay for this each month and don’t use the app anymore. It’s probably their favorite number. Gross.
author: The Fear of Music

title: I really like the app
content:
The app is pretty great. I use it a fair amount and never have any issues. 
One little thing I think that could be added, is maybe a way to show either the begging AND ends of trails. Sometimes I know the area where the trail ends but no clue where it starts and with longer trails it could be 15-30 miles in any direction where it starts. But if you could have a pin at the end also or add a setting to show the beginnings or ends of trails or maybe even pins for some notable steals like like on the trail where you can click on the pin near the lake, and it’ll show you which trail leads you there.
author: Anyone you want it to be

title: Can’t trust this app
content:
I read the Developer response and did what they said, it cut out in a strange city where I didn’t know where I was going. All I can say is, if you trust this app it will get you killed!

I got lucky, I was close to home and knew the trail, but this app cuts out and you can’t use downloaded maps. All trails cut out while I had good cell reception, so I tried to use the map I had downloaded. When I tried to use the map I had downloaded all that came up was a red line over a blank page. I was in the Marine Corps Infantry and attached to Special Operations, so I know how important it is to have a map and a GPS you can trust, AllTrails isn’t it. The other thing is I’m going to a remote part of Utah, the other GPS app has it, AllTrail doesn’t. What I’ve found is AllTrail cuts out a lot, and it doesn’t have maps for remote areas, what good is it. The worst part is I got suckered into paying $20 for Pro.
author: SemperFi1/5

title: Bricked my phone, twice
content: When it works it’s great. On two separate occasions, out on a trail, it has completely bricked my phone. The app freezes up and I am unable to exit, force quit, force restart, anything. Completely rendered my phone useless on two occasions. No way to call, text, navigate, email, etc… Left me without navigation I stupidly depended on this app. The only way I was able to recover my phone was to let the battery naturally completely drain to the point of shutdown. If it had a full charge that could be days. The only way I could draw power to speed up this process was waking the phone up as it was frozen halfway asleep and then I could wake to use power to up the brightness. THIS HAPPENED TO ME TWICE WITH THIS APP! No other app has ever rendered my phone completely useless. Unreal that an app used for navigation in the wild would do this.
author: meeeezbo

title: Accurate and reliable
content: My favorite hiking app! I live in the blue ridge mountains of North Carolina, so my hiking options are pretty unlimited. I am horrible at putting trail maps into perspective so I love that they put the estimated time it takes. Even though it’s usually way longer than it takes me, it’s nice to know before you go. I also love the active gps, it tells you where you are on the trail even when your service cuts out. This has been a life saver for me as I always think I’m going the right way. The pictures are awesome too! Especially when you don’t know what it’s going to be like at that time of year.
author: 2019aliah

title: Great maps, NOT user friendly
content:
I am not sure I understand all the great reviews.  The maps are superb.  But I think it is confusing and awkward to use.   I generally don’t know what trail I am going to go on when we leave the house and cel phone range. I live in Colorado and would just like to download the entire state.   I don’t care if that takes 10 GB.  But you cannot do that.  

Also once I have downloaded an area with the strange process they gave me (tracing a LARGE hiking route to capture the whole area) then once I start on a route I would expect it to realize what route I am on and show that like “Hiking rainbow lake trail”.   It does not do that.   

I also find it quite buggy.   Hangs up a lot when downloading trails.  FYI I have a new modern i Phone.  Also it is supposed to allow my wife to download the same files, but it never seems to work quite right.   Her resolution is way less than on my identical phone.   Why?   

Last, I have found it to lose signals sometimes so you have gaps in your traced route.  

Overall I love the map details.   But both my wife and I find that it needs some serious improvement.
author: Robegul

title: Easy, quick, helpful!
content: This app just makes it easy for finding ideas on where to hike and getting beta on the current conditions of the trails. My only frustration is that while on trail, the app often closes all the way to the start when I have my phone’s screen off. I often have to wait for the app to load and then reselect the trail all over again to see where I am. Most tracking apps just keep that page and you can immediately see your location when you unlock your phone. It’s a good 20secs waiting for this app to reload and then 3 touches to direct it back to where I was. Other than that annoyance I really like it.
author: Wyred11

title: Needs and Orange Indicator
content:
Very useful app that I’ve used for years now. However, I think this app could get better and more interactive/informative by having somewhere early in the trail description if there is hunting nearby to alert hikers to wear Orange! 
I’ve been looking at a few trails that were found by this app in my state and several of them are near hunting grounds with trailheads that clearly state and warn hikers/bikers to have Orange on you along with the hunting season times. 
Please find a way to have this feature in there. I know this app has been used by many novice hikers now and I’m sure many do not have Orange vests/hats in their cars at all times like I do (crazy nut-case).
Happy trails to everyone!
author: AMWF2021

title: Lia
content: Hands down one of the best apps you could have if you like the outdoors or travel. They provide places and information about it through maps and other people experiences. This app is for people of all activists I use hiking/ walking myself. All the maps I’ve used to guide me have been extremely accurate and easy to follow. Everything you can do for free. You can upgrade to plus if you’d really like. I never thought about it until today so I could download my maps incase I were to lose service but I go alone. I’ve been on several trails I would’ve never found without this app.
author: LiaLob

title: Alltrails will make your PRIVATE 3rd party activities PUBLIC
content:
TLDR: Alltrails makes every activity public by default, even if it’s coming from a linked 3rd party where the activity is private. Nothing clearly shows this when linking 3rd parties, you better read the fine print and check the settings!
—
One day I linked alltrails to my garmin account in hopes of getting routes from alltrails to my garmin smartwatch. That wasn’t a thing, and I forgot about it.

It turns out that when you connect alltrails to garmin, alltrails gets access to all your activities & recordings, even if they’re private. Alltrails also publishes the recordings on their own platform but makes them ALL PUBLIC by default even if they were originally PRIVATE on garmin. Yeah, that completely disregards common sense about user privacy. As a result hundreds of my private garmin activities (think running through my neighborhood) were publicly available to anybody under my alltrails account.

I found out after nearly a year of this and messaged support. They were completely dismissive and essentially told me that I had accepted the ToS and that the behavior was normal and that I had signed up for it and didn’t configure my privacy settings. I can’t argue with that, I didn’t read the fine print and didn’t review settings before connecting the two services.

But it baffles me that they somehow think it’s okay to publish private activities from a 3rd party as public and that this is the DEFAULT behavior of the system. A proper privacy practice is that everything is private by default, period. If I want my stuff public, I’ll make it so. Somehow, that doesn’t bother them.

So one star for not caring about user privacy and for awful and dismissive customer support.
author: Whoodatss

title: Well worth a subscription
content:
I started using All Trails when I took up solo hiking, and it has been well worth it. I always download a copy of the map before every hike. Sometimes trails aren’t well defined in my area, and All Trails gives me peace of mind that I’m literally on the right path. I also share my hike with family every time I go out so they know exactly what trail I’ve taken, which makes me and them feel more confident when I hike on my own. 
My only complaint would be that it is really easy to accidentally turn on tracking on your hike. And that’s it. That is the only complaint I have about this app.
author: Haunted Daffodil

title: I’d have given 5 stars but...
content: I keep having issues with my location. It has my location as a completely different state and I keep getting an error message saying I need to have a data connection to change it, which I do AND I’m on Wi-Fi as well. Furthermore I’m trying to search for a very specific trail by name and I cannot find it on here. I’m wondering if it has something to do with my location..? I’ve searched by town, state and trail name. Other than the issues I’m having today I have gotten a lot of use out of this app. I have found many interesting trails near my house that I didn’t even know existed.
author: Deathmetaljess

title: Most useful app
content: AllTrails has been a total game-changer for me. I’m old-school and always use paper maps for long-distance hikes (still vital), but the motivation I got here has been astounding. I thought I’d hiked them all in my area and AllTrails got me back out exploring and tracking my progress. I use it on every walk and hike, swim and kayaking adventure and love looking back on my favorite memories! My whole family uses it now too, and it has saved me ton of time in finding my back in remote areas. I’ve even been tracking every mile my dog has hiked in his 6 years with me so far. I can’t say enough good things!
author: Andi Sunday

title: My Go-To for Hiking
content: Ive never even thought about using another app. All Trails always has what I’m looking for. Whether it’s a long hike, short walking trail, somewhere to bike, a waterfall or swimming hole—everything, everywhere. Ill even go visit friends and pull up some quick hikes in their state. And then the downloadable offline map is HUGE. My biggest fear is getting lost and Ive never gotten lost using All Trails’ maps. It shows you other’s reviews and photos of the trails, the weather in that area, parking options—it’s phenomenal honestly. I always find the kind of activity and views Im looking for. 10/10 recommend besties;))
author: Katrnia_grace17

title: Was great at one point, but not now.
content:
I’ve used AllTrails for 6 year and logged over 1200 miles. The last two weeks my downloaded maps are no longer working. Today I drove 45 minutes down a dirt road to get to a hike you needed a map just to start. To my surprise, my downloaded map is just green. No directions for anything. Happened in glacier national park two weeks ago.  Had to drive 45 minutes back into town to get cell reception, start my tracking, then drive back just so I had a clue what direction to go. Very disappointed with all the new updates and how poorly the app has been the last year. Going to start trying other apps to see if they are more reliable. 

Thanks for many good years.
author: Dandman311

title: Great functionality!
content: Love the way the app is designed the menus are easy to figure out and UI gives you all the information you'll need. The pro subscription is worth every penny especially with the emergency call functionality. While users improve the platform, its' not like many apps that require more users for its' core functions so you will get maps and information for even remote areas. Anything outdoors, including dual sport motorcycle riding like what I do, is perfect with this app, it does it all pretty well. Outside of a dedicated $300+ garmin, this is the best and does just about as good aside from no satellite coverage.
author: sirticsalot

title: Love this App for Hiking
content: I love to hike and this app is so easy to use. Pick and area and see what’s available, filter for the kind of hike you want to do based on your skill level, the length, and what you want to see (waterfalls, views, mountains, etc). And the reviews are the best part. You can see what other hikers that have done that trail had to say about it, as well as see photos. The other part that is a must have is being able to download the map ahead of time, as there isn’t always service once you're on the mountain and as well marked with blazes as most of the trails are, it’s easy to get off track.
author: LadyKirlis

title: If you hike, you should download this app.
content: I would call myself an experienced hiker. I have scaled rocks and cliffs in Red Rock Canyon to find a waterfall with a toddler in a hiking backpack on my back… and I absolutely LOVE this app. I love discovering trails no matter where I am (I’ve only used it in CA) and tracking our hikes, time, and elevation change is awesome. I love being able to see previous hikers photos of a trail, especially when we bring our kids along, because it lets me know if the trail is doable and also if it’s worthwhile. Love, love, love this app. It’s also amazing for finding running trails, I cannot run on concrete anymore. So that is super helpful.
author: pacificapea

title: Previously a 5-Star Review
content: I’ve been using All Trails for many years and never had complaints. The latest update has made a simple and convenient app to use annoying. Previously, when walking in an area without a formal trail you could start recording with one step. With the latest update the app requires you to go through 3 steps before you can start recording. The problem is, if you don’t have your reading glasses handy or it is very sunny and not easy to see the screen it can be frustrating seeing what you are clicking on. Why do I need to indicate what kind of activity I’m doing when I can summarize at the end? All Trails - simple is better!
author: Wanderlust 084

title: Free Account Rocks !!
content: Love AllTrails !! cons: there are some gps and app glitches when tracking your hikes and occasionally the hike difficulty ratings are skewed. pros: overall the app offers great insight into trail conditions, best time of day/year to hike, length of time, views in different seasons, and more. past hike reviewers leave useful tips like where to park, if bathrooms are available, and may recommend specific equipment like hiking poles for or waterproof shoes. I don’t pay for the premium subscription so I don’t know if the additional perks are worth it, but even just a free account offers everything you need to hit the trails :)
author: 707AJ

title: Am I expecting too much?
content: I love the info provided on the free site, but am a little annoyed that I can only “complete” hikes by recording them. It would also be helpful to have chance to search the trails by area and then difficulty...or vice-versa. It just makes sense to be able to search for future hikes, make and save a list of them...be able to prioritize them, and then mark them as completed. Users could then write a reflection and upload pics and videos to serve as “reviews” and notes for other potential climbers. Then again, maybe I’m expecting too much for free. Or maybe I haven’t played around with the app enough to find what I want yet. I’m still getting acquainted with it. If I’m missing it...it’s probably not user friendly enough for a novice like me.
author: smeister808

title: Fantastic app
content:
This app is amazing! It has become a tool every year for my annual Summer Camping Trip!

It has an effortless user-friendly interface, searching for trails and campsites is easy and suggestions around where you are is nice. The trail information provides easy-to-read ratings and elevation information, and I love all the maps! The feature that allows me to bookmark and folder recorded hikes in years past is particularly appealing.

If I happen to earn a couple more bucks each month sometime soon, I would undoubtedly consider purchasing the full downloadable-maps version!🤘⛺️
author: drumsrthebest

title: App completely fails for real hikers
content: I have been a faithful user of all trails app for many years however not sure what is up the app is now completely useless for real hikes.  Issue #1 is the app completely wipes your battery in a few hours of use I have IPhone 14 hardware with latest upgrades with one hike in about 2 hours my battery was gone and I had to return to start of hike before completing hike.  Issue # 2 happened last hike I had downloaded the map but halfway through the hike all of a sudden AllTrails app could not find the bloody map in search and even with no search term map just disappeared from downloads leaving me mapless deep into an area with no cell coverage.  So completely unacceptable behavior for an app that LITERAL SOLE PURPOSE is to guide me on a bloody hike.  I spend huge on this app and it 1000% failed me multiple times.  Goodbye.
author: M hiker

title: Every lover of the outdoors should have this app!
content: I’ve used this app for the past few years and have recommended it to so many others. It is a wonderful tool for finding new trails, seeing reviews about whether it’s worth the trip, current trail conditions, etc. I’m also a Pro member which comes in handy in allowing me to download maps for offline viewing while tracking my GPS location. That feature definitely came in handy with some of my hikes in Colorado where the cell reception was poor. Thank you to everyone on the All Trails team that helps others explore the outdoors!
author: TroyAnthony1993

title: Needs Better Descriptions
content: I really like the app.  I like the download feature. I have many hikes downloaded and it does a decent job keeping you on track. My biggest issue is that the descriptions do not contain blaze information and you will need to constantly check your phone to make sure you’re on the trail properly.   To me, having both pieces of information keeps you safest on the trail.  I like to know what blaze I’m looking for next as I’m hiking. This seems to be inconsistent for each hike.  Am I going to delete the app over it? No. But it could be better. Until then, do your homework before you hit the trail and know where you’re hiking. Happy trails!
author: Juniperjbird

title: Good app but broken after update to 13.0
content: It was all simple and easy before and now the app got annoying. If you want to start following your map you have to chose activity no matter that the activity is already set in your map. If you want to take a photo along the way you need to: 1. Tap ••• 2. Tap “Add a photo” 3. Tap “Take New Photo” 4. Take a photo 5. Tap “Use Photo” 6. Tap “Save” 7. And the you get annoying “Love the photo” pop-up 7 steps instead for dedicated photo button which will just “Take a photo”. This way taking a photo along your route makes you stop and spend time with the phone instead doing an activity. C’mon developers, make this simpler, or at least leave an option where we can have simpler photo taking process and easier choice of activity.
author: (o)v(o)

title: It’s ok.. when it works
content:
I paid to upgrade so I could track my hikes using my Apple Watch Ultra and it constantly loses my location even when I have the maps downloaded to my phone. It seems to work fine on the actual phone when I pull it out to check but the watch has no clue where I am and actually shows me back at the start of the trail half the time. I had this issue with my previous Apple Watch(5) as well.

Some trails will show up when you search them by name but not by using the “distance away” search. I’ve already paid for a year but wish I had a month to month I could cancel. It’s not worth it to me for the premium features since they don’t seem to work all that well.
author: Jjunior887

title: PLEASE MAKE THIS ONE CHANGE TO THE APP 🙏🏽
content:
This app is soooo good. But one thing I would love to see changed and why I gave only 3 stars, is If they changed their difficulty system from easy, moderate, hard to a 1-10 scale (1 = very easy, 10 = very difficult). 

You find yourself on a moderate hike and there are times when they’re too easy but also times when they’re too hard, but if it had a rating system, you would see 7.5 Moderate, which would lean towards a moderate/hard hike. This would allow people to pick hikes more similar to ones they’ve already done and allow people to challenge themselves and pick hikes with a higher rating for difficulty or lower rating if they’re bringing less experienced friends.
author: J_Moz

title: Freezes
content:
Love this app usually but recently every time I try to look up a trail I have saved it freezes on me! I’m bout to cancel my membership if this doesn’t get fixed asap! It’s a liability! I went on a hike a few weeks ago and had to make my own trail because I couldn’t get to a trail I downloaded without it freezing! I had a heck of a time staying on the trail I wanted because of it! Please fix this!!!!! ♥️🙏🏽♥️

Update: they reached out and I uninstalled and reinstalled and everything is back to normal and everything is still saved! Great customer service! So happy this got resolved! ♥️
author: SnowPrncss

title: Disappointing
content: Over I like the app but there are several major issues. 1. In the last couple updates, the contrast in the UI makes many pages unusable - the actual and planned elevation are unreadable in the sun. Please hire a UX person and test for WCAG compliance. Dark grey text on black background looks cool but doesn’t work. 2. Search for parks and trails is awful. Start entering a park name and the Ap suggests it - good. But results first show a half dozen OTHER parks- the one suggested is in the second or third screen of results. Most results don’t have the keywords anywhere in the name or description. Just prioritize matches in the name. 3. Needs to auto -stop tracking when you forget to turn it off. Yeah I know I’m supposed to do that but if I selected Hiking and am going 30mph, I’m probably not hiking anymore.
author: macsfast69

title: All trail info is crowd-sourced
content: This app is a good starting point to learn what trails may be available in a given area, but users need to realize all of the tracks and descriptions come from other hikers, and more research from other sources is required before hiking in an unfamiliar area. Difficultly ratings are subjective, based on the user’s physical fitness and experience. What is easy for one person, may be difficult for someone else. If a hiker goes off trail, that gets recorded and uploaded, so don’t rely solely on this app. Get a proper trail map and learn how to read it. Record and share your tracks, and write objective trail reviews, with other users in mind. This app will improve only if more users get involved creating content.
author: Bunigrl33

title: Cluttered UI makes it almost unusable now
content:
What happened?  I used to use AllTrails all the time, but now the cluttered user interface makes it almost unusable.  In map/explore mode, a full third of the screen is perpetually blocked by a search input above filter options above mode selection, making it much harder to explore the map!  If you accidentally zoom in so no trailheads are visible, like when you are trying to zoom in on a feature or part of a trail you haven’t selected, half the screen gets blocked by a warning, and you can’t see anything again until you zoom out to make it go away.  These are things that could so easily be fixed to take up less real estate and be toggled visible.  
I’m very disappointed that I’m going to have to find a new app for my hiking when this used to be perfect.
author: Sizzling Syzygy

title: Bait and switch
content: I re-up’d my membership a month or so ago so i could continue to customize existing routes to help me hike since I’m old and disabled and can’t usually manage the established hike. I went to use it a couple days ago and they stopped allowing my membership to use this and require that I pay more to use it. How do they justify advertising and offering an option and then steal it from you once you’ve paid only to extort more money out of you? I’ve written help to get this option back and they’ve ignored me so far. I paid money for this option specifically so if I can’t use it there’s no reason to pay them anything. They’re thieves and scoundrels. Leaving elderly and disabled people already on a budget unable to use their app and stealing their money while not providing the service we bought.
author: Zxasloptc

title: AllTrails Hike
content: We’ve been using AllTrails for almost three years now, and it has become an essential app for hiking and biking, no matter where we travel. AllTrails provides detailed trail maps, difficulty levels, elevation profiles, and real-time reviews from other users, making it easy to find the perfect route for any adventure. The GPS tracking feature helps us stay on course, and the offline maps are a lifesaver in areas with no signal. We’ve also discovered that AllTrails is a great tool for exploring cities in a new and exciting way. It’s a must-have companion for anyone who loves the outdoors!
author: R.Daca

title: Still loving this app!
content: I love this app! Free version will help you find great trails and the paid version will help you stay on the trails. Users leave helpful reviews to help you prepare for your adventure. The paid version breaks down to only a few bucks a month which is totally worth it! This gives you the ability to download the trial in advance which will help keep you on track and navigate areas where the trail is not clear. This app saved me a few times! Another feature I like is the ability to make lists, save your favorite hikes, and keep track of your accomplishments. Great app!
author: HikeHarder

title: Great
content: The AllTrails app is a must-have for any outdoor enthusiast! It offers an extensive collection of trail maps, complete with user reviews and photos that help you choose the perfect hike, bike ride, or running path. The app’s intuitive design makes planning outdoor adventures simple, allowing users to filter trails by difficulty, length, and rating. Its GPS trail maps can be downloaded for offline use, a fantastic feature for areas with limited reception. Whether you're looking for a leisurely nature walk or a challenging mountain trek, AllTrails connects you to the outdoors with confidence and ease. Truly, it’s the ultimate companion for exploring the natural world.
author: macro367

title: App is fine, customer service meh
content: The app in general is a good resource, but when I started paying for the app I couldn’t get my downloaded maps to work when offline, which could obviously be an issue if you are using this as your only resource which I don’t recommend. I reached out to customer service and as they were trying to figure out what was going on I ended up just deleting and then redownloading the app and that worked. This is a common issue based on others experiences on Reddit. Frustrated that they didn’t offer to compensate me for the 8 months the app wasn’t working. They should add a pop up that asks you to offload and reload the app, because the updates didn’t work for me. May shop around and try to find another more reliable app.
author: Kenixena

title: Lost without it
content:
❤️❤️❤️❤️ now that ive had the app its almost as   important as hiking with   one of my limbs not working 😂🙃.When my phone dies or I forget it in the car this is bad as me forgetting to put on my boots in the mud or snow I missed it that much. I don’t want to ever go without the ease n of finding new places to explore being able to go whatever direction with my dog and I feel like I’m not worried about getting lost and able to track how far I made it and how consistent I’ve been . That leads to more motivation to do it more often have pride and being healthy. 
 it’s just all-around so wonderful for me.
author: kAAADoooog

title: Don’t Hike Without It!
content:
Have lost track of the amount of times I have helped lost hikers without this app on their phones by showing it to them while hiking. Love it, with only one minor annoyance on my Apple watch, why is the complication just two small dashes and nothing else? I’d love to be able to indicate duration or distance instead. Thank you!  

Edit: To be clear, I am not referring to the app screens once its open(which I use often as well), but the complication that is displayed on the watch face before launching the app from that complication, simply as “—“ with no metrics or other indicator. 

Thank you for the reply!
author: mistaken113

title: Helpful app
content:
I use this app often to find trails, to learn of trail conditions, distance, scenery etc. ability to download maps is nice even though I rarely have to reference them. 
One thing I ask of the app owners/developers is please notify subscribers when they renew, when they are about to charge you for renewal. the transaction came up as potential fraud and my bank contacted me. Since I had no clue what the transaction was for, I noted it as fraud and am waiting for a new CC now. 
It was the day after the transaction posted that I received notification from Apple (not from All Trails) that I was charged for the All Trails subscription. 
All Trails, please email in advance of renewal.
author: clemags

title: Awesome sauce
content: The only things I would adjust are, I wish there was a drafts folder, so the hike I just finished and wrote a big review and look forward to recording doesn’t delete due to poor reception, which is basically every time I go to the mountains. I’ve done some awesome miles but few are recorded. Also, the trail and gps portion isn’t that accurate. So, if you’re one to relay heavily on the app, because you don’t have a map, you’ll be sharing a lake with bears and coming out with a lot of scratches from bush whacking. . I’m guessing (I’m not this has happened twice). Also, I would like to mark/add my trail rating, if it’s easy-hard. I love a challenge with grand elevation.
author: Amieienop

title: Haven’t died yet!
content:
My partner and I are...  let’s be honest, we’re getting old.  Recognizing that exercise is key in not becoming frail and old, we started walking in the forest... this has since turned to hiking and we’re in surprisingly spry health and energy.

That said, AllTrails has been essential for the last two years.  Finding new trails is simple and has an impressive search and filter system is easy and finds are surprising number of places.

The two caveats I would say are the Record function isn’t always the most accurate.  It gets interesting if you stop and take pictures every few feet.  And the Map is too big and red.  It was will appear as being a straight walk but the trail itself is a few miles of very intense switchbacks.  The topographic and the map itself are pretty accurate though if you want to track your location.

Note that you should NEVER rely on a iPhone with any app if you go into the wilderness!!!  Have and know how to read a map, and a real GPS is important.  Otherwise, this is a great app.
author: Whifton Polekitty

title: Good but key things missing
content:
Overall I like having a trail map that I can follow and not get lost. The reviews help ensure the description matches reality. However I have paid for the full version and still some key things are missing that seem obvious and there’s no way I can find to communicate with the developers. 

The main problem is you can’t download the layers such as waypoints. Most hikes have no cell service so there is no way to access this key feature while you’re on the trail. So all you get is a red line with zero info including the blaze colors you should be looking for. There also no way to contribute to waypoints which would allow users to clarify and update the map for other users. 

The other part I find extremely frustrating is there is no map to show adjoining trails so if you want to switch trails while you’re hiking you won’t have a map. Therefore I can only use this app in conjunction with Avenza meaning I have to pay twice  

I haven’t found a full service map app that combines All Trails and Avenza. Hoping there’s an enthusiast out there working on a good interactive trail map that would be like Waze for hiking.
author: mingum

title: Review for our class
content: The app itself was very accurate as long as there was some kind of cell service.  I had to close out the app and reopen, but it did let me continue where I left off at.  I feel AllTrails is a good hiking app, not sure about paddling or biking but I will try it out on my next paddle outing.  I feel it wasn’t missing anything.  I did enjoy have the compass on my watch to keep walking on the path, it tracked when I was off trail.  I don’t know if you can, but I would like for you to be able to download trails in your local area for free and not have to pay.  All in all a GREAT APP!!!!
author: mchill

title: Going downhill
content: I have been a member for years and a paid subscriber for over 5 years and in the past year or so your app has grown bloated (more clicks to get to what I want, can no longer easily just swipe through photos, too much scrolling to find basic information…), and now the new peak membership is making things worse. You’ve added a bunch of things I don’t need, and I have to maneuver around them to get to what I want. It’s like I am being made a second class citizen for an app I am already paying a lot of money for. À benefit of plus is no ads, and that should include your not pushing your higher tier at me. I am growing so frustrated by this I am starting to look for other options.
author: SuperLightness

title: Love this app!! ❤︎ ♡ ♥︎
content: This app is so convenient when bike riding on trails. It keeps track of everything my time, distance, elevation & calories burned!! It makes my phone a gps map to guide me each mile of the trail so I don’t get lost but while I’m following the trail it has a button to press to take quick pictures while I’m “in motion” riding past a pretty scenery. I can also send my travel data to friends  & we compete on fastest finish time on riding bike. It keeps me motivated to go explore all great wilderness trails & I have lost a lot of weight but having fun at same time!! i ❤︎love❤︎  how they also have a “lifeline” button on screen just in case u need it So genius!!
author: Skillyzzz

title: Going downhill as an app
content: I have used this app for many years, used it while traveling across the country, and loved it for a long time. Now, it’s almost impossible to use. It’s laggy and gets worse as you use it, the search feature and the back button aren’t compatible at all somehow so my searches clear anytime i look at a specific trail, and then want to return to my search list. Start all over, and can’t save your specific search features. I’m glad I’ve never paid for the pro version, i would be floored if i paid for an app that overheats my phone after looking for trails for 15 minutes like it does to mine. The only reason i still use it is bc they basically have a monopoly over trail searching sites that are reliable
author: tttaaayyyyyyyyy

title: DANGEROUS-PSA info is made public
content:
I have used and loved this app for years, until today. I was checking my online security and saw that if you google my name, my All trails profile comes up immediately showing all of my activity on the app, including my profile picture, when I added maps, where my hikes were, and when I completed them. I changed my profile to private to prevent this in the future, and to my dismay, after another google, it revealed ALL OF MY INFORMATION(my picture,
when I added maps, location, etc) even after the app was set to private and all the previously public content was deleted. Please be aware, for safety reasons, your information is being made available to the public WHETHER THE APP IS ON PRIVATE OR NOT. This is very very scary for me as a young woman hiking alone. Please be careful if you use this!!!!
author: brendog1234

title: Newest update bugs
content: Newest update slowed down the app a lot. It seems like taping on a trail or scrolling through trails on the map view of explore is extremely unoptimized for the iPhone 11. No real settings to mess with how trails and trail information is displayed on the map either. Before in previous versions, it only showed the trail in a thin red line which was preferred. Now it’s a very thick line that covers the trail and gives direction arrows which I feel is unnecessary at a cursory glance. Also can’t control how the trails are grouped visually in maps. I loved to open up the completed tab in maps and see all the areas I’ve explored with the pins, but now everything is just grouped in one big number. PLEASE give us the option to adjust these or try to optimize the app, it’s almost unusable with how slow and buggy it is.
author: hiker trash panda

title: Great for Outdoorsy People!
content: Don’t usually leave reviews but I love this app. The maps help so much on trails that may be overgrown or snowed on, the directions function is great because sometimes the location you’re doing to is coordinates, usually up to date with weather and closures, you can see the details of your hikes, record them, etc. There are so many functions and it’s so useful. I use this app to scout out my next hikes, make lists, alert emergency contacts when I’m going into the mountains, plan, everything. This is a must have for people who backpack, back country ski, mountain bike, anything!
author: KyraHedgehog

title: Gone Downhill?
content:
I used to love this program, but on our current vacation in Maine I have experienced issues with (1) the major, maintained trail I am standing on not appearing on the map (I did download the entire park ahead of time), and (2) more seriously, the map showing me significantly off from where I really was - thankfully Apple Maps, of all things, correctly placed me. But these are a couple of things that an outdoor mapping app should get right 100% of the time.

In addition, there seems to be a stronger push for “social” elements.  When I complete a hike, no, I do not want to post a review at that moment. And no, I do not want to tag a friend.  Stop asking me. It actually feels kind of “in your face.” I do not recall this nagging behavior on prior trips.  If this persists I will not be renewing.
author: ADudeinBoston

title: Free version is unusable
content:
I don’t mind having some features locked, but every action I take on this app seems to get interrupted by a modal dialog nagging me to buy for some reason, that I have to dismiss before continuing. I wouldn’t trust this app on a trail where I might actually need the information I was trying to get. 

The general design style of the free app seems to have been to entice users to try to access premium features, then ply them with ads. This may not affect the experience of paid users, but the use of the tactic itself—as opposed to laying out what’s free and what’s paid at the beginning, de-emphasizing paid feature paths in the free app, and letting me see if I like the darn thing—really turns me off paying them on principle. 

Not sure what’s out there as an alternative, paid or free, but I’d rather just use maps and trail guides.
author: Yet another guy named Phil

title: Almost perfect
content: I’ve been doing a lot of hiking this year and use AllTrails to select and track my activity. Downloading the maps ahead of time has been great and their information is accurate. My major issue is with the estimated distances. I’ve been in two major hikes that were severely underestimated. I didn’t deviate from the trail and though I could see my location on the map was nowhere near the end, in each case I had already gone further than the planned distance. On a 8+ mile hike, underestimating by a mile or more is just not cool. I e read plenty of reviews where others have made similar comments so it needs to be addressed.
author: sostuckish

title: Some very frustrating design decisions
content:
Generally a very good app, although if you want to manage lists of trails it can be frustrating. The experience around saving trails is very poorly thought out and occasionally buggy. Saving a trail to multiple lists requires two taps for each, and waiting for a menu to open and close as the change is saved. 

Additionally, the app is very spammy if you don't pay for it, often popping up prompts to purchase a subscription right when I go to start a hike. I would be happy to pay for it if I could manage lists more easily, but right now it just isn't worth it.

Still the best hiking app out there!
author: emmattention

title: New version is a disaster
content: I have had a paid membership for several years and use to love the app to record my hikes. Never had a problem with the recording crashing during a hike before, but twice in the last week it has just stopped midway through a hike. Normally I keep my phone safely in my pack while on the trail so it is frustrating to get to the end of a hike and learn I don’t have a record of my route. Customer service told me I should only take pictures from the app, and have no other apps running, but I wasn’t taking pictures or running other apps when the navigation just quit. The only other advice they offered was to check while hiking to make sure the app hasn’t stopped. Sure, stopping every few hundred yards, getting my phone out and checking an app is a sure way to enjoy a hike. NOT.
author: Jend13

title: I’m so thankful I had this app!!
content: So i already loves the app, when I was finally able to take a hike I had planned on the app, I used the map of the trail I was on.  The trail wasn’t well marked so when we hit what we thought was a fork we went right.  Unfortunately it wasn’t a fork but a dried up water way.  I checked my map again and saw we were pretty far off the trail. I had my 3yo with me so it could have been disastrous. Once we turned back and got to the trail...my blue dot showed me I was back on coarse.  I love how the searches work and love how I can save trails to lists.  Still figuring out all of the bells and whistles, but I can say this...I will never hike without it.
author: hikewithme2015

title: The hiking app I’ve been looking for
content:
This app allows me the have a GPS on my phone overlaid on the topo lines, showing the route others have taken and my present location.  It also shows the elevation profile. Plus it works without an internet or phone connection.  

There’s even a rangefinder that shows the “crow fly” distance to any point you chose on the map. 

There is a database of 50k plus hikes to chose from and this can be filtered in various ways. You can save any of these to your “favorites” list and arrange them in any order you like. 

And I can take photos and track my completed hikes along with basic stats.  And I get a map showing all my completed and planned hikes

I just recently discovered I can also organize the hikes I want to do by making a “list”.  This feature allows you to geographically (or any other feature) organize you hikes.  For example I’ve created a list of hikes along the Blue Ridge Parkway.  This allows me to quickly separate those hikes from Colorado (for example)
author: Justin engineer

title: Junk
content: I downloaded this app on my galaxy and bought a year long subscription for $30 after logging In with my gmail account. After completing the purchase the app informed me that I was charged for the subscription, but wasn’t able to get access to the subscriber features and to contact support. So I wrote support an email and went to the online help after trying everything I could for about 30 minutes. The help suggested I log out of the app and log back in. I logged out and was never able to log back in because the app couldn’t connect with google even though I had a perfect internet connection. I restarted the phone, uninstalled the app and reinstalled it and nothing worked so I figured I’d download it on my iPhone. It still doesn’t work and gives the same error. Fastest $30 I ever wasted. Save your time and money and find another app.
author: J-maxx

title: L❤️VE THIS APP!
content: This app is so handy. The search features are amazing - allowing you to use filters for different preferred attributes. It provides a weather forecast for the day/time you plan to hike. It provides a link to driving directions to the trailhead. You can look at recent photos of the hike, or by season, so you know what to expect and look forward to. My favorite part is the ability to download a trail map and have it follow you in real time to keep you on track. It has saved me many times from taking a wrong turn and has provided me peace of mind that I won’t get lost.
author: EEEJJJDDD

title: An Exceptional App - Last Update Is Much Improved
content: The app is one of you go to and must have apps as a avid hiker I really love all these features and use it when I’m traveling around the world when I’m planning a hike or planning an impromptu hike. I’ve been a Pro member for about five to six years and love some of the features including downloadable maps, navigation tracker and lifeline which is key when hiking in the remote areas that I do. I really like the last update when the 3D simulation hikes when introduced. For now, I intend to keep the subscription because it’s so useful and I use it constantly.
author: PennCCRN

title: Lost but found
content: I remember the year 2013 my buddy and I were trying to find water falls and any other cool stuff while having a whole day to do whatever we wanted. We managed to sorta find one waterfall off google but it was definitely a bust. The rest the day was fun but we never found anything we originally planned for. With all trails I have never gotten lost or haven’t found what I wanted to see in any geographical location since then. I love it and it has helped me find easily sooooo many spots! Probably been using it since the app started and i don’t travel without it ready.
author: 6 starr

title: Needs minor change
content:
Over all this app is great. I particularly like the map following feature and all the “obscure” trails that lead you through local neighborhoods. Lots of good detailed info to keep you on track with the trail. 
The only improvement I’d ask for is to remove the required feature to rate your event when done. Every time I “finish” an event I am required to rate that event. Make this an option instead of a requirement.
We do many of the same exact walks over and over again so having to rate it each time is a waste of time. Plus I don’t feel the need or see the advantage to rate every walk/event you take using the app.
author: ChrisOR83

title: Good app. Suggestion for another feature
content: I like the app and it’s super useful when out on trails.  But I have a request for them to add a feature. On a trail yesterday we stumbled upon an angry yellow jacket nest. It would be useful to add a feature to where you can add a warning at that location for something like this that other people on the trail can see. We saw another group walk right through it after us. Please add some way we can add a hazard to the trail that could notify others also on the trail or alert people when choosing or starting the trail. It could also be used for animal sighting or good things like rare flowers blooming to look out for.
author: tnt_3149

title: Decent little app
content:
I have been using All Trails for a few years now. For the most part I like it, but I wish it was faster to detect that routes have changed. If enough people are going “off route” in the same area, and take the same path to get back on route, that should be a hint to the system that something may have changed.
I also wish they would make a version that works with an iPad. I understand that very few people are taking their iPad on trail, but some of us would like to do our off-trail planning on an iPad as opposed to our phone.
All-in-all, I still like this app and use it almost as much as I use Gaia GPS for hiking.
author: Stevenhacker

title: Great app but…
content: I love this app, I’m able to get so much hiking done with this app. There’s just one thing that’s pretty frustrating. I had to delete a lot of my hikes I recorded because I forget to end the hike and then I drive all the way to my house. I don’t want no one to know where I live, plus now the stats are inaccurate. It’s frustrating when that happens. I gave the app 2 stars because there are apps like Strava that let you shorten the distance you went. Like why doesn’t all trails have that feature.😭 I gave it 2 stars because that’s how it feels after doing a 10 mile hike but forgetting to end it, so I drive all the way to my house. If only I was able to shorten that part so I didn’t have to delete the whole hike. This happened to me multiple times.
author: TestAnApp

title: Great functionality!
content: Love the way the app is designed the menus are easy to figure out and UI gives you all the information you'll need. The pro subscription is worth every penny especially with the emergency call functionality. While users improve the platform, its' not like many apps that require more users for its' core functions so you will get maps and information for even remote areas. Anything outdoors, including dual sport motorcycle riding like what I do, is perfect with this app, it does it all pretty well. Outside of a dedicated $300+ garmin, this is the best and does just about as good aside from no satellite coverage.
author: sirticsalot

title: Love this App for Hiking
content: I love to hike and this app is so easy to use. Pick and area and see what’s available, filter for the kind of hike you want to do based on your skill level, the length, and what you want to see (waterfalls, views, mountains, etc). And the reviews are the best part. You can see what other hikers that have done that trail had to say about it, as well as see photos. The other part that is a must have is being able to download the map ahead of time, as there isn’t always service once you're on the mountain and as well marked with blazes as most of the trails are, it’s easy to get off track.
author: LadyKirlis

title: If you hike, you should download this app.
content: I would call myself an experienced hiker. I have scaled rocks and cliffs in Red Rock Canyon to find a waterfall with a toddler in a hiking backpack on my back… and I absolutely LOVE this app. I love discovering trails no matter where I am (I’ve only used it in CA) and tracking our hikes, time, and elevation change is awesome. I love being able to see previous hikers photos of a trail, especially when we bring our kids along, because it lets me know if the trail is doable and also if it’s worthwhile. Love, love, love this app. It’s also amazing for finding running trails, I cannot run on concrete anymore. So that is super helpful.
author: pacificapea

title: Previously a 5-Star Review
content: I’ve been using All Trails for many years and never had complaints. The latest update has made a simple and convenient app to use annoying. Previously, when walking in an area without a formal trail you could start recording with one step. With the latest update the app requires you to go through 3 steps before you can start recording. The problem is, if you don’t have your reading glasses handy or it is very sunny and not easy to see the screen it can be frustrating seeing what you are clicking on. Why do I need to indicate what kind of activity I’m doing when I can summarize at the end? All Trails - simple is better!
author: Wanderlust 084

title: Free Account Rocks !!
content: Love AllTrails !! cons: there are some gps and app glitches when tracking your hikes and occasionally the hike difficulty ratings are skewed. pros: overall the app offers great insight into trail conditions, best time of day/year to hike, length of time, views in different seasons, and more. past hike reviewers leave useful tips like where to park, if bathrooms are available, and may recommend specific equipment like hiking poles for or waterproof shoes. I don’t pay for the premium subscription so I don’t know if the additional perks are worth it, but even just a free account offers everything you need to hit the trails :)
author: 707AJ

title: Am I expecting too much?
content: I love the info provided on the free site, but am a little annoyed that I can only “complete” hikes by recording them. It would also be helpful to have chance to search the trails by area and then difficulty...or vice-versa. It just makes sense to be able to search for future hikes, make and save a list of them...be able to prioritize them, and then mark them as completed. Users could then write a reflection and upload pics and videos to serve as “reviews” and notes for other potential climbers. Then again, maybe I’m expecting too much for free. Or maybe I haven’t played around with the app enough to find what I want yet. I’m still getting acquainted with it. If I’m missing it...it’s probably not user friendly enough for a novice like me.
author: smeister808

title: Fantastic app
content:
This app is amazing! It has become a tool every year for my annual Summer Camping Trip!

It has an effortless user-friendly interface, searching for trails and campsites is easy and suggestions around where you are is nice. The trail information provides easy-to-read ratings and elevation information, and I love all the maps! The feature that allows me to bookmark and folder recorded hikes in years past is particularly appealing.

If I happen to earn a couple more bucks each month sometime soon, I would undoubtedly consider purchasing the full downloadable-maps version!🤘⛺️
author: drumsrthebest

title: App completely fails for real hikers
content: I have been a faithful user of all trails app for many years however not sure what is up the app is now completely useless for real hikes.  Issue #1 is the app completely wipes your battery in a few hours of use I have IPhone 14 hardware with latest upgrades with one hike in about 2 hours my battery was gone and I had to return to start of hike before completing hike.  Issue # 2 happened last hike I had downloaded the map but halfway through the hike all of a sudden AllTrails app could not find the bloody map in search and even with no search term map just disappeared from downloads leaving me mapless deep into an area with no cell coverage.  So completely unacceptable behavior for an app that LITERAL SOLE PURPOSE is to guide me on a bloody hike.  I spend huge on this app and it 1000% failed me multiple times.  Goodbye.
author: M hiker

title: Every lover of the outdoors should have this app!
content: I’ve used this app for the past few years and have recommended it to so many others. It is a wonderful tool for finding new trails, seeing reviews about whether it’s worth the trip, current trail conditions, etc. I’m also a Pro member which comes in handy in allowing me to download maps for offline viewing while tracking my GPS location. That feature definitely came in handy with some of my hikes in Colorado where the cell reception was poor. Thank you to everyone on the All Trails team that helps others explore the outdoors!
author: TroyAnthony1993

title: Needs Better Descriptions
content: I really like the app.  I like the download feature. I have many hikes downloaded and it does a decent job keeping you on track.
