My biggest issue is that the descriptions do not contain blaze information and you will need to constantly check your phone to make sure you’re on the trail properly.   To me, having both pieces of information keeps you safest on the trail.  I like to know what blaze I’m looking for next as I’m hiking. This seems to be inconsistent for each hike.  Am I going to delete the app over it? No. But it could be better. Until then, do your homework before you hit the trail and know where you’re hiking. Happy trails!
author: Juniperjbird

title: Good app but broken after update to 13.0
content: It was all simple and easy before and now the app got annoying. If you want to start following your map you have to chose activity no matter that the activity is already set in your map. If you want to take a photo along the way you need to: 1. Tap ••• 2. Tap “Add a photo” 3. Tap “Take New Photo” 4. Take a photo 5. Tap “Use Photo” 6. Tap “Save” 7. And the you get annoying “Love the photo” pop-up 7 steps instead for dedicated photo button which will just “Take a photo”. This way taking a photo along your route makes you stop and spend time with the phone instead doing an activity. C’mon developers, make this simpler, or at least leave an option where we can have simpler photo taking process and easier choice of activity.
author: (o)v(o)

title: It’s ok.. when it works
content:
I paid to upgrade so I could track my hikes using my Apple Watch Ultra and it constantly loses my location even when I have the maps downloaded to my phone. It seems to work fine on the actual phone when I pull it out to check but the watch has no clue where I am and actually shows me back at the start of the trail half the time. I had this issue with my previous Apple Watch(5) as well.

Some trails will show up when you search them by name but not by using the “distance away” search. I’ve already paid for a year but wish I had a month to month I could cancel. It’s not worth it to me for the premium features since they don’t seem to work all that well.
author: Jjunior887

title: PLEASE MAKE THIS ONE CHANGE TO THE APP 🙏🏽
content:
This app is soooo good. But one thing I would love to see changed and why I gave only 3 stars, is If they changed their difficulty system from easy, moderate, hard to a 1-10 scale (1 = very easy, 10 = very difficult). 

You find yourself on a moderate hike and there are times when they’re too easy but also times when they’re too hard, but if it had a rating system, you would see 7.5 Moderate, which would lean towards a moderate/hard hike. This would allow people to pick hikes more similar to ones they’ve already done and allow people to challenge themselves and pick hikes with a higher rating for difficulty or lower rating if they’re bringing less experienced friends.
author: J_Moz

title: Freezes
content:
Love this app usually but recently every time I try to look up a trail I have saved it freezes on me! I’m bout to cancel my membership if this doesn’t get fixed asap! It’s a liability! I went on a hike a few weeks ago and had to make my own trail because I couldn’t get to a trail I downloaded without it freezing! I had a heck of a time staying on the trail I wanted because of it! Please fix this!!!!! ♥️🙏🏽♥️

Update: they reached out and I uninstalled and reinstalled and everything is back to normal and everything is still saved! Great customer service! So happy this got resolved! ♥️
author: SnowPrncss

title: Disappointing
content: Over I like the app but there are several major issues. 1. In the last couple updates, the contrast in the UI makes many pages unusable - the actual and planned elevation are unreadable in the sun. Please hire a UX person and test for WCAG compliance. Dark grey text on black background looks cool but doesn’t work. 2. Search for parks and trails is awful. Start entering a park name and the Ap suggests it - good. But results first show a half dozen OTHER parks- the one suggested is in the second or third screen of results. Most results don’t have the keywords anywhere in the name or description. Just prioritize matches in the name. 3. Needs to auto -stop tracking when you forget to turn it off. Yeah I know I’m supposed to do that but if I selected Hiking and am going 30mph, I’m probably not hiking anymore.
author: macsfast69

title: All trail info is crowd-sourced
content: This app is a good starting point to learn what trails may be available in a given area, but users need to realize all of the tracks and descriptions come from other hikers, and more research from other sources is required before hiking in an unfamiliar area. Difficultly ratings are subjective, based on the user’s physical fitness and experience. What is easy for one person, may be difficult for someone else. If a hiker goes off trail, that gets recorded and uploaded, so don’t rely solely on this app. Get a proper trail map and learn how to read it. Record and share your tracks, and write objective trail reviews, with other users in mind. This app will improve only if more users get involved creating content.
author: Bunigrl33

title: Cluttered UI makes it almost unusable now
content:
What happened?  I used to use AllTrails all the time, but now the cluttered user interface makes it almost unusable.  In map/explore mode, a full third of the screen is perpetually blocked by a search input above filter options above mode selection, making it much harder to explore the map!  If you accidentally zoom in so no trailheads are visible, like when you are trying to zoom in on a feature or part of a trail you haven’t selected, half the screen gets blocked by a warning, and you can’t see anything again until you zoom out to make it go away.  These are things that could so easily be fixed to take up less real estate and be toggled visible.  
I’m very disappointed that I’m going to have to find a new app for my hiking when this used to be perfect.
author: Sizzling Syzygy

title: Bait and switch
content: I re-up’d my membership a month or so ago so i could continue to customize existing routes to help me hike since I’m old and disabled and can’t usually manage the established hike. I went to use it a couple days ago and they stopped allowing my membership to use this and require that I pay more to use it. How do they justify advertising and offering an option and then steal it from you once you’ve paid only to extort more money out of you? I’ve written help to get this option back and they’ve ignored me so far. I paid money for this option specifically so if I can’t use it there’s no reason to pay them anything. They’re thieves and scoundrels. Leaving elderly and disabled people already on a budget unable to use their app and stealing their money while not providing the service we bought.
author: Zxasloptc

title: AllTrails Hike
content: We’ve been using AllTrails for almost three years now, and it has become an essential app for hiking and biking, no matter where we travel. AllTrails provides detailed trail maps, difficulty levels, elevation profiles, and real-time reviews from other users, making it easy to find the perfect route for any adventure. The GPS tracking feature helps us stay on course, and the offline maps are a lifesaver in areas with no signal. We’ve also discovered that AllTrails is a great tool for exploring cities in a new and exciting way. It’s a must-have companion for anyone who loves the outdoors!
author: R.Daca

title: Still loving this app!
content: I love this app! Free version will help you find great trails and the paid version will help you stay on the trails. Users leave helpful reviews to help you prepare for your adventure. The paid version breaks down to only a few bucks a month which is totally worth it! This gives you the ability to download the trial in advance which will help keep you on track and navigate areas where the trail is not clear. This app saved me a few times! Another feature I like is the ability to make lists, save your favorite hikes, and keep track of your accomplishments. Great app!
author: HikeHarder

title: Great
content: The AllTrails app is a must-have for any outdoor enthusiast! It offers an extensive collection of trail maps, complete with user reviews and photos that help you choose the perfect hike, bike ride, or running path. The app’s intuitive design makes planning outdoor adventures simple, allowing users to filter trails by difficulty, length, and rating. Its GPS trail maps can be downloaded for offline use, a fantastic feature for areas with limited reception. Whether you're looking for a leisurely nature walk or a challenging mountain trek, AllTrails connects you to the outdoors with confidence and ease. Truly, it’s the ultimate companion for exploring the natural world.
author: macro367

title: App is fine, customer service meh
content: The app in general is a good resource, but when I started paying for the app I couldn’t get my downloaded maps to work when offline, which could obviously be an issue if you are using this as your only resource which I don’t recommend. I reached out to customer service and as they were trying to figure out what was going on I ended up just deleting and then redownloading the app and that worked. This is a common issue based on others experiences on Reddit. Frustrated that they didn’t offer to compensate me for the 8 months the app wasn’t working. They should add a pop up that asks you to offload and reload the app, because the updates didn’t work for me. May shop around and try to find another more reliable app.
author: Kenixena

title: Lost without it
content:
❤️❤️❤️❤️ now that ive had the app its almost as   important as hiking with   one of my limbs not working 😂🙃.When my phone dies or I forget it in the car this is bad as me forgetting to put on my boots in the mud or snow I missed it that much. I don’t want to ever go without the ease n of finding new places to explore being able to go whatever direction with my dog and I feel like I’m not worried about getting lost and able to track how far I made it and how consistent I’ve been . That leads to more motivation to do it more often have pride and being healthy. 
 it’s just all-around so wonderful for me.
author: kAAADoooog

title: Don’t Hike Without It!
content:
Have lost track of the amount of times I have helped lost hikers without this app on their phones by showing it to them while hiking. Love it, with only one minor annoyance on my Apple watch, why is the complication just two small dashes and nothing else? I’d love to be able to indicate duration or distance instead. Thank you!  

Edit: To be clear, I am not referring to the app screens once its open(which I use often as well), but the complication that is displayed on the watch face before launching the app from that complication, simply as “—“ with no metrics or other indicator. 

Thank you for the reply!
author: mistaken113

title: Helpful app
content:
I use this app often to find trails, to learn of trail conditions, distance, scenery etc. ability to download maps is nice even though I rarely have to reference them. 
One thing I ask of the app owners/developers is please notify subscribers when they renew, when they are about to charge you for renewal. the transaction came up as potential fraud and my bank contacted me. Since I had no clue what the transaction was for, I noted it as fraud and am waiting for a new CC now. 
It was the day after the transaction posted that I received notification from Apple (not from All Trails) that I was charged for the All Trails subscription. 
All Trails, please email in advance of renewal.
author: clemags

title: Awesome sauce
content: The only things I would adjust are, I wish there was a drafts folder, so the hike I just finished and wrote a big review and look forward to recording doesn’t delete due to poor reception, which is basically every time I go to the mountains. I’ve done some awesome miles but few are recorded. Also, the trail and gps portion isn’t that accurate. So, if you’re one to relay heavily on the app, because you don’t have a map, you’ll be sharing a lake with bears and coming out with a lot of scratches from bush whacking. . I’m guessing (I’m not this has happened twice). Also, I would like to mark/add my trail rating, if it’s easy-hard. I love a challenge with grand elevation.
author: Amieienop

title: Haven’t died yet!
content:
My partner and I are...  let’s be honest, we’re getting old.  Recognizing that exercise is key in not becoming frail and old, we started walking in the forest... this has since turned to hiking and we’re in surprisingly spry health and energy.

That said, AllTrails has been essential for the last two years.  Finding new trails is simple and has an impressive search and filter system is easy and finds are surprising number of places.

The two caveats I would say are the Record function isn’t always the most accurate.  It gets interesting if you stop and take pictures every few feet.  And the Map is too big and red.  It was will appear as being a straight walk but the trail itself is a few miles of very intense switchbacks.  The topographic and the map itself are pretty accurate though if you want to track your location.

Note that you should NEVER rely on a iPhone with any app if you go into the wilderness!!!  Have and know how to read a map, and a real GPS is important.  Otherwise, this is a great app.
author: Whifton Polekitty

title: Good but key things missing
content:
Overall I like having a trail map that I can follow and not get lost. The reviews help ensure the description matches reality. However I have paid for the full version and still some key things are missing that seem obvious and there’s no way I can find to communicate with the developers. 

The main problem is you can’t download the layers such as waypoints. Most hikes have no cell service so there is no way to access this key feature while you’re on the trail. So all you get is a red line with zero info including the blaze colors you should be looking for. There also no way to contribute to waypoints which would allow users to clarify and update the map for other users. 

The other part I find extremely frustrating is there is no map to show adjoining trails so if you want to switch trails while you’re hiking you won’t have a map. Therefore I can only use this app in conjunction with Avenza meaning I have to pay twice  

I haven’t found a full service map app that combines All Trails and Avenza. Hoping there’s an enthusiast out there working on a good interactive trail map that would be like Waze for hiking.
author: mingum

title: Review for our class
content: The app itself was very accurate as long as there was some kind of cell service.  I had to close out the app and reopen, but it did let me continue where I left off at.  I feel AllTrails is a good hiking app, not sure about paddling or biking but I will try it out on my next paddle outing.  I feel it wasn’t missing anything.  I did enjoy have the compass on my watch to keep walking on the path, it tracked when I was off trail.  I don’t know if you can, but I would like for you to be able to download trails in your local area for free and not have to pay.  All in all a GREAT APP!!!!
author: mchill

title: Going downhill
content: I have been a member for years and a paid subscriber for over 5 years and in the past year or so your app has grown bloated (more clicks to get to what I want, can no longer easily just swipe through photos, too much scrolling to find basic information…), and now the new peak membership is making things worse. You’ve added a bunch of things I don’t need, and I have to maneuver around them to get to what I want. It’s like I am being made a second class citizen for an app I am already paying a lot of money for. À benefit of plus is no ads, and that should include your not pushing your higher tier at me. I am growing so frustrated by this I am starting to look for other options.
author: SuperLightness

title: Love this app!! ❤︎ ♡ ♥︎
content: This app is so convenient when bike riding on trails. It keeps track of everything my time, distance, elevation & calories burned!! It makes my phone a gps map to guide me each mile of the trail so I don’t get lost but while I’m following the trail it has a button to press to take quick pictures while I’m “in motion” riding past a pretty scenery. I can also send my travel data to friends  & we compete on fastest finish time on riding bike. It keeps me motivated to go explore all great wilderness trails & I have lost a lot of weight but having fun at same time!! i ❤︎love❤︎  how they also have a “lifeline” button on screen just in case u need it So genius!!
author: Skillyzzz

title: Going downhill as an app
content: I have used this app for many years, used it while traveling across the country, and loved it for a long time. Now, it’s almost impossible to use. It’s laggy and gets worse as you use it, the search feature and the back button aren’t compatible at all somehow so my searches clear anytime i look at a specific trail, and then want to return to my search list. Start all over, and can’t save your specific search features. I’m glad I’ve never paid for the pro version, i would be floored if i paid for an app that overheats my phone after looking for trails for 15 minutes like it does to mine. The only reason i still use it is bc they basically have a monopoly over trail searching sites that are reliable
author: tttaaayyyyyyyyy

title: DANGEROUS-PSA info is made public
content:
I have used and loved this app for years, until today. I was checking my online security and saw that if you google my name, my All trails profile comes up immediately showing all of my activity on the app, including my profile picture, when I added maps, where my hikes were, and when I completed them. I changed my profile to private to prevent this in the future, and to my dismay, after another google, it revealed ALL OF MY INFORMATION(my picture,
when I added maps, location, etc) even after the app was set to private and all the previously public content was deleted. Please be aware, for safety reasons, your information is being made available to the public WHETHER THE APP IS ON PRIVATE OR NOT. This is very very scary for me as a young woman hiking alone. Please be careful if you use this!!!!
author: brendog1234

title: Newest update bugs
content: Newest update slowed down the app a lot. It seems like taping on a trail or scrolling through trails on the map view of explore is extremely unoptimized for the iPhone 11. No real settings to mess with how trails and trail information is displayed on the map either. Before in previous versions, it only showed the trail in a thin red line which was preferred. Now it’s a very thick line that covers the trail and gives direction arrows which I feel is unnecessary at a cursory glance. Also can’t control how the trails are grouped visually in maps. I loved to open up the completed tab in maps and see all the areas I’ve explored with the pins, but now everything is just grouped in one big number. PLEASE give us the option to adjust these or try to optimize the app, it’s almost unusable with how slow and buggy it is.
author: hiker trash panda

title: Great for Outdoorsy People!
content: Don’t usually leave reviews but I love this app. The maps help so much on trails that may be overgrown or snowed on, the directions function is great because sometimes the location you’re doing to is coordinates, usually up to date with weather and closures, you can see the details of your hikes, record them, etc. There are so many functions and it’s so useful. I use this app to scout out my next hikes, make lists, alert emergency contacts when I’m going into the mountains, plan, everything. This is a must have for people who backpack, back country ski, mountain bike, anything!
author: KyraHedgehog

title: Gone Downhill?
content:
I used to love this program, but on our current vacation in Maine I have experienced issues with (1) the major, maintained trail I am standing on not appearing on the map (I did download the entire park ahead of time), and (2) more seriously, the map showing me significantly off from where I really was - thankfully Apple Maps, of all things, correctly placed me. But these are a couple of things that an outdoor mapping app should get right 100% of the time.

In addition, there seems to be a stronger push for “social” elements.  When I complete a hike, no, I do not want to post a review at that moment. And no, I do not want to tag a friend.  Stop asking me. It actually feels kind of “in your face.” I do not recall this nagging behavior on prior trips.  If this persists I will not be renewing.
author: ADudeinBoston

title: Free version is unusable
content:
I don’t mind having some features locked, but every action I take on this app seems to get interrupted by a modal dialog nagging me to buy for some reason, that I have to dismiss before continuing. I wouldn’t trust this app on a trail where I might actually need the information I was trying to get. 

The general design style of the free app seems to have been to entice users to try to access premium features, then ply them with ads. This may not affect the experience of paid users, but the use of the tactic itself—as opposed to laying out what’s free and what’s paid at the beginning, de-emphasizing paid feature paths in the free app, and letting me see if I like the darn thing—really turns me off paying them on principle. 

Not sure what’s out there as an alternative, paid or free, but I’d rather just use maps and trail guides.
author: Yet another guy named Phil

title: Almost perfect
content: I’ve been doing a lot of hiking this year and use AllTrails to select and track my activity. Downloading the maps ahead of time has been great and their information is accurate. My major issue is with the estimated distances. I’ve been in two major hikes that were severely underestimated. I didn’t deviate from the trail and though I could see my location on the map was nowhere near the end, in each case I had already gone further than the planned distance. On a 8+ mile hike, underestimating by a mile or more is just not cool. I e read plenty of reviews where others have made similar comments so it needs to be addressed.
author: sostuckish

title: Some very frustrating design decisions
content:
Generally a very good app, although if you want to manage lists of trails it can be frustrating. The experience around saving trails is very poorly thought out and occasionally buggy. Saving a trail to multiple lists requires two taps for each, and waiting for a menu to open and close as the change is saved. 

Additionally, the app is very spammy if you don't pay for it, often popping up prompts to purchase a subscription right when I go to start a hike. I would be happy to pay for it if I could manage lists more easily, but right now it just isn't worth it.

Still the best hiking app out there!
author: emmattention

title: New version is a disaster
content: I have had a paid membership for several years and use to love the app to record my hikes. Never had a problem with the recording crashing during a hike before, but twice in the last week it has just stopped midway through a hike. Normally I keep my phone safely in my pack while on the trail so it is frustrating to get to the end of a hike and learn I don’t have a record of my route. Customer service told me I should only take pictures from the app, and have no other apps running, but I wasn’t taking pictures or running other apps when the navigation just quit. The only other advice they offered was to check while hiking to make sure the app hasn’t stopped. Sure, stopping every few hundred yards, getting my phone out and checking an app is a sure way to enjoy a hike. NOT.
author: Jend13

title: I’m so thankful I had this app!!
content: So i already loves the app, when I was finally able to take a hike I had planned on the app, I used the map of the trail I was on.  The trail wasn’t well marked so when we hit what we thought was a fork we went right.  Unfortunately it wasn’t a fork but a dried up water way.  I checked my map again and saw we were pretty far off the trail. I had my 3yo with me so it could have been disastrous. Once we turned back and got to the trail...my blue dot showed me I was back on coarse.  I love how the searches work and love how I can save trails to lists.  Still figuring out all of the bells and whistles, but I can say this...I will never hike without it.
author: hikewithme2015

title: The hiking app I’ve been looking for
content:
This app allows me the have a GPS on my phone overlaid on the topo lines, showing the route others have taken and my present location.  It also shows the elevation profile. Plus it works without an internet or phone connection.  

There’s even a rangefinder that shows the “crow fly” distance to any point you chose on the map. 

There is a database of 50k plus hikes to chose from and this can be filtered in various ways. You can save any of these to your “favorites” list and arrange them in any order you like. 

And I can take photos and track my completed hikes along with basic stats.  And I get a map showing all my completed and planned hikes

I just recently discovered I can also organize the hikes I want to do by making a “list”.  This feature allows you to geographically (or any other feature) organize you hikes.  For example I’ve created a list of hikes along the Blue Ridge Parkway.  This allows me to quickly separate those hikes from Colorado (for example)
author: Justin engineer

title: Junk
content: I downloaded this app on my galaxy and bought a year long subscription for $30 after logging In with my gmail account. After completing the purchase the app informed me that I was charged for the subscription, but wasn’t able to get access to the subscriber features and to contact support. So I wrote support an email and went to the online help after trying everything I could for about 30 minutes. The help suggested I log out of the app and log back in. I logged out and was never able to log back in because the app couldn’t connect with google even though I had a perfect internet connection. I restarted the phone, uninstalled the app and reinstalled it and nothing worked so I figured I’d download it on my iPhone. It still doesn’t work and gives the same error. Fastest $30 I ever wasted. Save your time and money and find another app.
author: J-maxx

title: L❤️VE THIS APP!
content: This app is so handy. The search features are amazing - allowing you to use filters for different preferred attributes. It provides a weather forecast for the day/time you plan to hike. It provides a link to driving directions to the trailhead. You can look at recent photos of the hike, or by season, so you know what to expect and look forward to. My favorite part is the ability to download a trail map and have it follow you in real time to keep you on track. It has saved me many times from taking a wrong turn and has provided me peace of mind that I won’t get lost.
author: EEEJJJDDD

title: An Exceptional App - Last Update Is Much Improved
content: The app is one of you go to and must have apps as a avid hiker I really love all these features and use it when I’m traveling around the world when I’m planning a hike or planning an impromptu hike. I’ve been a Pro member for about five to six years and love some of the features including downloadable maps, navigation tracker and lifeline which is key when hiking in the remote areas that I do. I really like the last update when the 3D simulation hikes when introduced. For now, I intend to keep the subscription because it’s so useful and I use it constantly.
author: PennCCRN

title: Lost but found
content: I remember the year 2013 my buddy and I were trying to find water falls and any other cool stuff while having a whole day to do whatever we wanted. We managed to sorta find one waterfall off google but it was definitely a bust. The rest the day was fun but we never found anything we originally planned for. With all trails I have never gotten lost or haven’t found what I wanted to see in any geographical location since then. I love it and it has helped me find easily sooooo many spots! Probably been using it since the app started and i don’t travel without it ready.
author: 6 starr

title: Needs minor change
content:
Over all this app is great. I particularly like the map following feature and all the “obscure” trails that lead you through local neighborhoods. Lots of good detailed info to keep you on track with the trail. 
The only improvement I’d ask for is to remove the required feature to rate your event when done. Every time I “finish” an event I am required to rate that event. Make this an option instead of a requirement.
We do many of the same exact walks over and over again so having to rate it each time is a waste of time. Plus I don’t feel the need or see the advantage to rate every walk/event you take using the app.
author: ChrisOR83

title: Good app. Suggestion for another feature
content: I like the app and it’s super useful when out on trails.  But I have a request for them to add a feature. On a trail yesterday we stumbled upon an angry yellow jacket nest. It would be useful to add a feature to where you can add a warning at that location for something like this that other people on the trail can see. We saw another group walk right through it after us. Please add some way we can add a hazard to the trail that could notify others also on the trail or alert people when choosing or starting the trail. It could also be used for animal sighting or good things like rare flowers blooming to look out for.
author: tnt_3149

title: Decent little app
content:
I have been using All Trails for a few years now. For the most part I like it, but I wish it was faster to detect that routes have changed. If enough people are going “off route” in the same area, and take the same path to get back on route, that should be a hint to the system that something may have changed.
I also wish they would make a version that works with an iPad. I understand that very few people are taking their iPad on trail, but some of us would like to do our off-trail planning on an iPad as opposed to our phone.
All-in-all, I still like this app and use it almost as much as I use Gaia GPS for hiking.
author: Stevenhacker

title: Great app but…
content: I love this app, I’m able to get so much hiking done with this app. There’s just one thing that’s pretty frustrating. I had to delete a lot of my hikes I recorded because I forget to end the hike and then I drive all the way to my house. I don’t want no one to know where I live, plus now the stats are inaccurate. It’s frustrating when that happens. I gave the app 2 stars because there are apps like Strava that let you shorten the distance you went. Like why doesn’t all trails have that feature.😭 I gave it 2 stars because that’s how it feels after doing a 10 mile hike but forgetting to end it, so I drive all the way to my house. If only I was able to shorten that part so I didn’t have to delete the whole hike. This happened to me multiple times.
author: TestAnApp

title: Don’t Hike Without It!
content: AllTrails is my favorite app! I love hiking and alltrails is the best way to find trails in the US. I have a terrible sense of direction so alltrails keeps me from getting lost as well.  I really like knowing what to expect as far as altitude gain, length of trail and difficulty when I choose a trail. The reviews give you extra details about shade cover, parking, and water needs along the way. I have been using the app for a couple of years now and I love it so much I recently bit the bullet and went Pro so I could download the maps and save my phone battery life.
author: Six-toed Sloth

title: Fantastic
content:
OK, I’m giving this app four stars rather than five stars for two reasons. First, I tend to put more stock into reviews that are not perfect so I’m hoping this one shows sincerity. Also, nothing is perfect so keep making improvements on this great app.

I’m 54 years old and a newbie when it comes to hiking, so this app has been integral to me being able to start hiking.

I also paid for the annual subscription. I did this not because I needed it since the free version pretty much gives me anything I need. However, the developers deserve my money because it’s such a great app. That is why I bought a subscription.
author: JEANMR1

title: Good so far
content: I have the free version and I can’t tell you that it didn’t disappoint so far , for showing you all the trails and being able to choose trails while you’re on the trails i give this app a 5*. I share it with other friends and they downloaded right away. Now i guess some bad reviews have some good points if you pay for the pro version and doesn’t meet the expectations but for what i use it and compared with the fancy ones out there and trust me I tried all of them , All Trails is the most i use it and I deleted all the other ones..
author: lotherm69

title: Valuable features removed
content:
I used to love AllTrails, especially the way it logged information and made it possible for our hiking community to answer each others questions. 
However a recent app redesign saw some of those features disappear completely, and others become more difficult. 
You used to be able to look at trail photos on the trail map, by where they were taken. This was quite helpful, especially for planning places to camp or get ideas of water sources. 
Now, the pictures are significantly less organized. It’s impossible to view them on a map except an incomplete “tour” that seems to arbitrarily choose some pictures for fun. 
Why take away such a valuable feature?
author: maggiejeansewingmachind

title: Great but can’t record video or take pics without app pausing
content: The app seems to think I’m done hiking if I take a quick video or picture while still hiking/moving. It takes more time to keep checking the app to make sure it’s still recording my hike. My friends and I hike fast so I only take a quick pic or video while I’m hiking. I just wish the app wouldn’t pause if I’m still moving. Sometimes the app just crashes so I have to keep checking to see if it’s recording. I would love to have all my mileage recorded. I’m looking at maybe running another app as well so maybe between 2 I’ll get my full hike recorded.
author: Hikarimidori

title: Don’t buy if you really care about data
content:
The app is pretty good but has some major flaws.

1. The pause/finish buttons are located at the bottom. For newer iPhones without the no home button, you need to swipe up to minimize the app. It’s a major UI design flaw. I can’t believe it hasn’t been corrected. That can lead to unplanned pauses/finishes which can (a) pause tracking and therefore stop collecting data, or (b) finish the hike and there’s no back button. 

2. The app can also just stop tracking. I’ll lock the phone and put in my pocket only to find it stopped collecting data some time ago. I need to constantly check to see if it’s still tracking . It cause me anxiety which is not what I’m looking for when I go outdoors.

3. You can go into your profile on a PC and, through a complex process, correct the route but you then lose your hiking time and pacing data. Pick your poison. 

4. This is a know issue with many complaints. They would rather make the app look pretty than fix core issues. 

Going to give Garmin and/or Gaia a chance.
author: Significant Design Flaw

title: A hikers must have!
content: Have been using Alltrails as my hiking bible for many many years. It’s a must have especially for areas with no cell service. With the subscription you can upload the trail prior to arrival. Alltrail will track you and keep your assigned lifelines updated. What I love most is that you will never ever get lost!  and believe me you can get lost in the wilderness and unmarked trails. Alltrails will 𝐀𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐭 you when you are off the trail map. We are avid hikers and will never go without Alltrails. PS: you can use Alltrails without a subscription but will have the most benefits if you do.
author: 02trickynick

title: Only while you have cell reception
content:
When I found AllTrails, I really liked it, and started to plan my hikes with it and record them too. Unfortunately, at the moment you leave the cell phone network behind, it stops being usable. Literally. All you get is "oops something went wrong. Lets try again", in an endless loop. You can start the App while you have a network, and then drive to your trail (stopping every ten minutes to move the screen a bit, so iOS doesn't offload it), but otherwise, it is simply dead. On multi-day trips however, you are dead in the water on day two - you simply cannot start the app at all.
So either they point is to force you to pay, or the developers never left town while testing.
author: W. in Orlando

title: Better than Colin Fletcher at your side
content: I’m a veteran hiker who knows his way around topos, GPS’s and such. This app is a great amalgam of all of it as well as how to get to the trailhead and what others think. Kind of like finding a local outdoor outfitter and asking for advice but without the randomness of getting the person who knows what they’re talking about. It’s also like the manifold “best hikes” guides but it’d be 3 feet thick and with crowd sourced feedback. I use it wherever I hike now but I still carry an old school compass and paper map. It’s a great app all right but if your batteries die, you lose signal or trash your phone you’d better have backup.
author: Tsglass201

title: Hiking, walking and travel app that works seamlessly!
content: We journeyed by rental car, plane and taxi across the Israeli-Jordan border at Eilat, all to visit Petra, Jordan, a UNESCO site and one of the wonders of the world. We were feeling adventurous as we entered the Petra site at 8 am, thinking we would be the first to record an AllTrails hike in this beautiful red rock area of caves and ancient temples. Clicked on the App, and moments later a half dozen or more hikes in Petra appeared! The app recorded our progress as we hiked on sandstone paths through remote hills, and sidestepped donkeys, horse carts and camels. It worked fantastically, so impressed with this app!  Going to try it when we travel to Greece and Italy later this year :)
author: BMK Report

title: Wow major hit yo your battery
content: I’ve used all trails for years. I’ve been on pro for just under a year. I started using the app to record my hikes because I like the final stats. Some of the last upgrades have really done a number on battery life. I was at 74% upon starting my hike. Less than 20 minutes in and I was down to 14%. As soon as I hit stop recording, my battery drain stopped. I ended up using the app the remaining hour and 30 minutes as just a reference and my battery only went down to 12%. I use other fitness apps to record activities,all trails is officially the biggest power hog.
author: Pixiejynx

title: Great App, some changes has been taking place and it’s appreciated
content:
AllTrails is an amazing tool for finding and tracking hikes. The interface is smooth, the trail details are accurate, and overall, it’s a great experience.
I had initially given it a 3 stars because of some issues that are now included in the premium. It’s only 36 a yr and worth it even if you only hike 3 months out the year, 12 a month for accurate and ability to download trails for offline hikes. I’m in the Olympic rainforest in wa right now using it again this year. Great app.
author: The.Fallen.Angel

title: New update
content:
I never write reviews unless something really gets to me. 
This got to me. The app was fine how it was maybe make some improvments to things but the way the pictures are laid out I click to check out a trail it give you almost like a video of the pictures taken. No thanks. Then as I’m searching up trails in my area. I click on a list of 7 tails can’t scroll down past the first one. I do not like this update it’s a lot to take in when all you wanted to do was get outside. Now I’m spending 30 minutes just figuring out the app.
author: bodi1111

title: Not bad
content: I use this app every time I hike. I like trail forks as well (use for mtb mostly) but it kills your battery. One huge recent dislike is that after paying $36 for quite a few years now suddenly they want you to pay $70 to access “peak”. With the way the economy is $70 is a ridiculous price to ask for. I also can no longer see the trails near me while recording. Guess that’s only for “peak” members now. So I have to leave my recording to view other trails around me so I can make sure I’m on my planned route. I don’t know I’m just really disappointed after being a member for so long that they  wouldn’t at least offer a discount for already being a member.
author: Osaraho999

title: Just one issue
content: This is a fantastic app for hiking. The only problem that I have seen with it is not only myself, but I’ve seen other people that forget to turn it off so it record your entire drive and your hike from your house. There should be a setting where if you are going over say five mph it should ask if you want to continue recording. Also, it will be nice in this case to edit the map and the hike to delete the driving part. I would like to see how many miles that I walk, but it’s also adding my Drive if I forget to turn it off. Five stars when this is fixed.
author: Bryks1111

title: Great for all outdoor exploring
content:
I use AllTrails when I am walking, biking, hiking and kayaking. It is great to find new trails and parks or pick a trail based on the wonderful maps, pictures and information. 
It is helpful to find my way back if I decide to explore. It keeps track of all the things I did and is helpful to get directions to “that one hike I did a couple years ago that had the waterfall…” because I had forgotten the name of the park/trail. I have used it overseas and it was perfect. I can share fun trails with my friends easily. I 100% recommend this app.
author: It is me Bubbles

title: Buggy but useless App
content: Ok I am a pro user and have been using this app for a long time. It has great features, pretty much everything you want except that the app is buggy. I have never been able to upload any pic of my hikes (because it would just not upload the photos or videos). Lately the software has shown more issues where I cannot open a map, have to restart it multiple times and it just takes too much time to get it working that is to track your route. Because of these bugs I may not renew my membership. If you have any other app that is less buggy on your phone I would recommend to use that one instead.
author: pro user AllTrails

title: Frustrating
content: Three ⭐️for potential. AllTrails has been recommended by many fellow hikers & bikers, so I finally purchased after also upgrading to a new iphone 13 to ensure I’d be able to use the App offline. I’m really looking forward to being able to use & rely on App as others have described. I’ve downloaded GPX file to a new/created map successfully, however App will not let me download the map for offline use. It continues to suggest upgrade to Pro after I’ve already purchased Pro, and see it’s active in my settings/subscriptions. I’ve unloaded, rebooted phone all to no avail. Tried a download in airplane mode - same issue. Hope they get it resolved. Happy Hiking.
author: GG.rollz

title: Time waster
content: This app has excellent trails and an easy to read layout. I would love it except for 1 major feature which kills it completely for me.  At the end of every hike/bike/run i do… this app forces me to give a star rating to my route, then goes through a series of other screens which ask me to add pictures and names. At the end of my route, i am TIERD and BUZY loading a bunch of gear into my car.i don’t want to stand around at that time playing with my phone.  I just want to end my route and go home not drop everything and  give all trails more fodder for their social media. This app cares  more for social media, than it cares for athletes serious about training.
author: Hfhfgdy

title: Great resource but lacks accurate distances
content:
I use all trails to find hikes, and it is an amazing resource. It makes finding hikes really convenient with its interface. However the distances are always wrong by at least a few miles which is frustrating. 

My 14 mile hike will actually be 16.5 miles, and that’s really frustrating. These mileage is not trustworthy and makes all trails an unreliable resource for anything outside of finding a trail head. Even tracking a hike the distance measurements and elevation will not be accurate. Sometimes it’s so inaccurate that it will impact your ability to make a plan. 

For more accurate route planning, distances, elevation and logistics planning use Gaia GPS.
author: f0ck_this

title: Problematic
content: I had high hopes for AllTrails. It tracks very well and handles waypoints well but uploading photos and synchronizing across devices is problematic. After returning from a home I submitted the recording and then attempted to edit from my laptop. I could edit my description very easily but changes failed to appear on my device a half hour later. I also attempted to upload photos from my camera card to the hike - 15 minutes and still waiting. My Internet is slow but not that slow - I can upload files and photos to other apps without problem. I keep working with it because I can find no alternative but it may simply be more trouble than it’s worth for general use. I’m using the Pro version.
author: Mrhvmd

title: I wanted to love this, but…
content: I really just wanted to purchase the peak, but the only way to do it is purchased the plus, for them to refund the plus when you purchase the peak. Seems very tedious. There are a few trails in Las Vegas area that have detours and the detours are not shown on the map and some trails that I tried to go on and there are no trespassing signs so these trails are not active any longer. They should have left it custom trails under plus because I have no need for any other items in peak category. I do like the active live sharing, but one thing I absolutely dislike is if I go off the trail It doesn’t record it, especially when there’s a detour. I will be going with a different trail GPS app for less money.
author: redjeepgirl89

title: Never go into the woods without it!
content: I have been using all trails now for almost 4 1/2 years. I live in an area where I have over 60 miles of hiking trails available to me. Just a short walk from my home. I often go hiking daily from 4 to 6 miles each time and alone. I send a live share to a family member or friend so that they always know where I am. In addition to this safety feature it is also a great way to find out what hiking and other trails are available in areas that I may be traveling to. I never go into the woods without it.
author: Rlbneo

title: Great hiking trail apps!
content:
I use AllTrails for finding & keeping track of my hikes. The fellow user reviews are akin to Yelp, which I love, because they give good insight into what you can expect in terms of trail condition, weather, difficulty level, location, accessibility, animal allowance, etc. 

Definitely the most comprehensive trail app I’ve found so far! I love that they’re constantly updating and making improvements, including one of the most recent additions of trail weather conditions. 

If I could make one improvement to the app right now, it would be to find tune the trail difficulty ratings: currently, trails can be rated Easy, Moderate, or Hard. It would be nice to have a scale more detailed than 1-3 in difficulty, as many users could feasibly rate the same trail at different levels. I would suggest Easy, Moderately Easy, Moderate, Moderately Hard, and Hard. 

Otherwise - I LOVE this app, and recommend it to anybody and everybody looking for places to hike wherever they go. Keep it up, AllTrails!
author: sasssquash

title: Just About As Good As It Gets
content: If you’re getting into hiking, new to an area, or want to get a feel for a hike, AllTrails is absolutely excellent. Trail maps can be a little wonky but otherwise pretty dependable, and the sorting features for finding hikes is tremendous. HOWEVER, it can’t replace experience and community. Nothing can. Nature is an active, elusive lady; trails change, slopes get slippery, and numbers don’t always tell the full story. 78 degrees F in the forest on a mountain is miles different from 78 in the desert. The first thing to tell you that isn’t going to be AllTrails, it’ll be the friends you make along the way. Or Reddit. My point still stands.
author: Al Butherol

title: Necessary app for outdoor enthusiasts
content: If you like hiking, biking, or generally being outdoors this app is absolutely essential. I know some people like paper maps but there is something about having absolute confidence about where I’m going when hiking which is very comforting and convenient. I love the different trail options, and the ability to download offline maps that still track where you are going so I know where I’m going on a trail even if I don’t have service as a paying member. I use this app at least once a week.
author: OAK1023

title: Best Trail App Ever
content: I’ve been using All Trails for a few years and I couldn’t be happier! It is the best at identifying trails nearby whatever area we happen to be in across the US. The reviews of each trail is pretty accurate also thanks to feedback from users. The difficulty ratings and data for each trail are very helpful in determining our choices. I appreciate that they have the option for offline use as well. Many other features in addition make this a must have more anyone wanting to get outdoors and not sure where to go.
author: Nowoscat

title: Can’t find most trails in my area
content:
I have been using this app for about a year now, and I do love it. However, I have found that it only locates what it assumes are “popular”trails. I live in WA state and we have many many trails, but I can’t find a lot of them on this app unless I google them. 
The purpose of wanting these trails on the app is so that I can check the preview details, etc. I hope they upgrade it to locate all the trails available here. There’s many great trails that are very well known, but you won’t locate them on this app unfortunately. 
Also, I need them to let me choose the country.  I live about 20 min from Canada, and sometimes I just want to search WA trails.
author: Irritated human

title: App is good but lags and freezes a lot
content: App is good! I’ve been using it all the time. The only frustrating thing is that it lags when you tap on a trail from search result selection. It takes such a long time to load. It needs to be optimized. Also another frustrating thing is when there is not cell phone signal and you open the app and you wait an hour for it to unfreeze. You have got to test such things throughly on all the devices. I’m using iPhone XS. Another thing would be to cache the trails you marked as favorite or placed in a list. So when you are in no data zone it opens up quickly. If you fix it, would be 5 stars!
author: adik2009

title: Great app but…
content: Downloaded the app awhile ago and have used it to locate hiking trails. When it changed to a subscription only app, I was a little upset, only because I didn’t use it regularly anyway. Took a trip to New Mexico and decided to take the free trial for a spin. The app assured me that it would notify me before it charged the yearly subscription fee.  It did not and tried to charge me anyway. While the plus version of the app was very clean and easy to use offline, I was annoyed that it constantly kept pushing the Peak version on me. An otherwise great app for avid hikers. No need to try and be sneaky.
author: CJNibbles

title: An app worth giving a shot
content: I didn’t know how much I liked the outdoors until I realized there was a trail in my backyard! (Behind my apartments lol) I went almost daily and thanks to this app I felt unstoppable. Not only was I able to navigate through the trails with low signal, but I was able to access all the trails in my city, get personalized reviews from other trailblazers  but I was able to share my own experiences and feel apart of the community. The achievements definitely help boost my moral to do more outdoors, I’m just so glad I can across this app.
author: krissy ✨

title: Great app, great customer service
content: Downloaded the free trial and it was great for my vacation to Hawaii where hikes are available everywhere. Cancelling the subscription was a breeze with the chatbot service. Would definitely recommend the app depending on where you live. Unfortunately I live in flat Iowa without any real hiking so it doesn’t serve much purpose for me day to day like it could for some. Very user friendly app though with good user interaction and nice to see the reviews of trails ahead of time to assess difficulty, conditions, and just overall experience.
author: Zlit

title: New Update
content: I love all trails I use it on every hike. I came here to beg that you please fix the record. I love the fact that I can now see my elevation gain, mileage, calories burned etc. however the record now crashes. Everytime my app refreshes it stops recording and I have to resume so my mileage isnt accurate, nothing is accurate its awful. I paid for the pro version not that long ago and im incredibly disappointed. I am still going to use this app but this is a bummer and I hope it gets fixed. I love seeing my stats. I also cant see where exactly I am on route so its difficult to navigate because the blue marker only shows up if you have service, most hikes don’t. So its just a red line on top of a red line. Fix it!! please!
author: Esoko333

title: Good bang for your buck
content: I’ve used the paid version of the app for years and find it incredibly useful when searching for hikes of various intensities and ensuring I have an accurate map in case I lose service. Since many of my hikes are in the Rockies where snow lasts long after it’s melted on the front range, I also find it helpful to read the reviews and comments left by recent hikers - this gives me a sense of whether I might need spikes for a portion, if it’s muddy from snow melt, or if there’s a chunk of trail missing from a winter-time avalanche (it happens!).
author: Selslie

title: Over it
content: This app has gotten so much worse over the last few years. The features of the free version were so much better before. It stalls and shuts down constantly, overheats my phone after using it for 2 minutes, and trying to select pictures from others’ trail reports is quite literally impossible. The picture I try to click on is never the picture that loads, and isn’t even close to the one that it enlarges. The ads for purchasing pro are incessant and naggy, and I wouldn’t want to pay for it anyway, because it will probably still overheat my phone and not work the way I want it to. Can’t even create my own waypoints in the desktop version anymore either. Just pay for something better like onX backcountry
author: Yikesbro3

title: A Must Have for Hikers & Adventurers
content: AllTrails is the best. If you enjoy hiking or being in the woods, AllTrails is a must have. This app has literally saved me when I’ve been lost and had no idea how to get back to the trailhead. it has a ton of cool features like seeing the most recent trail conditions from fellow hikers, being able to choose based off of what characteristics you’d like, such as good views or dog friendly, and a ton more on that app that I’m still exploring and it’s been over two years now that have been using it. Download and enjoy your adventures!!
author: Sarah Terminator

title: Please make an iPad app
content: The app for mobile is great! But please make an iPad app. And iPad app would make it much easier to view the different map layers, and plan hikes with a group because of the ability for multiple people to look at a larger screen. Also, I would love the ability to be able to plan my own hiking routes instead of only being able to select and gather detailed information on the hiking routes that have already been predetermined by the app. This is for sure by far the best hiking app on the App Store! Adding these features would just push it farther ahead.
author: Listener 22

title: Good for finding trails, terrible watch app
content:
This app is one of the best, if not the best app for finding trails. It also has a large user base, so it’s easy to find updated info about the trails via recent comments from other users. This is very useful!

Offline use would be better if I could download entire selected regions or states. 

The watch app is terrible. It’s unreliable, provides little information, and forces you to pull your phone out more often than not, which makes it redundant. They should either get rid of the watch app or rewrite it entirely. There are much better solutions for hiking with an Apple Watch, so look elsewhere if that’s what you want/need.
author: b•r•e•n•d•a•n

title: What. Is. The. Point.
content:
This app seems totally useless. I’ve tried to find some possible use for it, given that it seems to have some important information stored (like mileage, elevation, and conditions), but accessibility to these features is just bonkers. I fiddled around in every possible way for two weeks, trying to set routes, select paths on the map, locate overnight sites, and so on, and I just couldn’t get the app to do anything I wanted it to in any meaningful or helpful way. Not to mention the fact that it asked me to upgrade to the “Pro” version every new screen, which eventually pushed me to delete and leave a review.

If you’re looking for downloadable trail maps, I’d recommend looking elsewhere. If you’re looking for anything else, I’d recommend looking elsewhere.
author: peterthedragon

title: Named Waypoints on maps and “High Five”
content: I am disappointed in the most recent update. I rely on waypoint markings as GPS points to use on iNaturalist for my photography. When marking the waypoints in the field, I select the option for my named waypoints to show on the map. The names of the waypoints I’ve assigned show while actively using the app, however the names do not show on the map once I save my hike and close it. This did not happen in the previous version. I hope this glitch is fixed soon, particularly for the paid version. I also find the congratulations and high five every time I mark a waypoint annoying and artificial, as well as when I save my hike.
author: Asteracae

title: Map app with no large screen (iPad) support?!
content:
Apple makes it so easy to support multiple screen sizes, and even an iPhone-only app has to do this already. Why not support the iPad, even if it's just a "blown-up" interface with no custom design? Being able to use the full screen to view maps and plan trips would be so nice. I guess for now using the web site (yuck) is the only option.

EDIT: By "blown-up interface" I mean a true universal app that runs at full native resolution, even if the UI elements are just the same ones as in the phone UI. This takes very little developer effort and I don't understand why it can't be done as an interim solution while working on whatever it is you are working on for iPad later on. Using the zoom button on the emulated phone app is a far inferior experience to this.
author: ABR3434

title: Loving the app!
content: I always used the web version, so it’s nice to finally have the app to use and view maps with ease. Although it doesn’t actually have all the trails, it connects this trails to others which can make it confusing. For example west ridge trail in New Hampshire can be found on iMaps but not on Alltrails, yet when click an adjacent trail it will include that trail in it. So just be on the lookout for that. Other than that, it well help you tremendously and a one stop shop for searching for hikes as well as executing them. See y’all on the mountain!
author: Seanyslime

title: THIS APP IS AWESOME!
content: I’ve had many trail apps before which I stopped using and unsubscribed from because they were confusing and just spammed my inbox. This app is amazing. I even taught my 70 year old dad how to use it. Very easy to filter and find trails in your area. And also, if it’s not on this app, the trail doesn’t exist. It tells you the difficulty level, distance, time, and rating. But you can filter anything from waterfalls, to wild flowers, to pavement, to mountain biking, to whether or not dogs are allowed, etc. AND you can track your progress. I would have gotten lost so many times if it wasn’t for this app!! Enjoy!
author: jessica n95

title: No color for different color trails
content: It would seem like something that should be a standard feature, but AllTrails does not have color  for the corresponding color of the trails. Why not? This seems like a simple feature to implement, and would be immensely helpful to plan the trail instead of staring at the phone every few minutes to ensure you're standing at the right location. Instead every trail is colored according to difficulty which is itself helpful for planning, but does not help you once you're on the trail to understand  which way to turn. Additionally, the written description does not adequately provide instructions for where to turn etc. so app has not been very helpful.
author: Sharpie770

title: Realistic Review  June 7, 2024
content:
There are few pluses the app delivers but truthfully it has a lot to be desired for an app that has a yearly fee. Works well to finding trails and showing where a trail is to stay on course. It’s better when the trails are popular but fall off a lot when they aren’t. Here are where the app needs much more improvement. 

1. Elevation scale should be available in landscape mode and the ability adjust ratio for more realistic elevation in relation to map. 

2. You currently can’t mark and hold a spot on the elevation scale or map to mark a point or where you are without keeping your finger down on it. 

3. The app can’t show you selected point to point distance measurement 

4. Crowd sourcing information on maps is limited and not encouraged to leave helpful tips on campsites and water sources

5. When display turns off, the app resets making you have to open the maps again losing your place or have to quit the app since the map will disappear on you. 

6. The track your route feature is too easily accidentally pressed, an issue when trying to conserve battery life on your phone. 

7. Navigating in 3D is  too sensitive making it difficult to do fly over to view elevation of route. 

8. There should be an option to have app open to current trail on rather than always having to navigate through the app to find it. Wastes a lot of time when on trail. 

9. Can switch route to go reverse example instead of going north to south, change to south to north. 

10. Can’t press icons to get more information on maps. If there’s an icon, you should offer useful info what’s available for hikers. 

I could probably go on, but you see it has a lot to improve on and nowhere close to a 4.9 rating in my personal opinion. Hopefully they take all this and update otherwise I can’t see myself continuing to pay for the subscription. You’ll see what I mean when you start using the app yourself.
author: _Ataraxia_

title: We love AllTrails
content: Before AllTrails it was up to me to find maps and information from various sources. Some word of mouth. You know how that goes. A spoken direction or misinterpreted landmark to look for could have you lost. Sometimes questioned by local farmers. Ever noticed that country folk don’t particularly like you driving up and down their roads or looking aimlessly into what may be a trail head or their pastures. They may think your up to something. I’m not sure what. I don’t care to talk back to folk in rural areas if you get my drift. So with AllTrails this happens less. It’s neat !
author: Ranger Rick Bush Adventures

title: The navigation lacks the needed information
content:
I have been using the app (pro version) for a few weeks now. Most of the app is wonderfully helpful and uaedul.

One improvement can be to add the ability to see “remaining distance” for a hike. Just saw that “remaining time” feature was added. The pace differs from person to person and so that is not very helpful.

Ideally one plans few way points for a full hike. It is useful to identify (mark) waypoints and get a “remaining distance to the next waypoint” presented as a motivator to accomplish planned goals and keep to a planned schedule.

The offline maps show the GPS location on the map and the elevation at the point can be seen. So I am surprised why not the remaining distance to the next waypoint or end of the trail?

I also see that the interface to using a “pause” in the middle of the hike is very unintuitive. Pause state changed to hold after a few seconds -  not sure what that implies. Realized that a long hold on the hold moves to a different UI state that has a resume option.
author: RRtaken

title: This app is a lifesaver, but
content: I love this app! I couldn’t have gone the places I’ve been the past couple of years without it. “But, you only gave them 3 stars.” The app is not without bugs. Most recently, it crashes constantly. I begin to record my hike and turn off my screen- more often than not, the app pauses itself and does not recognize that I’m still in motion. It has also been painfully slow lately and just now, while browsing, the app just crashes for no reason. I’ve deleted and re-downloaded and hard restarted my phone. Frustrating. I will continue to be a paid subscriber because it is a great app - when it works.
author: Lacircuitgirl

title: Please go back to the basics
content: I’ve been an AllTrails Pro user for years, but this might be the final year as the slowness of the app recently has been truly awful. I know they’ve been trying to transition to a more “community” feel within the app, however recent updates have made it incredibly difficult to use. I’m lucky if I can get a trail page to even load sometimes. Open a trail page for basic information AND wait for the map to fully load? I could be over a half mile through a trail before that happens… and it HAS happened, even with offline maps. It’s really unfortunate as it is/has been a user friendly guiding app and has been pretty clutch for me the past few years.
author: alcheming

title: Okay app but pretty darned annoying
content:
The app works well and I have a pro subscription.  However it is pretty darned annoying to use.   First, it does not have the ability to keep the phone awake like every other nav app.  The phone goes to sleep on a ride and I have to wake it.  

I use the app solely for biking.  The app does not have the ability to set a default activity which is a bother.   I would rather be able to set a default and if I do something other than a bike ride change the activity for that time.  

The biggest annoyance is you can’t just save your ride like you can with map my ride.  The stupid app wants you to give a star rating before it will save the ride and won’t take no for answer.  At least it will let you skip posting photos.
author: John in MD

title: Don’t Hike Without It!
content: AllTrails is my favorite app! I love hiking and alltrails is the best way to find trails in the US. I have a terrible sense of direction so alltrails keeps me from getting lost as well.  I really like knowing what to expect as far as altitude gain, length of trail and difficulty when I choose a trail. The reviews give you extra details about shade cover, parking, and water needs along the way. I have been using the app for a couple of years now and I love it so much I recently bit the bullet and went Pro so I could download the maps and save my phone battery life.
author: Six-toed Sloth

title: Fantastic
content:
OK, I’m giving this app four stars rather than five stars for two reasons. First, I tend to put more stock into reviews that are not perfect so I’m hoping this one shows sincerity. Also, nothing is perfect so keep making improvements on this great app.

I’m 54 years old and a newbie when it comes to hiking, so this app has been integral to me being able to start hiking.

I also paid for the annual subscription. I did this not because I needed it since the free version pretty much gives me anything I need. However, the developers deserve my money because it’s such a great app. That is why I bought a subscription.
author: JEANMR1

title: Good so far
content: I have the free version and I can’t tell you that it didn’t disappoint so far , for showing you all the trails and being able to choose trails while you’re on the trails i give this app a 5*. I share it with other friends and they downloaded right away. Now i guess some bad reviews have some good points if you pay for the pro version and doesn’t meet the expectations but for what i use it and compared with the fancy ones out there and trust me I tried all of them , All Trails is the most i use it and I deleted all the other ones..
author: lotherm69

title: Valuable features removed
content:
I used to love AllTrails, especially the way it logged information and made it possible for our hiking community to answer each others questions. 
However a recent app redesign saw some of those features disappear completely, and others become more difficult. 
You used to be able to look at trail photos on the trail map, by where they were taken. This was quite helpful, especially for planning places to camp or get ideas of water sources. 
Now, the pictures are significantly less organized. It’s impossible to view them on a map except an incomplete “tour” that seems to arbitrarily choose some pictures for fun. 
Why take away such a valuable feature?
author: maggiejeansewingmachind

title: Great but can’t record video or take pics without app pausing
content: The app seems to think I’m done hiking if I take a quick video or picture while still hiking/moving. It takes more time to keep checking the app to make sure it’s still recording my hike. My friends and I hike fast so I only take a quick pic or video while I’m hiking. I just wish the app wouldn’t pause if I’m still moving. Sometimes the app just crashes so I have to keep checking to see if it’s recording. I would love to have all my mileage recorded. I’m looking at maybe running another app as well so maybe between 2 I’ll get my full hike recorded.
author: Hikarimidori

title: Don’t buy if you really care about data
content:
The app is pretty good but has some major flaws.

1. The pause/finish buttons are located at the bottom. For newer iPhones without the no home button, you need to swipe up to minimize the app. It’s a major UI design flaw. I can’t believe it hasn’t been corrected. That can lead to unplanned pauses/finishes which can (a) pause tracking and therefore stop collecting data, or (b) finish the hike and there’s no back button. 

2. The app can also just stop tracking. I’ll lock the phone and put in my pocket only to find it stopped collecting data some time ago. I need to constantly check to see if it’s still tracking . It cause me anxiety which is not what I’m looking for when I go outdoors.

3. You can go into your profile on a PC and, through a complex process, correct the route but you then lose your hiking time and pacing data. Pick your poison. 

4. This is a know issue with many complaints. They would rather make the app look pretty than fix core issues. 

Going to give Garmin and/or Gaia a chance.
author: Significant Design Flaw

title: A hikers must have!
content: Have been using Alltrails as my hiking bible for many many years. It’s a must have especially for areas with no cell service. With the subscription you can upload the trail prior to arrival. Alltrail will track you and keep your assigned lifelines updated. What I love most is that you will never ever get lost!  and believe me you can get lost in the wilderness and unmarked trails. Alltrails will 𝐀𝐥𝐞𝐫𝐭 you when you are off the trail map. We are avid hikers and will never go without Alltrails. PS: you can use Alltrails without a subscription but will have the most benefits if you do.
author: 02trickynick

title: Only while you have cell reception
content:
When I found AllTrails, I really liked it, and started to plan my hikes with it and record them too. Unfortunately, at the moment you leave the cell phone network behind, it stops being usable. Literally. All you get is "oops something went wrong. Lets try again", in an endless loop. You can start the App while you have a network, and then drive to your trail (stopping every ten minutes to move the screen a bit, so iOS doesn't offload it), but otherwise, it is simply dead. On multi-day trips however, you are dead in the water on day two - you simply cannot start the app at all.
So either they point is to force you to pay, or the developers never left town while testing.
author: W. in Orlando

title: Better than Colin Fletcher at your side
content: I’m a veteran hiker who knows his way around topos, GPS’s and such. This app is a great amalgam of all of it as well as how to get to the trailhead and what others think. Kind of like finding a local outdoor outfitter and asking for advice but without the randomness of getting the person who knows what they’re talking about. It’s also like the manifold “best hikes” guides but it’d be 3 feet thick and with crowd sourced feedback. I use it wherever I hike now but I still carry an old school compass and paper map. It’s a great app all right but if your batteries die, you lose signal or trash your phone you’d better have backup.
author: Tsglass201

title: Hiking, walking and travel app that works seamlessly!
content: We journeyed by rental car, plane and taxi across the Israeli-Jordan border at Eilat, all to visit Petra, Jordan, a UNESCO site and one of the wonders of the world. We were feeling adventurous as we entered the Petra site at 8 am, thinking we would be the first to record an AllTrails hike in this beautiful red rock area of caves and ancient temples. Clicked on the App, and moments later a half dozen or more hikes in Petra appeared! The app recorded our progress as we hiked on sandstone paths through remote hills, and sidestepped donkeys, horse carts and camels. It worked fantastically, so impressed with this app!  Going to try it when we travel to Greece and Italy later this year :)
author: BMK Report

title: Wow major hit yo your battery
content: I’ve used all trails for years. I’ve been on pro for just under a year. I started using the app to record my hikes because I like the final stats. Some of the last upgrades have really done a number on battery life. I was at 74% upon starting my hike. Less than 20 minutes in and I was down to 14%. As soon as I hit stop recording, my battery drain stopped. I ended up using the app the remaining hour and 30 minutes as just a reference and my battery only went down to 12%. I use other fitness apps to record activities,all trails is officially the biggest power hog.
author: Pixiejynx

title: Great App, some changes has been taking place and it’s appreciated
content:
AllTrails is an amazing tool for finding and tracking hikes. The interface is smooth, the trail details are accurate, and overall, it’s a great experience.
I had initially given it a 3 stars because of some issues that are now included in the premium. It’s only 36 a yr and worth it even if you only hike 3 months out the year, 12 a month for accurate and ability to download trails for offline hikes. I’m in the Olympic rainforest in wa right now using it again this year. Great app.
author: The.Fallen.Angel

title: New update
content:
I never write reviews unless something really gets to me. 
This got to me. The app was fine how it was maybe make some improvments to things but the way the pictures are laid out I click to check out a trail it give you almost like a video of the pictures taken. No thanks. Then as I’m searching up trails in my area. I click on a list of 7 tails can’t scroll down past the first one. I do not like this update it’s a lot to take in when all you wanted to do was get outside. Now I’m spending 30 minutes just figuring out the app.
author: bodi1111

title: Not bad
content: I use this app every time I hike. I like trail forks as well (use for mtb mostly) but it kills your battery. One huge recent dislike is that after paying $36 for quite a few years now suddenly they want you to pay $70 to access “peak”. With the way the economy is $70 is a ridiculous price to ask for. I also can no longer see the trails near me while recording. Guess that’s only for “peak” members now. So I have to leave my recording to view other trails around me so I can make sure I’m on my planned route. I don’t know I’m just really disappointed after being a member for so long that they  wouldn’t at least offer a discount for already being a member.
author: Osaraho999

title: Just one issue
content: This is a fantastic app for hiking. The only problem that I have seen with it is not only myself, but I’ve seen other people that forget to turn it off so it record your entire drive and your hike from your house. There should be a setting where if you are going over say five mph it should ask if you want to continue recording. Also, it will be nice in this case to edit the map and the hike to delete the driving part. I would like to see how many miles that I walk, but it’s also adding my Drive if I forget to turn it off. Five stars when this is fixed.
author: Bryks1111

title: Great for all outdoor exploring
content:
I use AllTrails when I am walking, biking, hiking and kayaking. It is great to find new trails and parks or pick a trail based on the wonderful maps, pictures and information. 
It is helpful to find my way back if I decide to explore. It keeps track of all the things I did and is helpful to get directions to “that one hike I did a couple years ago that had the waterfall…” because I had forgotten the name of the park/trail. I have used it overseas and it was perfect. I can share fun trails with my friends easily. I 100% recommend this app.
author: It is me Bubbles

title: Buggy but useless App
content: Ok I am a pro user and have been using this app for a long time. It has great features, pretty much everything you want except that the app is buggy. I have never been able to upload any pic of my hikes (because it would just not upload the photos or videos). Lately the software has shown more issues where I cannot open a map, have to restart it multiple times and it just takes too much time to get it working that is to track your route. Because of these bugs I may not renew my membership. If you have any other app that is less buggy on your phone I would recommend to use that one instead.
author: pro user AllTrails

title: Frustrating
content: Three ⭐️for potential. AllTrails has been recommended by many fellow hikers & bikers, so I finally purchased after also upgrading to a new iphone 13 to ensure I’d be able to use the App offline. I’m really looking forward to being able to use & rely on App as others have described. I’ve downloaded GPX file to a new/created map successfully, however App will not let me download the map for offline use.
